stories.title: Man shoots girlfriend three times, then dies by suicide:Couple had argument on road; woman in critical condition
stories.summary: In Meerut, on Wednesday evening, a history-sheeter first shot his girlfriend, then shot himself to death. The young man was shot in the chest, while the young woman was shot twice in the stomach and once in the head. Upon reaching the hospital, doctors declared the young man dead, while the young woman's condition remains critical. The incident occurred around 4:30 PM at zonal park in Defense Enclave Colony, Kanker Khera. According to eyewitnesses, the young man arrived on a Pulsar and the young woman arrived on a scooter. They stood near the park talking for some time. Soon an argument broke out between the two. The young man pulled out a country-made pistol and shot the young woman three times. The young woman fell to the ground, writhing in pain. When people nearby rushed over, the young man immediately placed the pistol to his own chest and shot himself. When the police arrived, they called an ambulance and took both to Kailash Hospital, from where they were referred to Subharti Medical College. Both are residents of Kankarkheda According to the police, the injured girl has been identified as Anushka (23), a resident of Govindpuri, Kankarkheda, and the deceased youth as Aditya (26), a resident of Shivlok Pura Colony, Kankarkheda. Aditya is an ITI graduate and also a history-sheeter of Kankarkheda police station. Kankarkheda police station officials and a forensic team reached the spot. They collected evidence from the scene and also recovered a pistol. Police are also scanning nearby CCTVs to ascertain activities before and after the incident. Police are questioning the families of both SP City Vinayak Bhosale said, “In the CCTV footage, there was an argument between the young man and the young woman. After this, the young man shot her. The families of both are being questioned. After this, further action will be taken.”

stories.title: Five cyber criminals held for siphoning crores from poor people:Police seize 43 ATM cards and 12 passbooks
stories.summary: The Cyber Crime Police of Varanasi Commissionerate has busted an interstate gang involved in cyber fraud. The gang used mule bank accounts and APK files to defraud unsuspecting people. Five gang members have been arrested. Police recovered 15 Android mobiles, three iPhones, 43 ATM cards, 12 passbooks, 10 chequebooks, 11 QR codes, 12 SIM cards, one laptop, one diary, two four-wheelers (Mahindra Thar and Hyundai i-20), and ₹12,060 cash from the possession of the accused. During interrogation, it was revealed that the gang used to open bank accounts in the name of poor and needy people and take possession of their ATM cards, passbooks, and internet banking details. These accounts were used for transactions of money obtained through cyber fraud across the country. Police have registered a case and started investigating the criminal history of the accused. On Wednesday, DCP Crime Neetu Kadyan revealed the arrest of a gang of cyber criminals in the Police Line Auditorium. The DCP informed that the team has apprehended five notorious criminals of an interstate cyber gang. The investigation into the complaint of fraud from a businessman's account revealed links to a gang of cyber criminals. With the help of preliminary investigation and the surveillance team, one was apprehended. The arrested accused revealed that they formed cyber gangs and provided mule bank accounts to active cyber criminals across the country. The gang used to lure innocent and economically weak individuals with money and open accounts in various banks in their names. ATM cards, passbooks, checkbooks, SIM cards, internet banking IDs, passwords, and other banking documents were taken from the account holders, thereby gaining complete control of the accounts. The accused would then make these accounts available to their other cyber criminal associates and foreign cyber criminals. By obtaining transaction APK files from foreign cyber criminal associates, installing them on devices with mobile numbers linked to the accounts, and providing access, money obtained through cyber fraud is transferred into these accounts. This money is then subsequently transferred to other accounts at various levels, thereby committing cyber fraud. 8 to 15 per cent commission During interrogation, it was revealed that the gang members took 8 to 15 per cent commission on the money extracted from cybercrime. The gang members would then distribute it among themselves. It has been learned that the accused purchased Mahindra Thar and Hyundai i-20 cars with the money earned from cybercrime, and their EMIs were also paid from this illegal money. During the investigation, important digital evidence related to bank accounts, cyber transactions, suspicious chats, Telegram communication, and cybercrime was obtained from the accused's mobile phones, laptops, and other digital devices. This evidence is currently undergoing scientific examination. Arrested members of the gang: 1. Adarsh Chaubey son of Mithilesh Chaubey, resident of Ramgarh, Police Station Chunar, District Mirzapur (Current address - Varuna Enclave, Police Station Cantt, Varanasi) 2. Ashish Yadav son of Omkar Yadav, resident of Tofapur Bindwal, Police Station Bilariaganj, District Azamgarh (Current address - Varuna Enclave, Police Station Cantt, Varanasi) 3. Sujal Singh son of Vijay Singh, resident of Kawal, Police Station Jansath, District Muzaffarnagar (Current address - Ganpati Enclave Sunderpur, Varanasi) 4. Piyush Singh son of Ramkuwar Singh, resident of Bhikampur, Police Station Ghosi, District Mau (Current address - Kabir Nagar, Bhelupur Varanasi) 5. Yuvraj Verma son of Ashish Verma, resident of Gandhi Nagar, Naria, Police Station Lanka, Varanasi Recoveries from the Accused 15 Android mobile phones 3 iPhones 43 ATM cards 10 Passbooks 8 Chequebooks 11 QR codes

stories.title: Boating at Ramgarh Tal may resume this weekend:AI cameras and geo-fencing to be introduced before operations restart
stories.summary: Boating is likely to resume in Gorakhpur's Ramgarhtal from the coming Saturday. Boating had stopped at the lake after last Sunday's boating accident in which one person lost his life. Initially, preparations are being made to allow boating only from platforms number 1 and 6. The security arrangements of platforms number 4 and 5 are being investigated by separate committees of the district administration and Gorakhpur Development Authority (GDA). The reports from both committees are expected to be submitted by Friday. Strictness on speed boats, new system to be implemented GDA plans to implement several new rules keeping security in focus. Now, after sunset, speed boats will not be able to operate from any platform. Meanwhile, ordinary motor boats will only be able to operate till 9 PM. AI-based speed cameras will be installed on every platform, which will monitor the speed of the boats. If the speed exceeds the prescribed limit, the license of the concerned operator will be revoked and a fine will also be imposed on them. Route will be determined by geo-fencing and blinking lights Geo-fencing will be done in the lake so that boats from every platform operate only on their designated routes. For this, blinking lights will be installed in the water, so that boat operators can clearly see their path even at night and the possibility of accidents is reduced. In addition, AI cameras will also monitor whether any boat is going off its designated path or entering a restricted area. In the future, there are also plans to establish a water police outpost at Ramgarhtal to further improve patrolling and rescue operations. Two committees are investigating the accident A three-member committee constituted by District Magistrate Deepak Meena and a four-member committee of GDA are investigating the accident. Both committees are investigating security arrangements, boat drivers' licences, compliance with contract terms, and the causes of the accident. The GDA Vice Chairman stated that if the investigation report is satisfactory, boating will be resumed by the end of this week with some conditions. Based on the report, administrative and legal action will also be taken against the culprits.

stories.title: After Gen Z, Gen Alpha children protest in UP school:Demand clean water, electricity, toilets
stories.summary: After the Gen Z protest at Jantar Mantar, a video of a Gen Alpha children's movement from Uttar Pradesh has now surfaced. In the video, schoolchildren can be seen protesting to have their basic demands met. This incident is from Sarvodaya Inter College in Kishanpur, Fatehpur district. Children can be seen raising slogans against the school. A boy present at the protest is heard saying in the video that the school toilets are not clean. Children who are still inside the school and want to come out to join the protest against the management are also reportedly not being allowed to leave. The banner in the children's hands reads: "Improve the college system, build the children's future." The students claim that if they raise their voice against the principal of Sarvodaya Inter College, they are also threatened with being failed. The students' protest began at 7 am, once the school gate opened. They were raising their voices against the school's dilapidated buildings, contaminated water, and the principal's poor behaviour towards students. Students stated during the protest that the school toilets are dirty, there is no electricity, and the fans are broken. In addition, there are no facilities for a computer lab, library, or sports. The condition of the school's fans is reportedly so poor that some children have already received electric shocks. The school administration allegedly charges fees from children arbitrarily in the name of admission, and similarly, money is said to be demanded when students ask for mark sheets and other documents. Students remained firm on their demands Students from Classes 6 to 12 took part in the protest. Principal Lal Bahadur Singh and Station House Officer (Kishanpur) Manish Singh initially tried to persuade the students to end the protest, but they refused and remained firm on their demands. The protest continued into the afternoon until District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) Rakesh Kumar arrived at the campus. Kumar spoke with the students and assured them that their demands would be met within 24 hours. Following the protest, the school was closed for the day. After videos of the children's protest circulated, the DIOS confirmed that the students' demands had been accepted. Four fans will now be installed in every classroom by the next day, and the wiring will be fixed. Desks and benches will be provided within a month, and one RO water cooler will be installed. Students' demands accepted Rakesh Kumar told the students that arrangements for clean drinking water at the school would be made immediately. Toilets will be kept clean, and a computer laboratory, library, and sports facilities will also be provided with immediate effect. If illegal fees are being collected from students, this will be investigated, and strict action will be taken against those responsible. Who are Generation Alpha? Generation Alpha includes children born between 2010 and 2024. They follow Generation Z, whose members were born between 1997 and 2012.

stories.title: Student hacks IIT Kanpur website after missing admission:Says 'I just need one chance', director offers a fresh test after seeing his talent
stories.summary: A student hacked the website of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kanpur after failing to secure admission. He had applied for the Bachelor's in Cyber Security programme. On Tuesday, he breached the institute's high-security website and posted the message: "I just need one chance." The student also shared screenshots of the hack on social media platforms X and Reddit, taking responsibility for the breach. The incident caused a stir within IIT, and the matter reached the institute's director. The administration initially considered filing an FIR but later changed its decision, taking the student's future into account. IIT Kanpur Director Manindra Agrawal said that if the student genuinely possesses strong cyber security skills, he will be invited back for a fresh test. However, he stressed that illegally breaking into a cyber system is not the right way to demonstrate cyber security expertise. For now, the institute has not disclosed any information that could identify the student, citing concern for his future. Student wrote on hacked website: 'Give me a chance to prove myself' After hacking the website, the student posted the following message: "I completed the entire IIT admission process properly. I submitted my application, paid the fee, uploaded all the required documents, and even provided proof of my work in cyber security. All I want is one opportunity for my abilities to be recognised. I want my skills to be evaluated. My intention was never to harm anyone. I hacked the website only to draw the attention of the institute's cyber security professors. Users can continue using the website by clicking the button below. If you are part of the IIT administration or the cyber security team, I request you to understand my side of the story. I want to explain my situation as a hacker and why I felt compelled to take this step. I have the capability to damage the website, but I was not considered worthy of selection for the B.Cyber programme." Director says student will be invited for a fresh test IIT Kanpur Director Prof. Manindra Agrawal said, "Applications for the four-year Bachelor's in Cyber Security (B.Cyber) programme were accepted from 15 to 25 June this year. A hackathon was held on 5 July as part of the selection process, giving applicants an opportunity to demonstrate their skills. At that stage, this student was unable to prove his capabilities. "Now, to verify his claims, we will invite him to the institute for a fresh test. IIT Kanpur has previously given opportunities to talented young people in cyber security. Recently, a youth who identified a vulnerability in the CBSE online portal was offered a job at the institute's C3iHub." How admission to the B.Cyber programme works Admission to IIT Kanpur's Bachelor's in Cyber Security (B.Cyber) programme is not based solely on JEE Main scores. Students must have completed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM). The selection process begins with an assessment of the candidate's JEE Main performance. The institute also evaluates prior work in cyber security, such as bug bounty programmes, Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions, open-source projects, or other cyber security projects. Shortlisted candidates are then invited to IIT Kanpur, where they undergo a technical assessment and a hackathon to evaluate their practical skills. Final admission is based on a combination of JEE Main scores, cyber security expertise and hackathon performance. Four-year programme The B.Cyber programme spans four years. During the first two years, students study on the IIT Kanpur campus, receiving both classroom instruction and hands-on laboratory training. In the final two years, students undertake internships with government security organisations across India. During these placements, they work on real-world projects involving cyber defence, preventing hacking, and securing government systems.

stories.title: 'Ram Mandir donation thieves, step down':Akhilesh raises slogans outside Parliament; Dimple arrives with donation box to mock govt
stories.summary: SP MPs staged a noisy protest outside Parliament on Wednesday over the alleged theft of Ram Mandir donations. Dimple Yadav arrived carrying a donation box and asked SP MPs and journalists to put money into it. Several SP MPs dropped cash into the box, followed later by Akhilesh Yadav. During the protest, SP MPs raised slogans of, 'Donation thief, step down from the throne'. Dimple Yadav alleged that BJP leaders had "swallowed" public donations. "Such a major incident has taken place in Ayodhya. It is the Chief Minister's responsibility to explain how this scam happened. SITs are formed merely as a formality to divert public attention," she said. Akhilesh Yadav said, "Those who could not even protect a donation box cannot be trusted with anything. The message is clear: if they can play with people's faith, they can also play with the future of our youth." Proceedings in the Lok Sabha were disrupted as soon as the House convened at 11 am on Wednesday, with opposition MPs raising slogans. Amid the uproar, the House was adjourned till noon. After reconvening, discussion resumed on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, related to paper leaks. The House continued the debate for a second consecutive day after a nine-hour discussion on Tuesday. Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad says government is protecting 'big fish' Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad said, "It is unfortunate that the BJP and its government are protecting the big fish. This government came to power because of Ayodhya, and it will fall because of Ayodhya. That process has already begun. The BJP will not win even 50 seats. This is not Awadhesh Prasad speaking; it is the will of the Lord."

stories.title: Former minister's wife faints as funeral procession begins:Brother accuses MLA's caretaker of murder, complains to Lucknow Police
stories.summary: A new twist has emerged in the death case of Nanakdeen Bhurji, the State General Secretary of BJP's Backward Class Morcha and a former State Minister. Nanakdeen's younger brother has filed a complaint at Hazratganj Kotwali, accusing Muhammad Arif, the caretaker of Ballia's Belthara Road MLA Hansuram, of murder. However, the police say that the investigation so far and the evidence found at the scene point towards suicide. Investigation is ongoing, keeping both aspects of the case in mind. Nanakdeen's last rites will be performed on Wednesday at Bhaisakund. Nanakdeen's final journey began on Wednesday morning from his residence in Khadra, Madeganj. During this, his wife Manju Devi fainted. Nanakdeen Bhurji died on Tuesday, 28 July, after falling from the seventh floor of the new MLA residence in Darulshafa. Nanakdeen reached the MLA's residence at 2 PM According to the police, on Tuesday afternoon around 2 PM, Nanakdeen Bhurji reached the new MLA residence of BJP MLA Hansuram from Belthara Road. The MLA was not present at that time. Nanakdeen asked the helper present there to bring coffee and sat in the room. Helper returned with coffee to find the chair empty According to the police, when the helper returned with coffee, Nanakdeen was not in the room. Meanwhile, noise was heard outside. People went downstairs and found Nanakdeen Bhurji lying on the ground in serious condition. Police, who arrived on information, immediately took him to the civil hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Brother accused of murder After the incident, Pradeep Kumar Gupta, the younger brother of the deceased, filed a complaint with the Hazratganj police, accusing Mohammad Arif, caretaker of MLA Hansuram, of murder. He has demanded an impartial investigation and action in the matter. The police conducted a post-mortem of the body and handed it over to the family. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and other evidence. According to family members, Nanakdeen Bhurji's last rites will be performed on Wednesday. Police say that every aspect of the case is being thoroughly investigated.

stories.title: Religious conversions carried out in Lucknow for 20 years:Locals say children cover their ears at the sound of bhajans
stories.summary: An organised network of religious conversion was operating in the Mohanlalganj (about 21 km from Lucknow) for about 20 years under the guise of prayer meetings. The gang first identified people in villages who were sick, childless, poor, and struggling with family problems. After this, they were invited to prayer meetings with temptations such as curing illness, having children, getting jobs, and arranging marriages. The newly converted were given ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh and a job based on their caste. After changing their religion, these same people trapped other people they know through the same temptations. Children are taught to stay away from the worship of Hindu deities and prasad. Children in the newly converted families would cover their ears as soon as they heard the sound of bhajans and kirtans. This network was spread not only in Mohanlalganj but also in surrounding villages and up to the border of Rae Bareli district. After the revelation of the conversion gang, a Dainik Bhaskar team reached Devaria Bharsawan in Mohanlalganj and found surprising information. The villagers said that those who have converted from Hinduism to Christianity are annoyed by devotional songs (bhajan-kirtan) and worship. Even the children in their homes cover their ears as soon as they hear the sound of bhajan-kirtan. 'Threatened for opposing conversion to Christianity' Amit Kumar, a resident of Devariya Bharsawan village in Mohanlalganj, alleges that Chandrabhan, his wife Aarti, Seema, Subala, Daniel, Sheela, and Ajay Rawat from the same village had been pressuring him for a long time to convert to Christianity. He states that the accused had told him that if he started going to church and accepted Christianity, he would have children at home. When he resisted, the accused said, "Do whatever you want; we are not afraid of anyone. We will continue to convert people." Gang apprehended on 22 July According to Amit, on 22 July, all the accused again reached Devariya Bharsawan village. He asked them not to come to the village with the intention of religious conversion, but they did not comply. After this, at around 8:15 PM, Amit informed the police on Dial-112. It is alleged that as soon as the accused learned about the police being informed, they started verbally abusing. Amit tried to stop them there until the police arrived. During this, when he tried to stop their Bolero vehicle, Chandrabhan threatened to run him over. Meanwhile, the police, who arrived on receiving the information, took all seven accused into custody from the spot. After this, Amit Kumar gave a written complaint of the entire incident to the police. Based on the complaint, a case was registered and all seven accused were arrested and sent to jail. Police say that during the investigation, some evidence related to religious conversion has also been found and the entire network is being investigated. Became a target for the gang due to not having children Amit works as a caterer. Amit said that he got married about 10 years ago. He does not have any children. Chandrabhan Rawat was aware of this. Chandrabhan repeatedly spoke of coming to God's refuge and said that they would have children. He used to ask him to come with him to the prayer place. Upon this, he agreed to go, but he said that he would not take any water or medicine there. “Give this in writing on a stamp paper so that no pressure will be put there, because of this, Amit's conversation with Chandrabhan stopped,” Amit recalled. Some time ago he had gone to work. Then Chandrabhan's wife Seema came home and started telling his wife that ‘if God wills, your lap will be filled’. For this, she started asking her to come to the prayer place daily. Similarly, she started luring Jai Prakash of the village as well. Jai Prakash has daughters, whose marriage Seema used to talk about arranging. Said in the video, ‘Let us pray to our God’ On the night of the incident, Amit informed the police and also made a video of the scene. In it, everyone is seen threatening Amit. Chandrabhan's wife Seema is saying, "You worship your God. We will worship our God. No one will be able to do anything." Ram Lal's nephew went to jail a year ago Villagers said that Ram Lal, Chandra Bhan, and Manoj Pasi of the village have converted their religion. Manoj's in-laws live in Mati Alinagar. They have also converted. Since then, every poor and weaker section of the village is being targeted. Ram Lal's nephew Malkhan, a resident of Baktaurikheda, has gone to Kanakaha Jail. After he went to jail, everything remained quiet for a few days, but after some time, everyone again got involved in the work of religious conversion. They would also pressure many people to convert by threatening them. They did not listen to bhajans and kirtans Kaushalya, a resident of the village, said that a Bolero car would come and park in front of her house, in which all the church people would arrive. They would take them home, introducing them as relatives. Everyone wore white clothes and there were also three or four women with them. Everyone would arrive at 8 PM and leave between 11 PM and 12 PM. Chandrabhan, Aarti, Seema, Manoj, and people from Manoj's in-laws' house in Alinagar also used to come. These people would come to see them off. Malkhan, who is Seema's paternal aunt's son-in-law, started it here. He went to jail a year ago. A lot of money comes from religious conversion, and everything was done by luring people with that money. If there was any bhajan-kirtan (devotional singing) in the village, the children from their house would cover their ears. When asked why, the children would say that their family members had told them not to take prasad (offerings) if there was any worship. Devils reside in gods and goddesses; sing the praises of your Lord. Poor families were targeted Poor families were often the target of this gang. Besides Bharsawa village, the accused also converted people from Phulwaria, Jyoti Nagar, and Gaura. Currently, their number has reached close to four thousand. The gang had fixed rates according to caste. They were guided by a church in Kanyakumari. The rates for Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Sheikhs, Sayyads, and Pathans were different. Used to give ₹3 lakh to upper castes and ₹2 lakh to backward castes Upon religious conversion, upper castes were given ₹3 lakh and backward castes ₹2 lakh. They promised to arrange marriages for unmarried men with girls who had already converted. Dalits received a proposal of ₹1 lakh, a job, and marriage. Now, most of the poor families are falling for their deception. Gaurakshaks also arrived upon receiving information Vimlesh Sharma of Shri Ram Sanatan Sevak Team stated that many families in villages around Bharsawa village have also been converted. On the day of the incident, as soon as we received information, we also arrived. Even on that day, we warned them to leave from there, but everyone was bent on bullying. After this, the police were informed. This work of religious conversion had been going on for about 20 years. ADCP South Rallapalli Vasanth Kumar said- On the night of 22 July, information was received from a caller in Bharsawa village that approximately seven people arrived in a Bolero vehicle, threatening some villagers and offering various inducements, attempting to convert them to Christianity.Considering the seriousness of the matter, the police team reached the spot. All seven accused were arrested. The Bolero car was also seized. All the accused have been sent to jail. The network is being investigated.

stories.title: Businessman's grandson murdered for ₹1 crore ransom:Accused says he needed to repay a ₹36 lakh debt
stories.summary: “I had a debt of ₹36 lakh. My father used to taunt me every month for not depositing the instalment. He called me worthless. Disturbed by this, I planned to kidnap the son of a bullion trader. With the help of AI, I gathered information about the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. I understood how the gang operates and how they demand ransom. I bought a Cambodian mobile number for ₹199 from the internet and created a WhatsApp account on it.” “On Monday evening, I lured Vaibhav with a gift and took him with me. When he started screaming, I got angry. I pushed him to the ground, put my knee on his chest, and strangled him. I stuffed the body into a sack and hid it in the house's basement. After this, I made a WhatsApp call and demanded a ransom of ₹1 crore from Vaibhav's father. To avoid suspicion, I continued to pretend to search for Vaibhav with my family.” This is the confession of computer teacher Sarvesh, alias Bittu Bhatt, accused of murdering Vaibhav, the 10-year-old grandson of a jeweller in Gorakhpur. Police have taken seven people into custody, including Sarvesh's father, brother, and wife. Sarvesh had been imprisoned for 40 days in Prayagraj's Naini Jail in 2024 in connection with a paper leak case in Bihar. He got married a year ago. Today, Vaibhav's last rites will be performed in Ayodhya. Find out when Vaibhav went missing and how the accused was caught. Lakshmi Narayan Verma lives in Khajni town. He is among the big jewellery businessmen in the area. Vaibhav, the youngest son of Hanuman, Lakshmi Narayan's son, studied in the fourth grade at Navels Academy. The accused Sarvesh's house is 20 meters away at the end of the same lane where Vaibhav's house is. Sarvesh's father Harinarayan owns a cloth shop. His elder brother Satish is a lawyer. Sarvesh himself runs a computer coaching centre, where diploma courses and TET preparation are offered. On Monday at 1:30 PM, Vaibhav returned from school. After reaching home, he kept his bag, changed his uniform, and left the house with his bicycle. Thirty minutes later, a neighbour came home and informed that Vaibhav's bicycle was lying behind the house. His grandmother reached 50 meters from the house, but Vaibhav was not seen. She searched nearby, but she could not find Vaibhav. The grandmother informed the family. One of Vaibhav's slippers was found lying in an empty field 100 meters away from where the bicycle was found. The family suspected kidnapping. The police were immediately informed. SSP Dr Kaustubh immediately formed five teams. One team started scanning CCTV footage. In a CCTV footage, Vaibhav was seen going towards the field with his neighbour Sarvesh Bhatt. Police apprehended Sarvesh. During interrogation, he confessed to his crime. Vaibhav's body was sent for post-mortem examination by a panel of two doctors on Tuesday. Its videography was also done. The post-mortem report confirmed that Vaibhav was strangled to death. After the post-mortem, the child's body was sent home by ambulance. After the incident, an angry mob entered the police station. They tried to pull out the accused kept in the lockup. Police acted strictly and dispersed the crowd. Killed and hid the body in the house's basement Sarvesh told the police, 'He had taken a loan of ₹25 lakh from a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC). Its monthly installment of ₹28,700 had to be paid. Besides this, he had borrowed 11 lakh rupees from a friend. Thus, he had a total debt of 36 lakh rupees. To repay this debt, he planned Vaibhav's kidnapping. He said, "Vaibhav was passing in front of the house. I stopped him and said that I have a gift for you, come with me. He refused and said he would complain to his father. However, he later agreed. I took him to the field at the edge of the house and strangled him to death. After the murder, the body was put into a sack. In the afternoon, he reached home with the sack. At that time, his father, wife, and sister-in-law were in their respective rooms. He placed the sack containing the body among the grain sacks in the basement and covered it with a quilt and a mattress. SP South Dinesh Puri said, “When the police searched the accused's mobile phone, they found several AI-generated questions and their answers. These included information related to Lawrence Bishnoi gang's extortion methods and gang activities. Police also found a Cambodian SIM card with him. The accused had also prepared a mule (fake) bank account.” Notice pasted on the accused's under-construction building The District Panchayat has pasted a notice on the under-construction building of the accused's father, Harinarayan, located in Rudrapur. stories.title: Yogi offers prayers at Gorakhnath Temple on Guru Purnima:Pays tributes to late Mahant Avaidyanath; feeds jaggery and gram to cows
stories.summary: On the occasion of Guru Purnima on Wednesday morning, Gorakshpeethadhishwar and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath performed special puja of Mahayogi Guru Gorakhnath with due rituals at Gorakhnath Temple. After this, he paid tribute to the gurus of Nathpanth, including his guru Brahmaleen Mahant Avaidyanath and Dadasguru Mahant Digvijaynath. During the worship, CM Yogi also offered prayers at all the major deities and the samadhis of the Brahmaleen Mahants located in the temple complex. According to the tradition of Nathpanth, Mahaprasad of 'rot' (bread) was offered to Guru Gorakhnath. After this, the Chief Minister reached the temple's cowshed and fed jaggery and gram to the cows. After leaving the cowshed, the Chief Minister also offered prayers at the ancient Kali Mata Temple. After this, he reached the 'Janata Darshan' (public audience), where he listened to petitioners' grievances and instructed the officials to ensure their speedy resolution.

stories.title: CM Yogi hears 200 complainants on Guru Purnima:Orders officials to ensure every grievance is resolved
stories.summary: On the occasion of Guru Purnima, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath met with people who had come to Janta Darshan, organised outside the Mahant Digvijaynath Smriti Bhawan located within the Gorakhnath Temple complex. The CM listened to the problems of about 200 complainants. He assured everyone that their complaints would be resolved. The Chief Minister himself went among the people and listened to their problems one by one. He instructed the officials that every complaint should be resolved seriously, sensitively, and in a time-bound manner. There will be no shortage of money for the treatment of serious patients Many people arrived at Janta Darshan seeking financial assistance for the treatment of serious illnesses. The Chief Minister assured that no one's treatment would stop due to lack of money. He instructed officials to quickly prepare an estimate for the patients' treatment and send it to the government, so that financial assistance can be provided on time. Some people from Ghazipur and Deoria complained about not getting possession of their land. The Chief Minister instructed officials to coordinate with the officials of the concerned districts to investigate the matter and ensure that eligible people get possession of their land. Gave chocolates to children, inquired about their well-being In the Janta Darshan, the Chief Minister gave chocolates to the children who came. He inquired about the children's well-being and also spoke with their family members. Before the Janta Darshan, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath visited the cowshed in the Gorakhnath Temple complex. Here, he fed jaggery and bread to the cows. Taking stock of the cowshed's arrangements, he instructed the staff to maintain cleanliness and ensure better care for all cows.

stories.title: Heavy rain lashes Sambhal, trees swept away in Gonda:Floodwaters enter 50 temples in Varanasi, 100 families flee homes in Ballia
stories.summary: Rivers across Uttar Pradesh are in spate following heavy rainfall in the hills. In Ballia, floodwaters from the Saryu River have entered villages, forcing around 100 families to leave their homes. In Varanasi, the Ganga has inundated more than 50 small and large temples. In Gonda, the Ghaghara River is eroding its banks at a rapid pace. Several bighas of farmland and many trees have already been washed away. Fearing further erosion, residents are demolishing their homes and migrating to safer places. Sambhal received heavy rainfall at around 11 am on Wednesday, leaving roads waterlogged. A rain alert has been issued for 60 districts across the state today, with six districts under a heavy rainfall warning. On Tuesday, rain was recorded in 55 cities across Uttar Pradesh. In Noida, heavy evening showers left roads submerged in waist-deep water, with cars and motorcycles stranded underwater. Four children were swept away in rainwater drains in Shrawasti, Bareilly and Bulandshahr. In Shrawasti, two young children who were washed away died. An eight-year-old boy in Bareilly and an 11-year-old schoolgirl in Bulandshahr remain missing. Bulandshahr recorded the state's highest rainfall in the past 24 hours, receiving 44.9 mm rain. Since 1 June, Uttar Pradesh has recorded 25% below-normal rainfall. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: "The monsoon trough is once again shifting towards Uttar Pradesh, while the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is also strengthening. As a result, both eastern and western parts of the state are likely to receive widespread rainfall. Several districts may witness light to moderate rain, with heavy showers at isolated places, till 30 July. There is also a possibility of lightning in some areas."

stories.title: 122 UP MLAs are turncoats, what lies ahead till 2027?:Ministers and MPs are no different, 30% of BJP legislators switched from other parties; see list
stories.summary: The buzz about party switching in UP politics has intensified again. It is very difficult to say which leader will be in which party before the 2027 assembly elections. Opportunism exists in every state of the country, but UP's political leaders are at the forefront of it. Some leaders are such who joined every party when they got the opportunity. Some leaders came back, but when they got the chance, they left the party again. UP government minister Dara Singh Chauhan has changed parties 5 times. When Dainik Bhaskar scrutinized 15 years of records, the picture of UP regarding turncoat leaders turned out to be shocking. Out of UP's current 399 MLAs, 30% i.e., 122 MLAs are turncoats. MPs also did not lag behind in changing parties when they got the opportunity. First, let's talk about UP's MLAs 78 MLAs reached BJP after being in other parties Ministers who changed party once Every second of our MPs changed parties Leaders from other parties behind SP's good performance Uttar Pradesh has 80 MPs in the Lok Sabha. Among them, SP's MPs are the biggest defectors. Out of 37 MPs, 19 have changed parties and joined SP. This is approximately 51%. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP achieved its best performance in its history, securing 37 seats. Leaders who came from other parties made a significant contribution to the SP's success. BJP has 33 MPs from UP in the Lok Sabha. Among them, 15 have joined BJP from other parties. Thus, about 45% of the party's MPs are defectors. Only 18 MPs are from the BJP cadre. Among alliance partners, 50% of RLD's MPs fall into this category. Out of RLD's total 2 MPs, one has defected. In Congress too, 50% of MPs joined the party sensing a political opportunity. Out of Congress's 6 MPs, 3 are defectors. These include Imran Masood, Rakesh Rathore, and Ujjwal Raman Singh. While Rahul Gandhi, Kishori Lal Sharma, and Tanuj Punia are staunch Congress members. Ministers who changed party twice Prominent figures who changed parties twice BJP MP SP Singh Baghel from Agra has changed parties twice. Mulayam Singh Yadav brought him into politics. In 1998, he became an MP for the first time from Jalesar on a SP ticket. After differences with Ramgopal Yadav, he left SP. In 2010, he joined BSP and went to Rajya Sabha. Just before the 2014 elections, he joined BJP. Since then, he has continuously been an MP from Agra on a BJP ticket (2014, 2019, 2024). Ministers who changed party 3 times Sakshi Maharaj, who first became an MP from Mathura on a BJP ticket in 1991, was an MP from Farrukhabad in 1996 and 1998. When BJP denied him a ticket in 1999, he joined the Samajwadi Party. He was expelled from the Rajya Sabha in 2006 after his name surfaced in a sting operation related to the MP fund scam. In 2012, he returned to the BJP. He was then elected as an MP from Unnao three consecutive times in 2014, 2019, and 2024. MPs who changed parties Cabinet Minister Nand Gopal 'Nandi' in the Yogi government has been a part of 3 parties in his political career. In 2007, he was elected MLA for the first time from Allahabad City South on a BSP ticket. He became a minister in the Mayawati government. In 2014, he was expelled from BSP on charges of indiscipline. He joined Congress. In the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, he contested from the Allahabad seat on a Congress ticket, but lost. Just before the 2017 UP assembly elections, he joined BJP. MLAs who changed parties Cabinet Minister Rakesh Sachan changed parties twice. He became an MLA on a Samajwadi Party ticket in 1993 and 2002. In 2009, he was elected MP from Fatehpur Lok Sabha seat. Just before the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, he joined Congress. Before the 2022 assembly elections, he joined BJP. He won from Bhognipur assembly seat in Kanpur Dehat. He is a cabinet minister in the Yogi government. Leaders who never changed their party UP government ministers have also benefited from changing parties Dara Singh Chauhan is the minister who has changed parties the most in the UP cabinet. He has changed parties 5 times so far. There are also many ministers who have become MLA, MP and then minister by changing parties once, twice or thrice. Leaders who changed parties twice (with Year) Parties are also adept at changing alliances Parties here have also frequently changed alliances. Currently, the NDA government is in power in UP. It includes BJP along with Apna Dal (S), Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), Suheldev Bhartiya Samaj Party (SBSP), and Nishad Party. Among these, Apna Dal and Nishad Party have been with BJP from the beginning. However, RLD and SBSP have changed their political partners from time to time. RLD - Sometimes with BJP, sometimes with SP, sometimes with Congress Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) formed alliances with different parties in different elections. The party has been a part of grand alliances formed sometimes with BJP, sometimes with SP, sometimes with Congress and BSP. Most often, RLD has contested elections with BJP and SP. SBSP: Alliances kept changing over the years Om Prakash Rajbhar's SBSP has also changed its political partners many times.

stories.title: Man reaches police outpost with knife lodged in back:Victim alleges bikers attacked him; sub-inspector took bribe but took no action
stories.summary: A young man arrived at a police outpost in Ballia on Wednesday morning with a knife lodged in his back, claiming he had been attacked by bike-borne assailants. He alleged that the attackers stabbed him in the back before fleeing. The victim further claimed he had complained about threats earlier, but no action was taken. According to the young man, he had been facing harassment for the past 15 days and had repeatedly approached the police. He alleged that the outpost in-charge accepted a bribe and failed to act on his complaints. When he reached the Hanumanganj police outpost, the blade was completely embedded in his back, with only the handle visible. A video of the incident has also surfaced. Now know the complete matter Thana Sukhpura area resident Ritesh Tiwari (45), who lives in Jeerabasti, is a stamp vendor at the registry office. On Wednesday morning, he had gone to the court. The distance from his village to the court is about 3 kilometers. Ritesh was returning from there around 9 am. On the way, near Devkali village, a bike rider coming from behind stabbed him in the back with a knife. Before he could understand anything, the bike rider had fled. Attack 500 meters away from police post In an injured condition, Ritesh reached Hanumanganj police post located 500 meters from the incident site. The knife was stuck in his back. Upon arriving here, he complained to the police personnel present. Ritesh said - A bike-riding criminal has attacked me. It is the result of the post in-charge's negligence that a life-threatening attack was made on me today. Ritesh was sent to the district hospital in critical condition. After primary treatment here, he was referred to Trauma Center Varanasi, where his treatment is ongoing. ASP South Sanjay Kumar Verma said - A person has been stabbed by a bike-borne miscreant. Police have taken 2 suspects into custody. They are being interrogated. There is an ongoing dispute between both parties over land. Action will be taken against the accused who carried out the attack. Station House Officer Ratnesh Dubey said- Chowki in-charge Adarsh Shrivastava has been transferred. Currently, the chowki is being operated from the police station itself. On July 4, Ritesh's brother had filed a case against Parvind Tiwari and 4 others for assault and causing injury. The investigation is ongoing. Meanwhile, 4 cases are also registered against Ritesh at the Kotwali.

stories.title: Woman crushed between 2 government buses:Drivers start moving together; victim dies on spot
stories.summary: A major accident occurred at the roadways bus stand in Hardoi. A woman died after being trapped between two buses. Two buses were parked together at the stand. A woman started to pass between them. Just then, both drivers suddenly moved their respective buses forward. As a result, the woman got trapped between the two. By the time both drivers could understand what was happening, the woman was crushed after being trapped between the buses. Her head burst open while she was standing. After the accident, there was chaos at the scene. People raised an alarm, and then both drivers became aware of the accident. The accident occurred at the roadways bus stand located in the City Kotwali area on Wednesday afternoon around 1:30 PM. Now the full story in detail Neha Singh (32), who lived in Khetui village in the Kotwali Dehat area, worked for a pharma (medicine) company. On Wednesday morning, she left home to attend a company meeting in Bangarmau, Unnao. She was waiting for a bus at the stand. According to eyewitnesses, Neha was sitting at the bus stand. Just then, a bus going to Unnao arrived. Neha got up to catch the bus. She started walking between the Kannauj Depot and Hardoi Depot buses that were already parked at the stand. Just then, the drivers of both buses started them and moved them forward. As a result, Neha got trapped between the front parts of both buses while standing. Neha screamed and shouted, and people rushed After this, Neha started screaming and shouting for help. At this, the people nearby rushed over. They made noise and stopped both drivers, but by then Neha was badly crushed. Her head was caught between the two buses and crushed. People pulled Neha out from between the buses and took her to the medical college, where doctors declared her dead. Upon receiving the information, the police arrived and sent the body for post-mortem. Meanwhile, upon hearing the news of his sister-in-law's death, Neha's brother-in-law, Vireesh Singh, reached the spot. He alleges that the accident happened due to the negligence of both bus drivers. Without checking whether anyone was present in front, both buses were moved forward simultaneously. Husband also died in a similar way Vireesh said - Sister-in-law Neha was working to manage the family responsibilities. 10 years ago, my brother (Neha's husband) Sarvesh Singh also died in an accident. He also died after being trapped between a DCM and a truck. He has a 15-year-old daughter, Riya Singh, and an 11-year-old son, Vivek. After the accident, both children became orphans.

stories.title: VIDEO shows guards beating 15-year-old in Lucknow:Police bring him to hospital for medical; Deputy CM seeks report
stories.summary: A 15-year-old boy was allegedly assaulted by security guards at Balrampur Hospital in Lucknow. A video of the incident has surfaced, showing the guards allegedly beating the child, triggering outrage. After the video came to light, the matter reached the health department. Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Brajesh Pathak took cognisance of the incident and ordered an inquiry. He has sought a detailed report from the hospital administration, and further action will be taken based on the findings. Incident at 6:30 AM, police brought him to the hospital for medical examination According to information, at two o'clock in the night, police brought a total of 5 people from Madayganj police outpost for medical examination. Medical examination of 2 of them was done, while 3 were left because of lack of papers. Police left them even in the emergency. Meanwhile, in the morning, these three had a dispute with EMO Dr. Surur Ali over some matter. After this, when the guards arrived at the scene, the argument escalated. Soon, a fight broke out. Instructions to submit investigation report in 3 days The Deputy CM posted on X and informed that he has instructed the Director General, Medical and Health, to personally visit the spot and investigate the matter, considering its seriousness. He has also asked to take action against the culprits and submit the investigation report within three days. He wrote that taking cognizance of the video related to the assault at Balrampur Hospital, Lucknow, orders have been given to the Director General, Medical and Health, to investigate the matter. After the investigation, action will be taken against the culprits and the report will have to be submitted within three days. CCTV footage is being reviewed Dr. Vivek Gupta, Director of Balrampur Hospital, stated regarding this matter that CCTV footage is being reviewed concerning the incident. Investigation orders have also been issued by the government. A report will be prepared based on an impartial investigation and then sent to the government. Efforts will be made to complete the investigation before the stipulated time.

stories.title: ‘Students are worried about their future,’ says Shankaracharya:Sant claims India is heading towards dictatorship; cow protection fight to continue
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's Gavishth Yatra, which started 81 days ago from Gorakhpur Rural, concluded today. Speaking to the media in a marriage hall in Ramjanki Nagar, Shankaracharya said- The country is moving towards dictatorship. Now the government wants to turn it into North Korea. Students are worried about their future. He said- Even the programs scheduled for July 24 in Lucknow were attempted to be stopped at the administrative level. I have told my army to organise programs in the assemblies, but I will participate in the program at the scheduled time and place. He said- CM Yogi has respected neither religion nor the constitution. Namaz has never been offered on the stairs of Hanumangarhi. He told a blatant lie. When he reached Ayodhya, he said- I will make everything clear. But he could not do it. When he went again, he fabricated a false story. It should be noted that he started his journey on May 3, 2026, from Gorakhpur Rural assembly constituency, demanding that 'Gau Mata' (Cow Mother) be declared the 'Rashtra Mata' (Mother of the Nation). The journey concluded on July 21 upon reaching Gorakhpur city. 5 Big Statements by Shankaracharya The movement will continue until a complete ban on cow slaughter nationwide Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said - This journey was not just a religious event, but a campaign for national consciousness. In 81 days, millions of people supported it, and the message of cow protection reached across the country. He reiterated that until 'Gau Mata' (Mother Cow) is given the status of 'Rashtramata' (Mother of the Nation) and a complete ban on cow slaughter is imposed nationwide, his movement will continue. Youth are fighting not for any party, but for their future Shankaracharya commented on the students' protest and police action at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. He said - the youth of the country are concerned about their future. He stated that students are protesting not for any political party or organization, but to secure their future. He said - if anyone guarantees their future, the youth will stand with them. Therefore, this movement should not be linked to any single party or organization. He said - during the protest, he witnessed a scene where police and security forces stood with weapons in front of students marching towards Parliament. Calling it a matter of concern for democracy, he said that just as students were dealt with strictly, common citizens might also be treated similarly in the future. In a democracy, the voice of protest should be answered with dialogue, not with the use of force. Danger of North Korea-like situation arising Shankaracharya said - Efforts are being made to suppress the voices of dissent in the country. Pressure is increasing on democratic institutions and action is being taken against those who protest. He said - If this situation continues, the day is not far when India's situation will become like North Korea. He called it a serious threat to democratic values. The administration stopped the July 24 program Shankaracharya said - The resolution ceremony of his Ashirvani Sena was proposed in Lucknow on July 24. For this, the ground fee had been deposited almost a month in advance, and an application for permission had also been sent to the administration 15 days prior. Despite this, permission has not been granted till date. He said - This is not just a matter of administrative procedure, but a deliberate attempt to sabotage his program. Whereas, in a democratic system, stopping a religious-social program in this manner is not appropriate. Supporters were threatened Shankaracharya said - During the Gavishthi Yatra, continuous administrative pressure was exerted. Those who expressed a desire to host him at their homes or offer support were threatened. Notices were issued against his supporters in many places. The administration made every possible effort to prevent the yatra from being successful, but despite this, public support continued to grow. He said- After not getting permission, he has instructed his Ashirwani Sena that all workers should organize 'Sankalp' (pledge) programs in their respective constituencies. Meanwhile, he himself will reach Lucknow on July 24 at the scheduled time and place to address his supporters. He said that the movement will not stop due to any administrative restrictions.

stories.title: 'Congress, SP first incited farmers, now students':Yogi says Oppn believes in unrest, hooliganism; accuses them of spreading lies
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath targeted the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress during an event in Gorakhpur, accusing them of misleading farmers earlier and now trying to provoke students. He claimed the Opposition was running protests as part of a conspiracy to defame students. He also alleged that SP and Congress supporters had surrounded Parliament in Delhi and accused both parties of spreading a false narrative. According to him, their strategy was to repeat lies until they appeared to be true, adding that such narratives must be exposed. Addressing a conference of booth presidents from Gorakhpur city and rural Assembly constituencies at the Yogiraj Baba Gambhirnath Auditorium on Wednesday, the Chief Minister gave election tips to 892 booth presidents ahead of the upcoming polls. Congress and SP glorified Jinnah Yogi claimed that during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Opposition spread misinformation in society. He alleged that Congress falsely promised to give ₹1 lakh and that SP and Congress created a misleading narrative on reservation. He said leaders such as Dr B R Ambedkar, Maharishi Valmiki and Sant Ravidas received due respect under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP government. The Chief Minister added that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who made a significant contribution to the nation, was also honoured by the BJP government through the construction of the world's tallest statue. He alleged that Congress and SP glorified Muhammad Ali Jinnah instead of recognising leaders such as Patel and Ambedkar. Booth presidents must expose Opposition's conspiracy Yogi urged booth presidents to remain alert, claiming that Congress and SP could once again try to create confusion in society, as they allegedly did during the 2024 elections. He asked party workers to expose what he described as the Opposition's misinformation campaign at the booth level. He also asked them to take the government's development and welfare schemes to every household and maintain regular contact with people. The Chief Minister invited those present to Thursday's inauguration of the six-lane flyover in Gorakhpur and encouraged them to visit the structure, take selfies and share them on social media. The booth that wins also wins the election Calling the booth the most important organisational unit, Yogi repeated Prime Minister Modi's slogan, Mera Booth Sabse Majboot (My Booth is the Strongest). He said elections are ultimately won at the booth level, not in the state, district or constituency. According to him, the booth with stronger public support and greater outreach is the one that secures victory. BJP will form government in Uttar Pradesh for a third term The Chief Minister compared booth workers to soldiers guarding the country's borders, saying their alertness helps the BJP form governments at both the Centre and in the state. He expressed confidence that the BJP would return to power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term in the 2027 Assembly elections. He also congratulated booth presidents for their full attendance at the conference. No one dies of hunger now, 80 crore people get free ration Yogi said India's image had improved globally under Prime Minister Modi's leadership and that the country was now viewed with respect and trust. He said welfare schemes such as housing, Ayushman Bharat, free ration and free LPG connections had reached every eligible beneficiary without discrimination. According to him, 80 crore people across India and 16 crore people in Uttar Pradesh are receiving free ration. The Chief Minister alleged that people died of hunger under previous governments and referred to reports of Musahar community members dying of starvation in Kushinagar. He also recalled former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's statement that only ₹15 out of every ₹100 sent by the government reached the poor, saying the current government has ensured full transparency through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Nine lakh government jobs given transparently Yogi said his government had provided nine lakh government jobs through a transparent recruitment process, claiming there was no recommendation, favouritism or bribery involved. He also alleged that during the SP government, recruitment for SDM posts had favoured a particular caste. The Chief Minister said that before 2017, young people from Gorakhpur and Uttar Pradesh were looked down upon, but today they receive respect wherever they go. He added that the BJP government had also preserved the state's cultural and religious heritage by constructing the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, redeveloping the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor and Vindhyachal Dham, and promoting the Naimisharanya pilgrimage site. In previous governments, deaths occurred due to hunger, now 80 crore people receive free ration In the Booth Presidents' Conference, Yogi also elaborated on the conceptual changes, development works, and public welfare that have come about in the BJP's double-engine government in the country and the state. He said that under the leadership of PM Modi, the world's perception of India has changed. Now India is seen not with suspicion, but with respect and trust. In the double-engine government, the benefits of poor welfare schemes have reached the person at the last rung of society without discrimination. The benefits of schemes related to housing, Ayushman, free ration, and free cooking gas have been ensured to reach every eligible person. He said that 80 crore people in the country and 16 crore people in the state are getting the facility of free ration. Whereas in previous governments, the poor died of hunger. Due to the failure of previous governments, many Musahars died of hunger in Kushinagar. The Chief Minister said that during the Congress government, their own Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi had admitted that out of 100 rupees sent by the government, only 15 rupees reached the poor. Whereas the double engine government has ensured 100 per cent transparency in providing scheme benefits to the poor through DBT. 9 lakh youths received government jobs with transparency CM Yogi also mentioned the unprecedented development and employment in the state and Gorakhpur. He said that his government has provided government jobs to 9 lakh youths with complete transparency. There was no recommendation, no 'jugaad' (improvisation/fix), and no money involved. Whereas during the SP government, the maximum number of SDM recruitments were made in the name of a particular caste. He said that before 2017, the youth of Gorakhpur, UP were looked down upon. But today, when the youth here go out, they are respected by others. He said that the BJP government also respected the heritage. A grand temple of Lord Shri Ram was built in Ayodhya. Kashi Vishwanath and Vindhyachal Dham were beautified, and the Naimisharanya pilgrimage site was developed. Everyone invited to the inauguration ceremony of the six-lane flyover The Chief Minister, calling the six-lane flyover a major achievement in the development of Gorakhpur, invited everyone to its inauguration ceremony on Thursday. He said, "Come to this biggest flyover in Gorakhpur, take a selfie, and share it on social media." The conference commenced with floral tributes to the portraits of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee and Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya, followed by the collective singing of Vande Mataram. The booth presidents' conference was also addressed by MP Ravi Kishan Shukla, Mayor Dr. Manglesh Srivastava, MLA of Gorakhpur Rural Assembly constituency Vipin Singh, BJP State Vice President and MLC Dr. Dharmendra Singh, and Regional President Vinod Rai. Welcoming Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath at the conference, BJP Metropolitan President Ramesh Pratap Gupta presented the program's introduction. On this occasion, former Metropolitan President Rajesh Gupta, Metropolitan Vice President Shashikant Singh, General Secretaries Achyutanand Shahi, Omprakash Sharma, Minister Ajay Srivastava, Regional Media In-charge Dr. Baccha Pandey, Naveen, Metropolitan Media In-charge Chandan Arya, other office bearers of the Metropolitan unit, and presidents of 457 booths from Gorakhpur City Assembly constituency and 435 booths from Gorakhpur Rural Assembly constituency were present.

stories.title: Man kills his mother for ₹5 lakh aid:Sat beside body and shed crocodile tears, blamed leopard for attack
stories.summary: In Bijnor, what the family initially believed to be a leopard attack turned out to be murder. A 70-year-old woman was killed by her own younger son by strangulation. According to police, lured by the compensation of ₹5 lakh given in leopard attack cases, he brutally killed his mother. After the murder, he spread a rumour that a leopard had grabbed his mother by the neck and taken her away. The son told people: I tried to chase away the leopard with a sickle, but couldn't save my mother. The incident occurred on Monday evening around 5 PM. The woman had gone to the field to cut fodder for the cattle. During this time, her younger son raised an alarm and called the villagers, claiming that a leopard had grabbed his mother and taken her away. However, the post-mortem report that came on Tuesday revealed that the woman died due to strangulation. Following this, the police took the son into custody. During interrogation, the son confessed to committing the murder. The case in detail Veeravati Singh (70), a resident of Ajupura Jat village in the Heempur Deepa police station area of Bijnor, lived with her younger son Bahal Singh alias Mania. Veeravati has two sons. The elder son Rup Chand works in Dehradun, while her husband Munne Singh had passed away five years ago. On Monday evening around 5 PM, Veeravati had gone to the forest to collect fodder for the cattle. After some time, her younger son Bahal Singh raised an alarm and called the villagers, claiming that a leopard had dragged his mother away. Veeravati's body was found a short distance away in the field, after which everyone assumed it to be a death caused by a leopard attack. Upon receiving information, teams from the Forest Department, Police, and Revenue Department reached the spot. Angry villagers and family members protested against removing the body. After much persuasion, the police sent the body for post-mortem. Forest Department became suspicious of son's story, postmortem report revealed the truth Meanwhile, the Forest Department team that reached the spot raised questions about the leopard attack in the initial investigation itself. The officials found that there were neither teeth marks on the body nor any clear evidence of claw attacks. No part of the body was torn or eaten. There were only injury marks on the hands and face. The postmortem report that came on Tuesday further confirmed the Forest Department's suspicion. It also changed the direction of the police investigation. In fact, the report revealed that Veervati's death was caused by strangulation. Additionally, marks of several serious injuries were found on the body and ribs were also broken. According to the medical report, heavy pressure was applied to the stomach with a heavy object or knee, which caused internal injuries. After the postmortem report, the police took the younger son, Bahal Singh alias Mania, into custody and started interrogation. CO Chandpur Desh Deepak Singh said that during interrogation, Bahal Singh alias Mania confessed to the murder. The accused told the police that he used to quarrel with his mother every day. On the day of the incident, both had gone to the field to cut grass. There, an argument and exchange of abuses occurred over something. In anger, he strangled his mother and killed her. After this, so that no one would suspect and to get the financial assistance available in case of a leopard attack, he fabricated a false story of a leopard attack. FIR registered on elder son's complaint Police said- Based on the complaint of the deceased's elder son, a case has been registered under relevant sections at Heempur Deepa police station. The accused has been taken into custody and further legal action is being taken.

stories.title: Akhilesh's detention sparks SP protest in Agra:Police forcibly put workers into buses and take them into custody
stories.summary: Police detained Samajwadi Party workers near the Agra Fort on Wednesday. All these workers had gathered to protest against the action taken against party chief Akhilesh Yadav in Delhi a day earlier. Party officials and supporters, including women workers, participated in the demonstration. Even before the protest began, police detained about 50 SP members. All of them were sent to the police line. During this, SP workers raised slogans against the government. In view of the situation, a large number of police personnel were deployed at the Red Fort premises. Police took them into custody and forcibly put them on a bus In protest against the removal and detention of Opposition leaders during protests in Delhi, the Samajwadi Party and Congress are protesting nationwide. As part of this, Samajwadi Party workers gathered for a protest at the Red Fort complex in Agra on Wednesday. Upon receiving information about the protest, a large police contingent was deployed at the fort. As soon as SP workers arrived and started protesting, all of them were taken into custody. All the workers were forcibly put on a bus and sent to the police line. Metropolitan President appealed; women continued to chant slogans During the detention, the SP's metropolitan president appealed to the police with folded hands not to take the workers, but the police did not listen. During this, women workers fiercely chanted slogans against the government. They protested the police action. For some time, an atmosphere of chaos prevailed at the spot. Sloganeering in Police Line In Agra's Police Line, SP workers protested the detention of Akhilesh Yadav and the violence against children in the Delhi protest. They raised slogans against the government. Activists chanted the slogan, 'Where do we madmen go, let's go to jail, brother, let's go to jail.' Additionally, slogans like 'Whenever Yogi gets scared, he puts the police forward' were continuously being raised.

stories.title: Samajwadi Party to oppose Jauhar University demolition:15 MLAs to meet Rampur DM on July 23, MP Mohibullah absent from delegation
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) will send a delegation to Rampur on Thursday to oppose the proposed demolition of Jauhar University, the dream project of senior party leader Azam Khan. The delegation, led by Uttar Pradesh Leader of Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey, will meet the District Magistrate and submit a memorandum demanding that the demolition drive be halted. The team comprises 15 sitting MLAs, district presidents from Rampur, Moradabad, and Bareilly, along with several former legislators. Move follows Akhilesh Yadav’s directions In a letter issued by state president Shyam Lal Pal, the party said the delegation is being sent on the instructions of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. The SP argued that demolishing Jauhar University would violate the constitutional spirit and the right to education. According to the party, thousands of students from across the country study at the university at affordable fees. It said any damage to the institution would disproportionately affect students from poor, backward, and Dalit communities. Who is part of the delegation? Apart from Mata Prasad Pandey, the delegation includes MLAs Nasir Ahmed Khan, Kamal Akhtar, Shahid Manzoor, Ataur Rahman, Nawab Jan, Haji Nasir Qureshi, Faheem Irfan, Shahjil Islam Ansari, Rafiq Ansari, Atul Pradhan, Pankaj Malik, Pinki Singh, Iqbal Mahmood, and Ram Khiladi Singh Yadav. Several former MLAs and the district presidents of Rampur, Moradabad, and Bareilly are also part of the delegation. Rampur MP Mohibullah not included Rampur MP Mohibullah Nadvi has not been included in the delegation. The party said no Members of Parliament were included because the ongoing Parliament session would prevent them from participating. However, political observers have also linked his exclusion to the long-running differences between Azam Khan and Mohibullah Nadvi. Why Are Azam Khan and Mohibullah Nadvi at odds? 1. Disagreement over Lok Sabha ticket Ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Akhilesh Yadav met Azam Khan in Sitapur Jail. Azam reportedly wanted Akhilesh himself to contest from Rampur, but the party instead fielded Mohibullah Nadvi. The decision allegedly upset Azam Khan, who appealed to his supporters to boycott the election. 2. 'Reform home' remark After becoming an MP, Mohibullah Nadvi said in an interview that Azam Khan was "not in jail but in a reform home." Azam reportedly viewed the remark as a taunt and expressed displeasure over it on several occasions. 3. Refused to recognise him After his release from jail in September 2025, Azam Khan reportedly declined to acknowledge Mohibullah Nadvi when asked about him by journalists. Responding to the incident, Mohibullah said Azam Khan had grown old and may have had difficulty recognising him. He also expressed a desire to meet Azam, but the meeting never took place. 4. Asked not to accompany Akhilesh to Rampur Following Azam Khan's release from jail, Mohibullah Nadvi accompanied Akhilesh Yadav while travelling to meet him in Rampur. However, Azam Khan reportedly objected to his presence. As a result, Mohibullah stayed back in Bareilly, while Akhilesh Yadav continued alone to Rampur to meet the senior SP leader.

stories.title: Life sentence for man who raped minor daughter and daughter-in-law:Firozabad court orders 1 lakh fine in addition to sentence
stories.summary: A local court in Firozabad has sentenced a man to life imprisonment for raping his daughter-in-law and minor daughter. Additionally, a fine of ₹1 lakh has been imposed on him. The court directed that 80 per cent of the fine amount be given equally to both the victims. Fast Track Court Judge Devdatt announced the verdict on Tuesday evening, stating: The convict should be kept in prison until his last breath. If the victim's statement is solid, irrefutable and credible, then the accused can be convicted based on that alone. This case is from a neighbourhood in the Dakshin Thana area. In the year 2024, four members of a family suddenly left their home. After this, the head of the family filed a missing persons report with the police. When the police started investigating, the case turned out to be one of rape. Father was raping daughter and daughter-in-law On May 11, 2024, a 45-year-old man filed a complaint with the police that his wife, son, daughter-in-law and minor daughter had been missing from home since 9 May. The police registered a missing persons case and started the search. About a week later, the family was found in Aligarh. After this, the police interrogated everyone separately. During interrogation, the accused's wife revealed that her husband had been raping his minor daughter and daughter-in-law for the past six months. When she protested, he would threaten to kill her. When she tried to complain, he would lock the entire family inside the house. Fed up with the torture, the family had moved to Aligarh. Accused also took son's name Police recorded statements of both victims. During interrogation, the accused also took his son's name. After this, police also registered a case against the son. After completing the investigation, police filed a chargesheet against both. Son acquitted as charges not proven The case was heard in the court of Additional District and Sessions Judge (Fast Track Court-1) Devdatt. ADGC Manoj Kumar argued on behalf of the prosecution. The defense argued that the victims' medical examination was not conducted, therefore the charges are not proven. The court found the statements of both victims and other evidence credible, convicted the accused father and sentenced him to life imprisonment. The court ordered that he be kept in prison for the remainder of his natural life. However, the accused's son was acquitted due to lack of sufficient evidence.

stories.title: Congress workers march to CM residence with sticks in Lucknow:Protest over BJP demonstration at Congress office, 4-layer barricading deployed
stories.summary: The Congress has given a call to gherao (lay siege) the Chief Minister's residence in Lucknow on Wednesday. Following the BJP's call to gherao the Congress headquarters, Congress State President Ajay Rai called a meeting of workers. After the meeting, Congress workers will set out to gherao the CM residence. Barricades have been put up on all three routes to the Congress headquarters. Four-layer barricading has been done Four-layer barricading was set up near the Waqf Board on the route coming from the VVIP Guest House. Besides this, barricading was also done on the routes going towards the CM residence from Lal Batti Chowk and on the Udayganj route. On Tuesday, the top Congress leadership had gheraoed PM Modi's residence in Delhi. In response to this, BJP had called for gheraoing the Congress headquarters. 'Let's talk about students' rights' Congress leader Ahmed Raza arrived with a welcome poster. The post read 'Come, you are welcome, we will talk about students' rights'. Ahmed said that if the Bharatiya Janata Party comes to our headquarters, we will talk about students' rights and the Constitution. He said that this government does not want dialogue. “In Delhi, our leader Rahul Gandhi also went to PM Narendra Modi's residence so that we could talk about students' rights, we want to do this in Lucknow,” he said.
