stories.title: Ayodhya Ram Temple Trust assigns religious duties to 9 saints:Govind Dev Giri to head panel; CEO appointment still pending
stories.summary: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust took two major decisions at its meeting in Ayodhya on Wednesday. The first was the formation of a 9-member religious committee, comprising 5 saints from Ayodhya and four members from the temple trust. Trust Treasurer Swami Govind Dev Giri has been appointed chairman of the committee. The second decision was that the trust will appoint an official spokesperson. A secretary will also be appointed. The meeting was held from 3 pm to 5 pm at Shri Swami Mani Ram Das Chhawani under the chairmanship of Trust President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das Maharaj. No consensus was reached on the appointment of a permanent General Secretary or the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). Krishna Mohan will continue as the Acting General Secretary for now. The next trust meeting will be held on 2 September, when the names of the new General Secretary and CEO are expected to be announced. For the post of General Secretary, Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) General Secretary Bajrang Lal Bangda remains the leading contender. He also attended the meeting. This was the trust's second meeting since the temple donation theft case. At the meeting held on 6 July, the resignations of Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra were accepted, and retired IFS officer Krishna Mohan was appointed Acting General Secretary. Champat Rai and Anil Mishra had resigned on 26 June following the donation theft case. Key issues discussed by the Trust Anger over SBI's lapses: The trust had signed an agreement with the State Bank of India (SBI) to handle the counting of donations at the Ram Mandir. However, the individuals deployed by the bank for the counting process were later found to be among the accused in the alleged donation theft case. Saints expressed displeasure over SBI's role. The Finance Committee has been directed to review the entire matter and take necessary decisions. CEO decision deferred by 1-month: The selection process for the new Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to manage the temple's administration is in its final stages. Around 5,200 candidates from across the country have applied online for the post. The selection committee sought an additional 1-month to complete the process, and the trust approved the request. The trust also approved the appointment of a Secretary to meet administrative requirements. Trust to appoint an Official spokesperson: To maintain regular communication with the public and the media, the trust has decided to appoint an official spokesperson. The move aims to ensure timely and authentic dissemination of information related to the temple and the trust. No decline in devotee footfall: The trust said that despite various allegations and what it described as a misinformation campaign, the number of devotees visiting the Ram Mandir has not declined. It said this reflects the unwavering faith of millions of Ram devotees and expressed gratitude to the saint community, devotees, and the people of Ayodhya. Religious committee reconstituted The trust reconstituted its Religious Committee to maintain the traditional purity of worship rituals. Swami Govind Dev Giri will chair the committee. Its members will include Jagadguru Shankaracharya Swami Vasudevanand Saraswati, Swami Vishwaprasannatirtha, Swami Dinendra Das, Swami Kamalnayan Das, Mahant Rajkumar Das, Swami Ramanand Das, and Swami Mithilesh Nandini Sharan. The meeting also reviewed the process of filling vacant trustee positions. The trust expressed hope that the appointments would be completed within the next few weeks. Satisfaction over CCTV arrangements The trustees reviewed the CCTV surveillance system in the temple complex. The trust said security officials have access to all cameras, including those installed in the donation counting room. The trustees expressed satisfaction with the existing surveillance arrangements. SIT report yet to be received The trust said it has not yet received the final report of the SIT probing the alleged irregularities in the counting of donations. As a result, no detailed discussion on the matter could take place. However, the trustees took note of the ongoing proceedings in the Supreme Court and the court's directions.

stories.title: Tripura DGP's final journey in Baghpat:Mother caresses his face, wife hugs body, son devastated; cremation today
stories.summary: Tripura Director General of Police (DGP) Anurag Dhankar will be cremated in Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday. His funeral procession began at 9 am. Earlier, on Tuesday night, when his mortal remains reached his home in Baraut, his mother and wife broke down in grief. Repeating, "My child... my child...", his mother walked up to the body and gently caressed his face one last time. His wife, Kalpana, clung to the body and wept uncontrollably. Their son, Abhishek, tried to console her, but she embraced him and continued crying. Abhishek, who had flown in from Canada, was unable to hold back his emotions. Calling out, "Papa... Papa...", he hugged his father's body and burst into tears. DGP Anurag Dhankar's body was found at the Tripura Police Headquarters on 20 July. According to the preliminary police investigation, he died by suicide. After receiving the information, Anurag's younger brother rushed to Tripura. Baghpat Superintendent of Police Suraj Rai and Additional Superintendent of Police Praveen Kumar Chauhan also travelled to the state. Later, accompanied by senior Tripura Police officials, Dhankar's mortal remains were flown to Delhi by air ambulance and then taken by road to his hometown of Baraut in Baghpat.

stories.title: WATCH | Virat, Anushka walk barefoot to meet Premanand Maharaj:Couple visits Vrindavan to seek blessings 2 days before the Guru Purnima festival
stories.summary: Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma were spotted at Vrindavan this morning on 22 July to meet spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj. As per the visuals, the couple walked barefoot in mud to the premises surrounded by the disciples of Premanand Maharaj near the Kelly Kunj Ashram. The couple arrived early in the morning to meet the revered saint and receive his blessings. Notably, the visit from the couple holds significance since they have arrived at the Ashram two days before the Guru Purnima festival, an occasion on which people honour the spiritual and academic teachers. Wearing face masks, Virat and Anushka were spotted heading straight into the ashram. The couple stayed at the ashram for about an hour. When they came out, Virat had a sandalwood tilak on his forehead and prasad in his hand. They then visited the ashram of Maharaj Ji's guru, Govind Sharan Maharaj, located 150 metres away. They paid their respects and sought his blessings. Earlier, after winning the IPL, Virat and Anushka had visited Sant Premanand in Vrindavan on June 2. The two had stayed at the ashram for two hours. They came out with sandalwood and Tripund tilaks on their foreheads and a book in hand. Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma's 4th Vrindavan visit in 2026 Earlier on 2 June, the couple had visited the ashram after RCB's title win against Gujarat Titans in the IPL 2026 final match. Before that, on 20 April, coinciding with the occasion of Akshaya Tritiya, the couple had also visited Premanand Maharaj’s ashram, where they attended a satsang and sought his blessings. Their repeated visits reflect their continued spiritual association with the saint and his teachings. What is Guru Purnima festival? Guru Purnima is a revered festival celebrated on the full moon day (Purnima) of the Hindu lunar month of Ashadha (June–July) to honour spiritual and academic teachers. It is deeply rooted in Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions and takes place on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. Virat Kohli scored two half-centuries in the ODI series against England The star cricketer recently appeared in the ODI series against England that India lost 2-1. However, Kohli performed well with the bat, hitting two half-centuries in the three games. In the first game, he got out early for 5, but in the next two matches, Virat made a spectacular comeback. He scored 65(66) and 74(60) in the rest of the two one-day matches. When will Virat appear again in one-day? Virat's next one-day appearance will be against West Indies, which is set to be a home series starting in September. It is a three-match ODI series, which is part of the West Indies Tour of India, with the first match set to be played in Trivandrum Virat and Anushka’s eighth visit to Premanand Maharaj Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma recently paid their eighth visit to spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj. The couple first met him on 4 January 2023, and have continued to visit his ashram regularly. Over the past three years, this marks their eighth meeting and their fourth visit in 2026. Earlier in 2025, they visited thrice in a year.

stories.title: Children fall ill during monsoon in Gorakhpur:High-grade fever cases rise at district hospital; doctors advise extra caution
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, children's illnesses are rapidly increasing with the changing weather. Dr. Ganesh Gaurav, Child Specialist at the District Hospital, reported that since the beginning of July, the number of patients with cold-cough, stomach pain, vomiting-diarrhoea, and high-grade fever in the OPD has increased by up to 10 per cent. He says that bacteria spread rapidly during the rainy season, which easily increases the problem of infections. The months of June-July are called infected months. During these months, all kinds of germs breed and are spread in the environment. The doctor explained that the skin of children from zero to 15 years is quite sensitive. Additionally, their immunity power is also weaker compared to adults. In such a situation, protecting them from their diet and the effects of weather during the rainy season becomes extremely important. Otherwise, even a small negligence can become a cause of major trouble. 60 to 70 patients with seasonal problems reach the OPD daily Dr Gaurav said that for the past few days, around 100 to 120 patients have been coming to the Child OPD. Out of these, 60 to 70 are completely new cases with fever, cold-cough, runny nose, vomiting-diarrhoea, and stomach pain. The patients include children from 0 to 15 years of age. The most problems are being seen in children up to 5 years of age. He said that during the rainy season, infections increase due to bacteria remaining active and rapidly growing anywhere. Why is illness increasing Small children, while playing at home or outside, unknowingly touch infected objects. Then they eat food or other things with the same hand. Now the germs hidden in the hands easily enter the stomach, and diseases start from there. He informed that more patients with high-grade fever and vomiting-diarrhoea are reaching the OPD. In the changing weather, the bad effects of sometimes rain and then sunshine are affecting their health. In such a situation, care must be taken that children should not get wet in the rain at all. Parents should pay special attention The doctor says that in such weather, the responsibility of parents increases. It becomes necessary to take care of everything from eating and drinking to wearing and covering. Even a little negligence can cause big trouble. He said that by following the doctor's precautions when the illness increases and taking small precautions, any patient generally recovers completely within a week. But negligence worsens the situation, and many patients have to be admitted to the emergency. What are the symptoms? The doctor explained that children affected by illness due to weather changes commonly show symptoms such as loss of appetite, lethargy, increased irritability, feeling warm in the body or forehead, frequent vomiting and diarrhoea, nasal congestion, difficulty breathing, and reduced sleep. Take these precautions He also explained preventive measures...

stories.title: Online fraud busted:Gang member arrested for fake gold and counterfeit notes scam; cyber café operator's vigilance exposes racket
stories.summary: In the Bharatpur area of Baragaon police station jurisdiction in Varanasi district, police have busted a gang of cyber fraudsters who were duping people by showing them gold and bundles of notes online. Police arrested one member of the gang late on Tuesday evening, while his two accomplices fled from the scene. Police are engaged in searching for the absconding accused. The case came to light during investigation of a complaint registered on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. Ricky Roshan, a cyber cafe operator located in Bharatpur under Baragaon police station, had complained that on 17 July, a suspicious transaction of ₹15,300 had occurred in his bank account. After this, the bank had held and frozen his account. Investigation revealed that on 17 July, a youth had taken cash from the cafe operator by showing online payment through QR code. After that, this action was taken on Ricky's account. Meanwhile, on Tuesday evening around 6 pm, the same youth came to the cyber cafe again and started demanding cash after transferring money online. Upon seeing the young man, the cafe operator recognised him and raised an alarm. Hearing the commotion, people nearby caught him while two other youths who came with him fled from the scene. Sub-Inspector Khushboo Singh from Badagaon police station, who arrived upon receiving information, took the accused into custody along with the police team. During interrogation, the arrested was identified as 40-year-old Alok Singh, a resident of Gopalapur in the Rampur police station area of Jaunpur district. The accused revealed that he, along with his associates Hemant Singh and Satish Singh, would defraud people by showing them gold and bundles of notes online. It is being reported that on 17 July as well, the accused had defrauded a person of ₹85,000 rupees by showing gold online. They had come to the cyber cafe to convert the ₹85,000 rupees obtained from the fraud into cash through the cyber cafe. The police have registered a case against Alok Singh under Section 318(4) of the Indian Penal Code. Meanwhile, the police are continuously conducting raids in search of the absconding accused Hemant and Satish.

stories.title: Sharda rises above danger mark in UP:Floodwaters enter villages; tree crushes biker, rain alert for all 75 districts
stories.summary: Rivers across Uttar Pradesh are in spate after 10 days of continuous rainfall. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda River is flowing above the danger mark, with floodwaters entering villages along its banks. The situation has become so severe that crocodiles have been spotted roaming on roads and through fields. In Sonbhadra, the road leading to the district jail was washed away after the Ghaghra River swelled. In Varanasi, the Ganga's water level has risen by 10 feet in the past week, submerging around 50 small and large temples between Assi Ghat and Namo Ghat. In Prayagraj, the steps of several ghats have gone under water. Intermittent light rain has been falling in Noida since Wednesday morning. Cloudy skies have been reported in around 50 cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur and Agra, with occasional sunny spells. A rain alert has been issued for all 75 districts of the state today (Wednesday), with heavy rainfall forecast for 10 cities. Earlier, on Tuesday, rain was recorded in 74 districts, including Lucknow and Prayagraj. In Unnao, a tree fell on a moving motorcycle due to strong winds. The rider suffered a broken neck and died on the spot. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: “The low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal weakened, resulting in heavy rainfall across Uttar Pradesh over the past three to four days. The monsoon trough is now shifting southwards. As a result, some districts may receive heavy rain today, while southern parts of the state could witness very heavy rainfall. Rainfall is expected to ease from tomorrow. After a three-day break, the monsoon will regain momentum from 26 July, and another spell of rain will begin across the state.”

stories.title: Six freight train wagons derail:Accident on Ghaziabad–Delhi route; 16 train services cancelled, 53 affected
stories.summary: Six wagons of a coal-laden freight train derailed on the Ghaziabad–Delhi route in the early hours of Wednesday. The accident occurred at around 2.36 am. On receiving the information, the Railway Divisional Manager (DRM) and other officials rushed to the spot and took stock of the situation. Fortunately, no one was injured. Senior railway officials have ordered an inquiry into the incident. Following the derailment, several train routes have been diverted, with long-distance trains being operated via New Delhi, Sadar Bazar and Old Delhi–Shahdara. Several trains cancelled after derailment Wagons of a coal-laden freight train derailed in Ghaziabad's Sahibabad area, spilling coal onto the tracks and disrupting rail traffic. As a result, several trains had to be cancelled at short notice. The routes of 24 trains running via Delhi and New Delhi have been diverted. Sixteen passenger trains have been cancelled, while five passenger trains have been partially cancelled. The timings of eight trains from the Moradabad Division and the North Central Railway (NCR) heading to Anand Vihar have also been rescheduled. In all, 53 train services have been affected.

stories.title: Akhilesh and Rahul arrested in Delhi:Midnight unrest in Lucknow as police drag away SP, Congress workers; 4 hospitalised
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party and Congress held a vigorous protest in Lucknow on Tuesday evening. Protesters took to the streets against the arrest of Congress leader Rahul and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav in Delhi. A strong demonstration was held near the Legislative Assembly, Janbhawan and Hazratganj intersection from 7 PM till around midnight. SP workers arrived to protest in groups of 20. They had a sharp confrontation with the police. The police dragged them and took them to Eco Garden. Four workers were admitted to Civil Hospital due to injuries. Earlier in the evening, Congress state president Ajay Rai, who was coming to gherao Janbhawan, was detained by police about 10 kilometers away in the BKT area. He was taken to Eco Garden and released. One hour after Ajay Rai was taken into custody, Congress city committee president Shahzad Alam and other workers reached Janbhawan. SP State President taken into custody In protest against the detention of Samajwadi Party National President Akhilesh Yadav in Delhi, Party State President Shyam Lal Pal reached the Legislative Assembly. He started raising slogans against the government. Police took him into custody from there. During this time, a large number of SP workers reached Hazratganj intersection and started raising slogans. National spokesperson Juhi Singh, Ram Singh Rana along with a large number of workers were taken into custody from Atal Chowk. During this, there was considerable scuffling between workers and police in which the protesters' clothes were torn. SP workers also staged protest at Janbhawan Around 8:15 PM, a large number of Samajwadi Party workers reached Janbhawan. During this time, the police tried to detain them. After this, SP workers lay down on the ground. The police dragged Pooja Shukla, an SP leader, along with many workers and took them away in a bus. During the protest, there was considerable pushing and shoving. Several workers fell ill SP leader Atul stated that the police beat them brutally, following which Mahendra Yadav, Kanchi, Navneet and Shiva ji were seriously injured. Their treatment continued for a long time at the Civil Hospital. The condition of several party workers is serious, and they will need prolonged treatment. Accused of tearing clothes SP leader Pooja Shukla was dragged away by the police. During this, she said, “We had come to protest. The police misbehaved with the protesters. Clothes were torn. This has not happened for the first time. This always happens. The police are tearing our clothes and we are fighting for their children.” Pictures of Congress's protest 'Rahul Gandhi is struggling in Delhi and we are doing it in Lucknow' Congress workers demanded the resignation of PM Modi and Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Dr. Shahzad, who was protesting, said that this government is continuously violating the rights of students. “On Monday, students were brutally lathi-charged in Delhi and they were injured, this is extremely shameful,” he said. “Our leader Rahul Gandhi is fighting this battle in Delhi and all of us workers are struggling for students in Lucknow,” he said. 'The future of students is becoming dark' Ravi, who participated in the demonstration, said that he is a student. They have come to surround Jan Bhavan today on issues concerning students' interests. Dharmendra Pradhan should immediately resign on the issue of NEET examination and paper leak. “Due to the government's poor attitude, students' future is going into darkness. We do not want to see Dharmendra Pradhan as Education Minister under any circumstances. Our movement will not stop until he resigns,” he said. Congress leader Aryan Mishra and Congress members reached Janbhavan. While raising slogans against the BJP government and Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, they threw ink on PM Modi's picture. Arya said, “This government has pushed students' future into darkness. That's why we are throwing ink on the picture.” “Playing with students' future will not be tolerated. Our leader Rahul Gandhi is continuously struggling. We are also part of the fight with him,” he said.

stories.title: 6 major drawbacks for skipping marriage registration:Lakhs in benefits could be blocked; know the online application process for ₹10
stories.summary: Marriage registration is mandatory in Uttar Pradesh. This is necessary for people of all religions and castes. Without a marriage certificate, many tasks from banking to going abroad can be jeopardised. What is the online and offline process for marriage registration? Residence certificate necessary for arranged marriage Marriage registration in UP is done under the 'Women Welfare Department' and 'Stamp and Registration Department'. Marriage registration will only happen in that tehsil where the groom, bride or their parents have a permanent address. Registration cannot be done based on the place where the marriage took place. If the boy is from UP and the girl is from another state, then the boy's residence certificate will be required while getting the marriage registered. According to the 'Uttar Pradesh Marriage Registration Rules 2017', for marriage registration, the groom's age must be at least 21 years, and the bride's age must be at least 18 years. In love marriage, testimony of a priest or qazi will be required If the marriage has not taken place with the family's consent, then at the time of registration, the testimony of the pandit or qazi who performed the marriage, their affidavit, and the video recording of the marriage must be submitted on a pen drive. To prevent fraud, biometric verification of Aadhaar has also been made mandatory in marriage registration from April 1, 2026. Registration is also necessary for those having a court marriage Many times people get married in court or at Arya Samaj temple. Then wedding cards are not printed. In this situation, the bride and groom will have to get an affidavit made. This has to be uploaded in the document section at the time of registration. Without this, the form will not proceed further. When and how will the marriage certificate be received? After the online form is submitted, the Sub-Registrar office will verify it. After this, an appointment is given. On the scheduled date, the bride-groom and witnesses have to appear with their documents. Here, their signatures and thumb impressions are taken. At the time of biometric at the Tehsil, the same 2 witnesses whose documents were uploaded online will have to go. Fifteen to 30 days after this process, you can download the certificate by visiting igrsup.gov.in and entering your application number and password. This has a barcode and digital signature, which is 100 per cent valid for all government and legal work. Also know the process to correct mistakes in marriage certificate If after downloading the certificate it is found that there is a spelling mistake in the name or date of birth, it cannot be corrected online. For this, one has to go back to the same sub-registrar office and submit an application. 6 major disadvantages of not getting registration done 1. Lakhs of funds can get stuck: If something unfortunate happens to someone's husband or wife, then the marriage certificate is the biggest legal proof for claiming the PF money deposited in the partner's name, gratuity or life insurance claim. Without this, companies and banks can refuse to give the claim, or the process can take years. 2. Difficulty in becoming nominee in bank accounts and property: Banks demand a marriage certificate to make a husband or wife a nominee in property or a bank account. Without this, getting property transferred becomes difficult. 3. Risk of passport and visa rejection: If you want to travel abroad after marriage or settle overseas, getting a 'spouse visa' is impossible without a marriage certificate. It is also necessary to add your partner's name to your passport. 4. Difficulty in joint home loans and banking: If a couple wants to apply for a joint home loan, car loan, or open a joint bank account, banks ask for the marriage certificate as a primary document. 5. Unable to avail government schemes: To avail benefits of UP's mass marriage scheme or housing schemes, submitting a marriage certificate is mandatory. 6. Divorce, alimony and child custody: If any legal dispute arises in marital life in the future, the first thing to prove in court is that the marriage is legally valid. Having a marriage certificate makes this process easier.

stories.title: Damini's love story began with love at first sight:Allegedly had husband killed by snakebite for affair with driver
stories.summary: In Meerut, Damini, who had her husband bitten by a snake, once loved him immensely. Seven years ago, both of them went against their families' wishes and got married. They also had a son. Everything was going well. Then what happened that Damini had to murder Atul? A new angle has emerged from police conversations with Damini and Atul's family members and friends. This story of love, marriage and then murder begins about eight years ago in 2018. Damini's house was 3 km away from Atul's house in Hastinapur. Damini's father had passed away. Her mother and younger brother lived at home. There was also a cosmetics shop at home, which Damini herself ran. One day Atul came to her shop to buy face wash. He fell in love with Damini at first sight. Ten days later, Atul went to the shop again. He told Damini, “We belong to the same community; we are both Gurjars.” Damini replied, “Yes, I am a teacher. I work at Swami Kalyandev School. I spend some time here at the shop.” Atul said, “I also studied at the same school. I left school in 2012-13, then went to Mumbai for a job in Merchant Navy. My elder brother is also in the same field. With his help, I stayed in Merchant Navy in Mumbai. I came back here in 2015. At home, there are Papa-Mummy, my elder brother, my sister-in-law, and their three children. My second brother is also in the Navy. He has a wife, a son, and a daughter. I am still single.” “I work a computer job at a company here. I also look after Vidya Prakashan's work and also do politics. I am a co-coordinator in ABVP. I have also held a position at the Mandal level. I have also held a position in the Yuva Morcha,” Atul said. Damini replied, “You do so much work and are also a leader.” 'Atul ki Gujari' tattoo While talking and meeting each other, both became friends. One day, Atul proposed to Damini. After this, both talked to their families about marriage, but the families did not agree. However, when both insisted, the families finally agreed. They got married in Hastinapur in 2019. Atul had a private job; Damini managed the household. A year after marriage, their son Manik was born. Both also created Instagram accounts in each other's names. During this time, both Atul and Damini went to visit Meerut. To express her love, Damini got a tattoo on her left hand. She had written 'Atul ki Gurjari'. Seeing his name on Damini's hand, Atul hugged her. Atul became the school director and Damini the principal After this, both of them opened a kids' school in a rented building in Hastinapur. Damini had experience working in a school. Therefore, Atul himself took on the responsibility of director and made Damini the principal. Damini used to teach children, while Atul looked after the school's management. Later, both started a new school in another rented building, which began running well. The school had around 150 children. A year ago, Tushar entered Damini's married life It was in this school that about a year ago, in March 2025, van driver Tushar made his entry. Along with dropping children, Tushar also started picking up and dropping Damini from school to home. During this time, closeness grew between the two. Gradually, they fell in love. Meanwhile, Damini told Tushar about her husband's medical insurance of ₹20 lakh. Both thought that Damini works all day at school, and Atul handles the management. “Why not remove him from the way, and we become one. We'll take the insurance money and get married and live life happily,” this was the plan of Damini and Tushar. Atul became suspicious Seeing the actions of Damini and Tushar going to and from school together, and also going to other places together during the day, Atul became suspicious. He asked Damini, “What is going on with Tushar? Stop this right here; this is not right.” Damini replied, “There is nothing like that.” After this, Atul suspected that Damini was feeding him sleeping pills in his food. He went home and told his mother about this. He said to his mother, “Damini wants to kill me.” Mother said, “Son, you had a love marriage. Now what can I tell you? You speak to Damini.” Atul hit by an Ertiga car Tushar and Damini started planning Atul's murder. Twenty days before the murder, Atul was going somewhere on his bike when an Ertiga car hit him on the way. Atul was wearing a helmet, so he survived. Atul came home and told Damini about this incident. On this, Damini said, “When you couldn't even identify the car, what's the point of filing a complaint? It must have been some mishap that got averted. That day, Atul considered Damini's words correct and ignored the incident.” Tushar and Damini were unhappy in their marriages One day Damini said to Tushar, “How long will this go on? I am tired. Something decisive should happen in this relationship. I want to live with you.” Tushar said, “I also want to leave my wife and live with you. You are unhappy with your love marriage, and I am with my arranged marriage. We will both together build a new world.” Planned together to kill Atul Damini told Tushar, “I have a plan. If I divorce Atul, all his property will not be in my name. Why not murder him? After Atul's murder, you divorce your wife. Atul has insurance of ₹20 lakhs. We will take that money too. After that, we will get married.” “I will keep the son with me because only if he stays with me will we get the 35 bigha land in Atul's name at the in-laws' place. We will also continue running the school,” she said. After this, both of them started thinking about how to remove Atul from the way. Read in the second part how Damini and Atul together conspired to commit murder…

stories.title: Ghaziabad double murder - Sister demands death penalty for brothers:Says, 'Kill them the way they killed our parents'
stories.summary: 'It would have been better if we had no brothers at all than brothers like these. Never thought that those who used to fight among themselves would one day take the lives of mother and father. Just as they killed mom and dad, both brothers should also be killed.' This was said by the sisters of the two men who murdered their own parents on the night of 20 July (Monday) in Ghaziabad. Neighbours say that both sons together killed their own parents. To know what the two daughters are going through after the murder of their parents, a Dainik Bhaskar team reached Bhimnagar. This area is adjacent to the Delhi-Meerut Expressway. A crowd of people had gathered outside the two-story house. Policemen were standing near the gate. Sounds of women crying were coming from inside the house. When we went inside, family members' statements were being recorded in one room in the presence of police officers. Both daughters Deepika and Jyoti sitting in a corner of the room kept crying. Birthday celebration turned into mourning Ganga Saran was originally from Sathla village in Bulandshahr. However, he had been living in Bhimnagar for many years. Both his sons, Deepak (alias Vicky) and Lalit, got married during the lockdown period. However, both sons' wives had left them. Family members said both were addicted to alcohol and occasionally drove taxis. Both daughters Deepika and Jyoti are also married. On 20 July, it was the birthday of the younger son Lalit. In the evening, mother Vimlesh organised a kirtan with neighbourhood women. She made kheer-puri for her son. However, as night fell, a drinking party started at home. Family members say that around 9 PM, the parents objected to the drinking. After this, a quarrel started. Late at night, both sons attacked their father. After that, they didn't spare their mother Vimlesh either, who came to intervene. They beat both of them mercilessly, attacked them with a hammer. Then they strangled them to death. Daughter says accused brothers should be punished The elder daughter Deepika said tearfully, “Both brothers took the lives of mom and dad due to property and alcohol addiction. Both of them used to drink and create fights at home earlier too. About a year ago, they stole and sold mother's 10 tola jewellery.” “Mom and dad overlooked their mistakes every time. They tried to handle them, but in the end, those very sons killed them so mercilessly. Never even dreamed that our own brothers would become the murderers of our parents,” she said. Younger daughter Jyoti said, “Both brothers often used to drink and beat mom and dad. That's why we sisters also started coming home less. Dad educated both brothers, built a house. Got us sisters married, but both brothers never reformed. Got a call at night that the brothers had killed mom and dad.” "At first, I couldn't believe it when I heard. It felt like someone was joking. But when I reached home and saw the condition of Mom and Dad, the ground slipped from under my feet. The house where Mom and Dad's voices always echoed, there was only screaming and mourning. Even today I can't believe that the brothers whom Mom and Dad raised with so much care, they took our parents lives. Uncle says no relation with such nephews Lekhraj, the brother-in-law of Ganga Saran, came from Aligarh after hearing the news of his brother-in-law's murder. He couldn't control himself after seeing the bodies of his sister and brother-in-law. He said, “The attack on the head and face was so brutal that it was unbearable to look at. We have no relation with those who killed their own parents. They should get the death penalty or life imprisonment.” Both daughters-in-law were living separately Deepak's marriage took place on 16 May 2020, with Monica, a resident of Bulandshahr. Relatives said that Deepak used to beat his wife as well while under the influence of alcohol. He has 2 sons. Troubled by domestic quarrels and harassment, Monica had gone to her maternal home with both her sons about a year ago and has been living there since then. Younger son Lalit had a love marriage with Soni, a resident of Vijaynagar in Ghaziabad, on 25 May 2020. Lalit has no children. There used to be frequent quarrels between Lalit and his wife. Due to continuous fights, Soni had also gone to her maternal home about 40 days ago. Even after the incident of murder of her in-laws, she did not come to her in-laws' house. Additional Police Commissioner (Law and Order) said- Both the accused were caught from their home itself. During interrogation, both have confessed to murdering their parents. An FIR has been registered and both have been arrested.

stories.title: Stones pelted at police after youth's murder in Saharanpur:Cops lathicharge, beat women; protesters block highway
stories.summary: Public anger erupted in Deoband, Saharanpur, on Tuesday evening following the murder of a 17-year-old boy. Family members, joined by hundreds of local residents, staged a protest by placing the teenager's body on the highway, bringing traffic to a standstill. The protesters demanded the immediate arrest of all the accused and strict action against them. A large crowd gathered at the site within a short time. Police initially attempted to persuade the protesters to disperse. When they refused, officers tried to remove them, leading to scuffles and pushing involving women. The crowd then allegedly pelted stones at the police, escalating the situation. Police responded with a baton charge to disperse the protesters and clear the highway. The ensuing chaos triggered a stampede in which four people were injured. Senior police and administrative officials later reached the scene with additional police personnel. They spoke to the victim's family, briefed them on the action taken so far, and assured them that the absconding accused would be arrested soon. Police personnel remain deployed across the area. See 4 pictures- Protest on Highway Clash with Police Women beaten by police Bricks and stones removed from highway Teen missing for two days; Body found in field at midnight Jaiprakash, a confectioner, lives in Shikshak Nagar Colony under the Deoband Kotwali police station area. His 17-year-old son, Shiva, went missing at around 10 pm on Sunday. The father lodged a missing person's report with the police. According to him, Shiva's friends, Tejas, Aditya and Suryansh, had called him out of the house that night. However, Shiva never returned home. On Monday evening, Jaiprakash found Shiva's friend Tejas in the neighbourhood. When questioned about Shiva's whereabouts, Tejas allegedly gave evasive answers. Growing suspicious, family members assaulted him before taking him to the police. During police questioning, Tejas allegedly confessed to the murder. He reportedly told police, “I have murdered Shiva. His body is lying in the field.” Police reached the field at around 12.30 am on Monday night, where they recovered Shiva's body. Injury marks were found on the body. The body was sent for post-mortem examination, while a forensic team collected evidence from the crime scene. After the post-mortem, the body was handed over to the family at around 6 pm on Tuesday. Soon afterwards, relatives and villagers took the body to the highway and began protesting. Highway blocked with body; Baton charge follows The family placed Shiva's body in the middle of the highway and raised slogans against the accused. Within minutes, long queues of vehicles formed on both sides of the road. Women and elderly residents also joined the protest. Police tried to persuade the demonstrators to clear the road, but they refused. Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Abhinandan also reached the spot and assured the family that strict action would be taken against the accused and that every possible assistance would be provided. Despite these assurances, the protest continued. When police attempted to clear the blockade, a confrontation broke out. Officers then carried out a baton charge, after which some protesters allegedly threw stones at the police. The unrest continued for nearly three hours. Additional police personnel were deployed, and after considerable effort, the highway was cleared and traffic resumed. Police: Accused lured Shiva to the field before killing him SSP Abhinandan said the investigation revealed that Shiva and the accused had previously been friends. However, an old dispute had led to hostility between them. According to the police, the accused allegedly lured Shiva to a field on a pretext, murdered him there, and abandoned the body. Shiva worked as a labourer and was the only brother among three sisters. Based on the complaint lodged by his father, police have registered a murder case against three youths. One accused, Tejas, has been arrested, while three special police teams are conducting raids to trace the two absconding suspects. Police investigating violence during protest SSP Abhinandan said police are also investigating the incidents of baton charging and stone-pelting that occurred during the protest. He said those responsible for disrupting law and order are being identified, and appropriate action will be taken against them.

stories.title: Akhilesh alleges electric shocks, tear gas used on students:SP chief says, 'Jauhar University next for demolition; Ikra chants 'shame, shame'
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday criticised the government during the Lok Sabha debate on the Paper Leak Amendment Bill, accusing it of making promises without delivering results. He said, 'The government offers slogans, not commitments. Those who could not even protect the offerings made to the deity, how will they stop paper leaks? They have committed a grave sin. Lord Ram will not forgive them.' 'What happened in Delhi resembled the emergency' Referring to recent events in Delhi, Akhilesh Yadav said- We recently witnessed scenes in Delhi that reminded us of the Emergency. Tear gas shells were fired. This time, electric shocks were also used. It was an attack similar to the Emergency. Change came after the Emergency, and we are confident that change will come this time as well. Remarks on Azam Khan's Jauhar University Commenting on the demolition action involving Azam Khan's Jauhar University, Akhilesh Yadav said- The BJP has not established a single government university. But if someone has built a private university, they are preparing to demolish it with hammers. Akhilesh Yadav spoke in the Lok Sabha for nearly 25 minutes. Whenever he criticised the government, Samajwadi Party MPs, including Dimple Yadav and Iqra Hasan, were seen raising slogans of 'Shame, Shame.' 'Hindu-Muslim politics will no longer work' Speaking to reporters outside Parliament, Congress MP Imran Masood said the country's political atmosphere had changed. Hindu-Muslim politics will no longer work. You cannot influence Gen Z in the name of religion. This is a new generation with innovative thinking. Everyone has seen the kind of innovation they demonstrated at Jantar Mantar. Pramod Tiwari questions action against students Congress MP Pramod Tiwari said the party would hold the government accountable for the use of force against students. He said, "The Congress Party will seek accountability for every baton used against young students. We will ask why the batons had nails attached to them. We will also ask whether the government now intends to use AK-47 rifles against the country's youth. The action taken against young women cannot be justified by any civilised government. The Home Minister must be prepared to answer these questions."

stories.title: CM Yogi signals cashless healthcare for lawyers:Warns social media will be used for conspiracies against India, stay alert
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government may introduce a cashless healthcare scheme for lawyers. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath hinted at the proposal on Tuesday while addressing advocates. He told lawyers, "Discuss the proposal with your Bar Association and reach a consensus. We are ready to provide cashless healthcare and other facilities." Yogi was speaking at around 2 pm during the oath-taking ceremony of the newly elected executive committee of the Civil Court Bar Association in Gorakhpur. According to the Ministry of Law and Justice, Uttar Pradesh has nearly 500,000 registered lawyers. If the proposal is implemented, they will be eligible for cashless medical treatment. 4 key remarks by CM Yogi 'We Increased the Advocates' Welfare Fund' Yogi said the financial assistance available under the Advocates' Welfare Fund had been significantly enhanced. "Earlier, lawyers received ₹1.5 lakh under the Advocates' Welfare Fund. We increased it to ₹5 lakh. We have also created a corpus fund of ₹500 crore, and the scheme will run on the interest generated from that fund." He added that financial assistance worth ₹200 crore had already been provided to the families of around 4,000 advocates. “Earlier, assistance was available only until the advocate reached the age of 60. Now, the family remains eligible even if the advocate is 70 years old. We have also provided funds for the construction of advocates' buildings and chambers.” 'Social media will be used for conspiracies' The Chief Minister said social media would increasingly be used to create divisions and weaken the country. "There will be conspiracies against India through social media. Attempts will be made to create disputes based on region and language, which will weaken the country. Some will question the judiciary, others the legislature, and others the executive. Therefore, the responsibility of the legal fraternity will become even greater." 'People once looked at UP with suspicion' Yogi said Uttar Pradesh's image had changed significantly since 2017. "Today, everyone speaks positively about Uttar Pradesh. Before 2017, people looked at those from UP with suspicion. They would keep their distance. Today, wherever you go in the country, if you say you are from Uttar Pradesh, people will come forward to greet you warmly. That transformation has taken place." 'Where illegal firearms were once made, BrahMos missiles are now being produced' The Chief Minister said the state's industrial landscape had undergone a major transformation. "Places where illegal country-made pistols and bombs were once manufactured are now producing BrahMos missiles. A state that once struggled with unemployment and migration now has one of the lowest unemployment rates in the country." He said this change had been achieved by creating new avenues of employment and developing modern infrastructure.

stories.title: New hope in UP's 69,000 teacher recruitment case:SC says we may settle dispute under Article 142 if all parties agree
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday heard the high-profile 69,000 teacher recruitment case from Uttar Pradesh. A division bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu heard arguments from all parties on the adjustment plan submitted by the Uttar Pradesh government. During the hearing, the bench suggested a one-time settlement under Article 142 of the Constitution, subject to the consent of all parties. The Court has directed all sides to reach a consensus and submit their consent through affidavits by Friday. Next hearing on 4 August to be crucial If all parties agree, the Supreme Court may resolve the matter under Article 142 at the next hearing scheduled for 4 August 2026. If no consensus is reached, the Court will continue hearing the case on the basis of the Lucknow Bench's judgment. It will also allow five lawyers from each side to present detailed arguments. What happened in the Supreme Court? The hearing began at around 11 am in Courtroom No. 10. The Court granted parties that had not yet filed their affidavits time until Wednesday to do so. Counsel representing the unreserved category argued that their clients had been serving as teachers for the past six years. He submitted that if they were suddenly dismissed, they would be left without employment. He argued that since the appointments had been made by the government, the teachers should not suffer because of errors in implementing reservation. Representing the reserved category candidates, senior advocate Manish Goswami and other counsel argued that the prescribed 27% reservation for OBCs and 21% reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs) must be implemented correctly. They urged the Court to uphold the Lucknow Bench's ruling, cancel the earlier selection list, issue appointments based on the revised merit list, and remove those who had secured appointments incorrectly. Court suggests consent-based resolution After hearing both sides, the bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu proposed a consent-based solution. The Court directed all parties to file their consent through affidavits by Friday. Advocate Mandeep Kalra has been appointed as the nodal officer to coordinate the process. Reserved category candidates ready to consent if appointed Reserved category candidate Amarendra Patel said that if the government proceeds with appointments to a total of 8,270 posts, including 3,324 OBC vacancies and 4,946 other vacant posts, eligible candidates are prepared to give their consent. Sushil Kashyap, State President of the Pichda-Dalit Sanyukt Morcha, and the organisation's spokesperson Rajesh Chaudhary also said they were willing to consent if all petitioners from both the Single Bench and Division Bench cases of the High Court receive the benefits sought in their petitions. Government's proposal In its affidavit, the Uttar Pradesh government stated that it was prepared to recruit candidates against 8,270 additional posts based on a revised cut-off. According to the government, this would also protect the jobs of approximately 67,000 teachers who are already in service. What is Article 142? Article 142 of the Constitution of India grants the Supreme Court extraordinary powers to ensure ‘complete justice’ in any matter before it. Clause (1): The Supreme Court may pass any decree or order necessary to ensure complete justice in a case. Such an order is enforceable throughout India. Clause (2): The Court has the authority to secure the attendance of individuals, summon documents, and take necessary action in matters relating to contempt of court. How could Article 142 affect the case? When existing legal provisions do not provide an effective solution to a dispute, the Supreme Court can invoke Article 142 to deliver complete justice through a special order. The 69,000 teacher recruitment case involves multiple legal and administrative complexities. In this context, the Court has proposed resolving the matter through a consent-based settlement under Article 142. A significant consequence of such an order would be that it would not serve as a legal precedent, and the matter could not be challenged again in court on the same grounds.

stories.title: Former minister falls from 7th floor of MLA residence, dies:Police probe suicide or accident; was BJP OBC cell leader
stories.summary: Former minister Nanakdin Bhurji died after falling from the seventh floor of the new MLA residence in Lucknow. The flat (No. 703) from which he fell has been allotted to SBSP MLA Hansu Ram. Hansu Ram represents the Belthara Road (Reserved) Assembly constituency in Ballia. Bhurji had gone to meet the MLA on Tuesday morning. He later fell under suspicious circumstances and died. Police reached the scene after receiving information about the incident. Investigators are examining whether Bhurji died by suicide or whether it was an accident. Police said it would be premature to draw any conclusions. The investigation is based on evidence collected from the scene, CCTV footage and statements from eyewitnesses. The 56-year-old Bhurji was the BJP OBC Morcha's State General Secretary. He had also founded an organisation called the Hindustan Pichhda Morcha, where he served as National President. The incident took place at around 2 pm on Tuesday within the Hazratganj police station area. 'We were at the party office' BJP OBC Morcha State President Prakash Pal said, "We were at the BJP state office when we received information that former minister Nanakdin Bhurji had fallen from the seventh floor of the new MLA residence. We immediately left for the spot, but on the way we were informed that he had been taken to the Civil Hospital." He said doctors declared Bhurji dead upon their arrival at the hospital. Prakash Pal added that it was still unclear how Bhurji fell from the seventh floor or under what circumstances the incident occurred. He said Bhurji was a resident of Madeyganj (Khadra) in Lucknow. He is survived by his wife Manju Devi, two sons, Uttam Gupta and Purushottam Gupta, and a daughter, Priyanka Gupta. None of the three children are married. Police say Bhurji had been suffering from depression According to Lucknow Police, the administrative officer of the new Darulshafa MLA residence informed the local police outpost on 28 July that Bhurji had fallen from the building. Police officers reached the spot and shifted the injured Bhurji to the Civil Hospital, where doctors declared him dead after examination. During the investigation, police said they learnt that Bhurji had been suffering from depression for a considerable period. He was often seen walking around the new MLA residence complex. His body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. Long association with the BJP Nanakdin Bhurji was born on 1 July 1970. After completing his Intermediate education on 11 September 1988, he pursued higher studies at the University of Lucknow. He remained an active face of the BJP's OBC politics for many years and held several important positions within both the party organisation and the government. From LDA member to minister of state rank In 2004, Bhurji was nominated as a member of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA). During the BSP government in December 2006, he was appointed Minister of State (equivalent rank) and also served as an adviser to the Backward Class Welfare Department. In a Facebook post, Bhurji had written, “My family's financial condition was extremely difficult. From 1988 to 2025, I devoted my entire life to the welfare of the Bhurji community.” He added that former Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav had helped him secure a clerical position in the Property Department of the Uttar Pradesh Secretariat. He further wrote that from 1990 onwards he became actively associated with various organisations representing the Bhurji community. In 2004, he was appointed a member of the Lucknow Development Authority, and in December 2006 he was nominated as Minister of State in the Backward Class Welfare Department. Relative rejects police claim of depression Bhurji's elder brother-in-law, Ramesh Chandra Gupta, a resident of Bada Chandganj in Aliganj, disputed the police's claim that Bhurji was suffering from depression. He said Bhurji left home at around 12 noon on Tuesday. As part of his daily routine, he regularly visited Darulshafa and the BJP office, where arrangements had been made for him to sit. According to Gupta, Bhurji had been visiting the BJP office regularly for nearly 25 years and was not suffering from depression.

stories.title: Fresh hope in UP teacher recruitment case:Supreme Court says verdict under Article 142 possible if all parties agree
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday held an important hearing in the much-discussed Uttar Pradesh 69,000-teacher recruitment case. A two-judge bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu heard the adjustment plan presented by the state government and the arguments of all parties. During the hearing, the court clearly stated that if all parties reach a mutual agreement on the government’s proposal, a verdict could be delivered next Tuesday under Article 142 of the Constitution. Next hearing on 4 August The court has given all parties time until next Tuesday to reach a consensus and inform the court about it. The next hearing in the case will now take place on 4 August. It is believed that if all sides agree, a solution could emerge in the long-pending dispute. What did the court say? During the hearing, the Supreme Court said that if all concerned parties agree to the government’s adjustment plan, the court can use its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution. In such a situation, the final order may also be passed next Tuesday. Earlier on Monday, all parties, including the government, had submitted their respective responses through affidavits. What proposal did the government submit in its affidavit? Through its affidavit filed before the court, the government stated that it was ready to make additional appointments to 8,270 posts as per the new cut-off list. This would ensure that the jobs of the 67,868 candidates already working remain protected, while new candidates who were denied appointments due to the reservation process could also be accommodated. What is Article 142? Article 142 of the Indian Constitution gives the Supreme Court special and wide-ranging powers to ensure "complete justice". It is considered a provision granting extraordinary powers to the court. Clause (1): The Supreme Court can pass any order or decree necessary to ensure complete justice in any matter, and such orders are enforceable throughout India. Clause (2): It gives the court powers to ensure the presence of individuals, summon documents, and take necessary action in matters related to contempt of court. When normal legal provisions are unable to provide an effective solution to a dispute, the Supreme Court can issue special orders under Article 142 to ensure justice. The Uttar Pradesh 69,000 teacher recruitment process involves several such complexities, and the court may need to use this constitutional provision to find a way forward.

stories.title: 15 IPS officers transferred in UP:Prayagraj Police Commissioner replaced after student protests
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government transferred 15 IPS officers on Tuesday afternoon. The reshuffle includes two Director General (DG)-rank officers, six Additional Director General (ADG)-rank officers, five Inspector General (IG)-rank officers, and two Superintendent of Police (SP)-rank officers. The Police Commissioners of Lucknow and Prayagraj have been replaced. Lucknow Police Commissioner Amrendra Sengar has been appointed DG (Intelligence). He has been replaced by ADG (Security) Tarun Gaba as the new Police Commissioner of Lucknow. ADG of Varanasi Zone Piyush Mordia has been appointed the new Police Commissioner of Prayagraj. Prayagraj Police Commissioner Jogendra Kumar has been posted as IG of the Police Training School (PTS), Moradabad. According to sources, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was displeased following the student protests and unrest in Prayagraj on 25 July over the NEET paper leak. Home Department Secretary and IPS officer Mohit Gupta has been transferred as IG, Anti-Corruption Organisation. Gupta was in the spotlight during the Prayagraj Maha Kumbh over the controversy surrounding Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's royal bathing procession, when questions were raised about his role in handling the matter. Who Is Lucknow's New Police Commissioner Tarun Gaba? Tarun Gaba, a 2001-batch IPS officer, is originally from Chandigarh. He spent the early part of his career on central deputation before returning to the Uttar Pradesh cadre in 2020. Gaba also served in the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), where he established a strong reputation. He was entrusted with leading the investigation related to IPS officer Rakesh Asthana. He has previously served as IG (Vigilance). After returning from central deputation, he was appointed to that post. In 2020, amid rising crime in Uttar Pradesh, the Yogi government replaced then Home Secretary S.K. Bhagat with Tarun Gaba. He has also previously served as the Police Commissioner of Prayagraj. See the complete list- Mutha Ashok Jain recently promoted to ADG, set to retire next month Mutha Ashok Jain, a 1995-batch IPS officer, was recently promoted from ADG to the rank of Director General. He has now been appointed DG of Fire Services. Jain is due to retire on the 31st of next month. Originally from Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, he holds an MBA from IIM Lucknow. During his career, he has served as SP, SSP and Police Commissioner in districts including Prayagraj, Kanpur, Etawah and Varanasi. While on central deputation, he served as Deputy Director General (DDG) of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). During his tenure, he supervised major investigations including the drugs angle in the Sushant Singh Rajput case and the Mumbai cruise drugs case. Why were these officers removed? Bhagwan Swaroop Srivastava: Bhagwan Swaroop Srivastava, who had been serving as ADG (Intelligence) for a long period, has been transferred as ADG (Technical Services). According to sources, the government believed intelligence inputs during the recent student protests were inadequate, leading to his removal. Amrendra Kumar Sengar: A 1995-batch IPS officer, Sengar became Lucknow Police Commissioner after Sujit Pandey went on central deputation. He has now been shifted from the Lucknow Police Commissionerate and appointed DG (Intelligence). He has also been given additional charge of the Security Headquarters. Why These Officers Have Been Given New Responsibilities Naveen Arora: A 1997-batch IPS officer, Naveen Arora has been appointed ADG of Varanasi Zone. He had been serving as ADG (Technical Services) for a considerable period and is regarded as an efficient and proactive officer. He has also previously served as Joint Police Commissioner in Lucknow. Piyush Mordia: A 1998-batch IPS officer, Piyush Mordia has been appointed Police Commissioner of Prayagraj. He is considered an efficient and dependable officer, which is why the government has entrusted him with the important Prayagraj Police Commissionerate. Ram Kumar: A 1995-batch IPS officer, Ram Kumar had been serving as ADG (Logistics). Regarded as a trusted officer, he has now been appointed ADG of Gorakhpur Zone. Dharmveer: After serving in the Home Guards department for the past six years, Dharmveer has now been appointed IG of the Eastern Zone of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) in Prayagraj. The post had remained vacant for a long time.

stories.title: Woman conspires with brother-in-law to kill husband:Agra man murdered three months after wedding following objection to illicit affair
stories.summary: Police uncovered the murder of a young man in Agra within 24 hours. The young man had been married three months ago. The young man's body was found in the bushes. There were injury marks on the young man's head. The young man was murdered by his wife and younger brother together. After that, they threw the body in the bushes. The accused stated he was becoming an obstacle due to their illicit relationship. After this, both of us planned the murder. Following clues from CCTV footage, the police uncovered the murder incident and arrested the accused brother and the wife accused of conspiring the murder. The incident took place in Sultanpura Chhoti Basti. Now read the full story Amit Kumar (22), a resident of Sultanpura Chhoti Basti Sadar, worked as a waiter at Pandit Ji Dhaba located in Cantt. On Wednesday morning at seven o'clock, he left home saying he was going to the dhaba. An hour later, local residents saw Amit's body lying in the bushes a hundred meters from his home. The young man had been murdered by crushing his head and face with a stone. The deceased's younger brother, Bholu, had accused a young man working at the dhaba of the murder. According to people present at the scene, the deceased's face was badly disfigured. Deep injury marks were found on the face and head. It is suspected that the attackers killed him by striking him multiple times with a heavy stone or a solid object. Bloodstains were also found around the body, suggesting that the murder took place at the scene. The police uncovered the sensational murder case within 24 hours. Murder in Illicit Relationship DCP City Syed Ali Abbas stated, “When the police scanned the CCTV cameras, Amit's younger brother Bholu was seen following him. The place where Amit was murdered is used by local residents for defecation.” Amit was sitting down to defecate, when his younger brother Bholu, who arrived from behind, picked up a cement stone lying there and struck him three times repeatedly on his face. After this, he strangled him with a scarf. The police, engaged in the investigation, reached the deceased's house on Thursday morning and called brother Bholu for questioning. Amit's wife Khushi got scared by the police action and attempted suicide. Upon strict questioning, he confessed to the crime. He revealed that he had an illicit relationship with his elder brother's wife, Khushi. His sister-in-law had instigated him to kill her husband. Their plan was that after killing the brother, they would both get married by informing the family. Now read the accused brother's confession During interrogation, Bholu stated that his elder brother Amit's wedding took place on February 19. “After the wedding, a love affair developed between me and my sister-in-law Khushi,” he said. Both wanted to live together. Three days ago, Amit saw them in an objectionable state. After this, there was also a quarrel at home. Following this, both planned to murder Amit and remove him from their path. His wife was also involved in this. The accused brother stated, “While he was urinating, I hit my brother on the head with a stone from behind. When he fell down, I strangled him with his towel.” He kept strangling him until his brother died. Even the deceased's neck bone was broken. Marriage took place three months ago The deceased Solu was married about three months ago. After the murder, the accused brother kept shedding tears over his death. He was crying loudly. Meanwhile, the deceased's wife faked a suicide attempt. She tried to hang herself in the house. DCP City said - Bholu has been arrested for murder and the deceased's wife Khushi has been arrested for conspiring the murder. Legal action is being taken against both of them.

stories.title: Hundreds of fair-price shop dealers protest:Warn of halting August ration distribution if demands not met; police stop Assembly march
stories.summary: Hundreds of fair price shop dealers from across the state arrived in Lucknow on Tuesday regarding their pending demands. They started from Charbagh to gherao the Assembly. The police stopped them at Charbagh itself. The fair price shop dealers were preparing to take out a foot march from Charbagh to the Assembly, but they were not allowed to proceed due to the presence of heavy police force. After this, all the protestors were put into buses and sent to Eco Garden. Fair price shop dealers associated with the All India Fair Price Shop Dealers Federation arrived to submit a memorandum to the Chief Minister. The organisation has made it clear that if the government does not take a quick decision on their demands, ration distribution will not be done across the entire state in August. The announcement of this movement has already been made through meetings in various districts. See 3 pictures- These are the main demands of the quota holders Quota holders have put forward several demands to the government. Among these, the most prominent demand is to increase the commission to ₹200 per quintal. They state that the commission received in Uttar Pradesh is quite low compared to other states. Additionally, the outstanding payment for free ration distribution during the coronavirus period in November 2021, pending funding for food grains distributed at market price, and payment for empty sacks deposited during wheat procurement have not yet been made. Immediate payment of all these arrears has been demanded. Government responsible if ration distribution is affected The organisation has warned that if the government does not take a positive decision on their demands, ration distribution will not be done throughout the state in the month of August. Ration dealers say that in such a situation, the government and the concerned department will be responsible for the disruption of ration distribution. UP receives 90 rupees per quintal as commission Ration shop dealers say that in Uttar Pradesh, ration shop dealers are given a commission of 90 rupees per quintal. The Haryana government gives its ration shop dealers a commission of 200 rupees per quintal. The Delhi government also gives the same amount to its ration shop dealers, whereas the Goa government gives its ration shop dealers a commission of 230 rupees per quintal. The Gujarat government is providing a minimum income guarantee of ₹2,000 to ration shop dealers. Many other states are also giving many times more commission than UP. Fair price shop dealers should also be given an honorarium Rajesh Tiwari, State President of the All Indian Fair Price Shop Dealers Association, said that due to low commission, fair price shop dealers always face livelihood problems amid severe inflation. In states like Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala, fair price shop dealers are given an honorarium. Therefore, to cope with inflation, fair price shop dealers in UP should also be given an honorarium.

stories.title: Boating suspended at Ramgarh Tal after accident:All four platforms closed; two panels to probe cause of crash; routes to be fixed for all vessels
stories.summary: The Ramgarhtal in Gorakhpur, where a young man lost his life on Sunday night due to a collision between two boats, remained closed for boating on Monday. Boating remained suspended from all platforms. Two committees have been assigned the responsibility of finding out the causes of this accident. One committee has been formed by the District Magistrate, and the other by the Gorakhpur Development Authority (GDA). Members of both committees will investigate who is responsible for the accident and whether the boat operators were following the standard operating procedures. Action will be taken thereafter. Learning from this incident, several arrangements are also being made. Geo-fencing will be done in the lake by the authority. Every type of boat will have its own route. Blinking lights will also be installed in them, so that the route is visible even in the dark. Also, speed boats will no longer operate after sunset, whereas normal boats may be allowed until 9 PM. Two families from Kushinagar had come to visit Gorakhpur Qayamuddin, a resident of Kaptaanganj in Kushinagar district, had come to visit Gorakhpur with his family and cousin Lakhmuddin. Qayamuddin had arrived on vacation from Saudi Arabia 10 days ago. To show his family around, they first went to the zoo. From there, they went to the mall for shopping. After that, at the insistence of the children, they reached Platform No. 5 to ride a boat. The entire family boarded a large boat. This boat was moving slowly, and as it passed in front of Platform No. 4, about 100 meters away, suddenly, a speed boat from Platform No. 4 was seen approaching. The driver of the boat on which Qayamuddin's family was sitting tried to move the boat away from the shore to escape, but the speed boat collided with it. One person fell into the water. Lakhmuddin's head hit the boat and burst, which led to his death. Qayamuddin sustained a shoulder injury. 8 people were injured, out of which 7 people were discharged by the afternoon of July 27. Boating remained closed on July 27 Dainik Bhaskar's team reached Ramgarhtal's jetty to understand the situation after the incident. Shops were open there, and a few people were arriving. Their eyes were towards the lake, but they were returning disappointed as boating was closed. There is a path to Platform Number 4 from this jetty, but it has been closed. From here, we reached Platform Number 5, which was also closed. A trial of a speed boat was conducted at the adjacent Platform Number 6, and it was brought to the platform for repair work to begin. Currently, boating takes place from Platform Numbers 1, 4, 5, and 6 in the lake. But on Monday, platforms everywhere appeared closed. Boats were tied to the platforms. Some employees were seen at Platform Number 6, but they expressed ignorance about yesterday's incident. They said that currently the jetty is closed, and they will operate boats when instructions come. Meanwhile, all boats will be repaired and cleaned. Qayamuddin's condition is out of danger, but he is in shock from the accident. Qayamuddin, injured in the accident, is now out of danger. Mayor Dr Manglesh Srivastava also went to see him. He is admitted to the male surgical ward of the district hospital. He says that today there is some relief from the pain. However, Qayamuddin seemed to avoid talking. He had brought everyone to Gorakhpur. The pain of losing his cousin right before his eyes was visible. To avoid the pain, he was not ready to say anything. He said, “Lakhmuddin's father Riasat lives in Saudi Arabia. He will reach home by tomorrow morning. What face will I show to my uncle and my siblings?” Lakhmuddin's family plunged into grief Lakhmuddin was a resident of Pipra Tiwari village in Hata police station area. He was studying in the 12th grade at Sant Pushpa Intermediate College in Dhada. Lakhmuddin was also planning to go abroad. That is why when he received information about Qayamuddin coming home, he reached Qayamuddin's house. Lakhmuddin had four siblings. Lakhmuddin's father works as a tailor. None of his siblings are married. Now know what arrangements will change in Ramgarhtal

stories.title: Eco-friendly Sawan at Kashi Vishwanath Dham:Temple authorities urge Kanwariyas to avoid plastic; 70–80 lakh pilgrims likely to arrive
stories.summary: To keep Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham completely plastic-free in Sawan month 2026, the temple administration has intensified a special campaign. Considering the arrival of millions of Kanwariyas and devotees from across the country, the administration is giving equal priority to environmental protection as it is to the convenience and safety of devotees. The temple administration's clear message is that plastic will not be used in Baba Vishwanath's Dham, and all devotees are being appealed to cooperate in this campaign. Appeal to Kanwariyas - Do not carry holy water in plastic containers The Chief Executive Officer of Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple stated that a large number of Kanwariyas are reaching the shrine for Abhishek (offering water) carrying Gangajal in plastic containers. Such devotees are continuously being requested to bring water in copper, brass, steel, or other eco-friendly containers instead of plastic. He said that a plastic-free shrine is not solely the responsibility of the administration, but this campaign will only succeed with the participation of every devotee. To ensure devotees do not face any inconvenience, the temple administration has provided paper glasses at all major entrance gates. If any devotee arrives with water in a plastic container, they can offer the same water in a paper glass to Baba Vishwanath. The objective of this arrangement is to prevent the use of plastic and to keep the Dham premises clean and environmentally friendly. 70 to 80 lakh devotees expected this Sawan During the month of Sawan, an estimated 70 to 80 lakh devotees are expected to visit Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham this year. Considering this large number, the temple administration and district administration have jointly completed extensive preparations. With the aim of providing devotees with an experience of 'devotion, service, security, and easy darshan', security, traffic, medical, drinking water, and darshan arrangements have been strengthened. The shrine will be monitored by 333 cameras Uttar Pradesh Police, CRPF, PAC, LIU, Bomb Disposal Squad, Dog Squad and NDRF have been deployed for the security of the temple premises. The entire shrine area will be monitored 24 hours a day through 333 CCTV cameras. Security checks will be mandatory at all major entry gates, while public address systems and lost and found centers will also remain operational continuously. For the convenience of devotees, arrangements for pure drinking water at 19 locations within the premises, medical aid centers, ambulance service, German hangers, and temporary shade have been made. Free cart service will be available for the elderly, disabled, and special guests. Additionally, live broadcasts of the worship will also be shown on large LED screens at the temple premises and pilgrim facilitation centres.
