stories.summary: A 10-year-old grandson of a jewellery businessman in Gorakhpur was abducted and murdered on Tuesday. His body was found stuffed inside a sack at the home of a neighbour living just 20 metres from the family’s house. Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Dr Kaustubh said Vaibhav Verma went missing on Monday evening. He had returned home from school and later went outside on his bicycle to play. Around 30 minutes later, the family was informed that the boy’s bicycle had been found abandoned. The family rushed to the spot and searched the surrounding area, where they found one of the child's slippers a short distance away. They checked with his school, friends and relatives before informing the police. Police, accompanied by a forensic team and a dog squad, reached the scene and examined CCTV footage. The footage showed the boy walking away with a computer teacher who lived in the neighbourhood. During questioning, the teacher allegedly tried to mislead investigators. Police then sought the help of a psychologist during the interrogation, after which the suspect confessed to abducting and killing the boy. However, he did not reveal the motive for the murder. Acting on the accused's lead, police recovered the child's body from the basement of his house. The accused has been arrested. The SSP said the accused had repeatedly lied during questioning. Police will also recreate the crime scene as part of the investigation. Forensic experts have been called in from Lucknow. The incident took place in Khajni town, around 50 km from the Gorakhpur district headquarters. Six Photos- Class 4 pupil went missing, family approached police suspecting abduction Laxmi Narayan Verma, one of the leading jewellery businessmen in the area, lives in Khajni town. His son Hanuman's youngest son, Vaibhav, was a Class 4 pupil at Navals Academy. At around 1:30 pm on Monday, Vaibhav returned home from school. After keeping his school bag at home and changing out of his uniform, he took his bicycle and went outside. His grandmother asked him to have lunch, but he told her he would be back shortly. Around 30 minutes later, a neighbour informed the family that Vaibhav's bicycle was lying behind the house. His grandmother rushed to the spot, about 50 metres away, but Vaibhav was nowhere to be seen. She searched the surrounding area but could not find him, and alerted the family. Vaibhav's father and other relatives arrived within 20–25 minutes and began searching. About 100 metres from where the bicycle was found, they discovered one of Vaibhav's slippers in an open field. Suspecting he had been abducted, the family immediately informed the police. Sniffer dog tracked scent for nearly 1 km after smelling child's clothes SSP Dr Kaustubh immediately formed five police teams. One team began scanning CCTV footage, while the others reached the spot with a dog squad. The sniffer dog was given the child's school uniform to smell before beginning the search. It followed the scent from the spot where Vaibhav's slipper had been found, tracking it through fields for nearly one kilometre before reaching a road. This led police to suspect that the child had been taken through the fields before reaching the roadside. CCTV showed boy walking with neighbour; suspect confessed during questioning Meanwhile, police found CCTV footage showing Vaibhav walking through a field with another man. Vaibhav was seen walking ahead, while the man followed behind. Police called Vaibhav's father, who identified the man as Sarvesh Bhatt, a neighbour living four or five houses away. Sarvesh was taken into custody, and during questioning, the case was cracked. According to police, Sarvesh met Vaibhav after the boy left home and asked him to come along. As Sarvesh was a neighbour whom Vaibhav saw regularly, the child went with him willingly. The two walked around for some time before Sarvesh took Vaibhav to his house. The house has two storeys and a basement, with the family living on the upper floor. Police said Sarvesh carried out the crime while his family members were upstairs. After killing the boy, he allegedly stuffed the body into a sack and hid it among sacks of grain in the basement to avoid raising suspicion, intending to dispose of the body later. Police detain accused's family as relatives demand death penalty Following news of the boy's death, the family staged a protest. Women from the neighbourhood surrounded the police station, while Vaibhav's father sat on a sit-in protest on the road. The family demanded that the accused be awarded the death penalty. Family members told SP South D.K. Puri that strict action should be taken against those responsible and that they should be sentenced to death. He assured them that the accused's house would be demolished within 24 hours. Meanwhile, police have taken all members of the accused Sarvesh Bhatt's family into custody for questioning. The accused's house has been locked, and police personnel have been deployed outside. Boy's mother had died just over a month ago Vaibhav's father, Hanuman Verma, said his wife, Shweta Verma, had died of an illness around one and a half months ago. Since then, Vaibhav had been spending most of his time with him. "After watching the CCTV footage, it was clear that it was a case of abduction. Some local residents were also seen in the footage. Later, we began to suspect Sarvesh," he said. Accused married a year ago, had spent 40 days in Naini Jail According to police, the accused, Sarvesh, was so calculating that he joined the family in searching for Vaibhav even though he had allegedly already killed the child. Police said that during questioning, Sarvesh claimed he stopped Vaibhav as the boy was passing in front of his house and told him, "I have a gift for you. Come with me." He alleged that when Vaibhav pulled away and said, "I don't want a gift. I'll complain to my father," he took the child to a field beside the house. Police said Sarvesh confessed to pinning the boy down by placing his knee on his chest and strangling him. He then allegedly put the body in a sack and carried it home in the afternoon. At the time, his father, wife and sister-in-law were in separate rooms upstairs. He allegedly took the sack to the basement, where sacks of grain were stored, hid it among them, and covered it with a quilt and a mattress. Accused's house sealed; father runs clothing shop, brother is a lawyer The accused, Sarvesh, lives at the far end of the same lane, about 20 metres from Vaibhav's house. Police have sealed his home. Beyond the house are fields and bushes, where police said the crime was carried out. Sarvesh's father, Hari Narayan, owns a clothing shop, while his elder brother, Satish, is a lawyer. Sarvesh himself runs a computer coaching centre that offers diploma courses and prepares students for the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). According to police, Sarvesh was jailed in 2024 in connection with a paper leak case in Bihar. He spent 40 days in Naini Jail in Prayagraj, where investigators believe he came into contact with hardened criminals. Police suspect he wanted to become rich quickly by taking shortcuts. Sarvesh got married a year ago.

stories.title: From snakebite murder to the blue drum case:Meerut's five killer wives now cutting grass in prison
stories.summary: Five wives are imprisoned in Meerut District Jail on charges of murdering their husbands. One got her husband killed by a snakebite, while another murdered her husband and stuffed him into a blue drum. All of them murdered their husbands with the desire to settle down with their lovers. The latest case is of Damini, who got her husband killed by a snakebite. Damini is imprisoned in Barrack No. 12A of the jail. Opposite her, in Barrack No. 12B for female inmates, four more wives are imprisoned who murdered their husbands with their lovers. These women have been brought to jail within a year. Some are peeling grass in jail, while others are sweeping and mopping. They have also been assigned cooking duties. Sewing responsibilities have also been given. 1. Damini sometimes sits sadly in the barrack, sometimes cries On the night of July 17-18, in Hastinapur, Damini, the principal of a private school, had her school owner husband Atul Pawar (32) bitten by a snake. Along with her school van driver lover Tushar and two other accomplices, she first gave Atul an overdose of sleeping pills in milk. After this, she had him bitten by a snake. Damini, Tushar, and both snake charmers are imprisoned. On July 18, 2026, Damini was brought to Meerut District Jail. For the first 2 days in jail, no one spoke to her. Female inmates, upon seeing her, would discuss among themselves what crime Damini had committed to be in jail? Damini repeatedly remembers her six-year-old son Manik in jail. Even after 9 days, no one has come to meet Damini in jail yet. She sits for hours at the barrack gate, gazing towards the main jail gate. She hopes to hear a voice from outside announcing that her family has come to meet her. She remains sad in jail. Sometimes she lies on her bed and starts crying. When other female inmates ask her how and why she killed her husband, she bows her head. Jail staff said that for the first two days, Damini barely ate anything. When the jail counsellor talked to her, she became a little more comfortable. Then she started eating a little. Damini is crying for her son, says, “I want to educate him in jail” Damini told the jail staff that she wants to teach female inmates and their children. She has teaching experience. She used to teach children and run a school until now. That's why she wants to become a teacher. The jail administration accepted her request and assigned her the work of teaching in jail and maintaining the library. Damini does not even have clothes to wear. She has received clothes from the jail. Once she expressed a desire to meet her lover Tushar. But due to jail regulations, she cannot meet Tushar. Damini wakes up in the morning and does her daily duties. She cleans and maintains the library. After this, she sits at the barrack gate and keeps gazing. When women talk to her, she starts crying. Currently, the investigation in Damini's case is ongoing. A charge sheet has not been filed in the case, but Damini has stated that she will fight the case with her own lawyer. 2. Muskan has been in jail for 17 months On the night of March 3, 2025, Muskan Rastogi, residing in Brahmapuri, along with her lover Sahil, murdered her husband Saurabh Rajput. The body was dismembered and solidified in a blue drum with cement and sand. Muskan and Sahil are in jail. Muskan has spent about 17 months in jail. She is in barrack number 12B. Now, jail has become Muskan's home. In these 17 months, no family member or relative has come to meet Muskan. Her parents, brothers, and sisters have severed ties with her. They clearly stated that Muskan is dead to them. Muskan has also given up hope of her loved ones coming to meet her in jail. She has considered the jail and the female inmates living there as her family. On November 23, 2025, Muskan gave birth to a daughter at the Medical Hospital. The daughter has been named Mannat. In jail, Muskan's first and last support in life is now only her daughter Mannat. She caresses and loves her daughter all day long. She feeds her, plays with her, and talks to her. Other female inmates also love Muskan's daughter. Alcohol-cannabis addiction is now gone After coming to jail, Muskan's health and beauty have improved. Muskan is now more beautiful and healthier than before. She has gained 15 kg in jail. In jail, Muskan takes an extra diet meant for pregnant women, in addition to dal-chawal (lentils-rice) and roti (bread). In this, she is being given milk, fruits, along with iron and vitamin supplements. After continuous counselling, Muskan has become mentally stable in jail. Muskan has completely given up her addiction. Now she doesn't consume alcohol, ganja, or anything. She also misses her lover Sahil less. Her entire time is spent taking care of her daughter. Muskan has a small child, so she has not been given any work in jail. Muskan is less educated. Therefore, she listens to Ramayana and Sundarkand being read by other female inmates in jail. She listens to the Sundarkand that is played in jail. She has expressed her desire to meet her lover Sahil, who is lodged in the male barracks, to the jail administration many times, but according to the rules, their meeting cannot take place. The verdict in Muskan's case will come in August Government lawyer Rekha Jain is fighting Muskan's case. The case has been heard before the District Judge for the past seven months. The testimony of 22 people has been completed. Final arguments have been made. Now the final cross-examination of witnesses is underway, in which the prosecution has presented its side before the court. Now lawyer Rekha Jain is cross-examining the witnesses, representing Muskan and Sahil. Cross-examination of 14 witnesses has been completed. The verdict in the case will come in August. 3. Strangled husband with lover, then released a snake In Akbarpur Sadat village of Bahsuma, Ravita, along with her lover Amardeep, strangled her husband Amit to death on April 17, 2025. After this, she released a rat snake on the bed. She faked that her husband was bitten by the snake. After the post-mortem report confirmed death by strangulation, the police arrested Ravita and Amardeep. Both are imprisoned. Ravita is waiting to get out of jail. She hopes that she will be acquitted in this murder case and will come out. Ravita, who has been imprisoned for about 15 months, often misses her home. She has been assigned cooking and cleaning duties in jail, which she performs regularly. Besides this, she practices yoga in jail. She has been given small gardening tasks in jail, such as weeding. Ravita's family members sometimes come to meet her. Ravita meets them and expresses regret for her actions. Ravita has told her counselor many times that she wants to come out. She regrets what she did, but the law is the same for everyone. Until Ravita's case is complete, she cannot come out. Ravita is now waiting to be released. Ravita's case is on trial at the District Judge's court. Cross-examination is currently ongoing. 4. Pledging jewelry, had BSF husband killed, now cooking food in jail In Dhanpur village of Inchauli, BSF jawan Nain Singh was shot dead while sleeping at home late night on March 27, 2026. Police checked the CCTVs installed in the village and surrounding areas on the day of the incident. In this, Nain Singh's wife Komal's lover Gulshan and Montu were seen. Komal had hired shooters by pledging her wedding jewelry. Komal was admitted to jail on April 3, 2026. She is confined in Barrack No. 12B. She has been assigned the work of cooking food in jail. Komal, who used to work all day in the fields and at home in the village, also does tailoring in jail. She has befriended other female inmates in jail. Komal also regrets her actions. She tells other women that blinded by love, she ruined her home. The house where she lived with pride, now she is spending time in jail. There is no one of her own here. Komal's family from her maternal home sometimes comes to meet her in jail. Whenever a new female inmate comes to jail, Komal always asks her, "Why did you do this wrong thing?" In jail, she also talks to Muskan and Ravita. After work, she sits silently. In her counselling sessions, Komal has repeatedly said that she regrets what she did. She has ruined her own home with her own hands. She made a mistake. “However Nain Singh was, he was my husband,” she says. Komal's case is on trial at the District Judge's court, where cross-examinations are continuously taking place. A private lawyer is fighting the case. 5. Had her husband shot in the chest by her lover, now sweeping and mopping in jail On the morning of November 1, 2025, Rahul's (28) body was found in the bushes outside Agwanpur village in Parikshitgarh. He had been shot in the chest. Rahul was murdered by his wife Anjali, who had her lover Ajay do it. Rahul and Anjali have three children. At night, Anjali called Rahul to the temple outside the village. Her lover Ajay also arrived there. Then Ajay shot Rahul three times, killing him. 26-year-old Anjali was admitted to jail on November 6, 2025. She is confined in barrack number 12B. Anjali has been assigned cleaning and sweeping-mopping work in the jail. She talks to old and new female inmates in the jail. Along with this, she also does tailoring work. Sometimes her family from her maternal home comes to meet Anjali in jail. Anjali often waits for her family to visit. In her free time, Anjali listens to the Ramayana. She is also learning to read. She hopes that she might someday be released from jail after serving her sentence. On that day, she will start her new life. But, she is waiting for that day to come. Anjali's case is on trial at the District Judge's court. Cross-examination is ongoing. Private lawyers are fighting her case.

stories.title: Dismissed professor speaks after participating in CJP protest:‘What crime did I commit? I only raised students’ voices,’ adds, 'A ruler should protect, not harass'
stories.summary: Assistant Professor Mohit Bhardwaj of a degree college in Bareilly has been dismissed. The professor had participated in a student protest at Jantar Mantar on July 20. He had raised slogans: Modi, come to your senses... Whenever Modi gets scared, he puts the police forward... He was removed from his job on July 22. Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Professor Mohit Bhardwaj. He said - In a democracy, everyone has complete freedom to express their views. In UP's aided colleges, dozens of such teachers and professors are now sitting as MLAs and ministers. If they can do politics, then can't a common teacher raise his voice for students and unemployed youth? When people associated with the ruling party openly display their strength in college campuses wearing saffron scarves or RSS black caps, no one has any objection. Has going to Jantar Mantar and raising my voice in favor of students become my biggest crime? The duty of a king is to protect his subjects, not to torment them. When students are committing suicide due to depression caused by paper leaks, remaining silent is the government's biggest sin. Mohit Bhardwaj is the President of the Samajwadi Party Yuvjan Sabha. He was also an Assistant Professor at Ganna Utpadak Post Graduate College in Bahedi, Bareilly. Read the complete interview with Mohit Bhardwaj Question: You were fired from your job after raising slogans at Jantar Mantar. What was your mistake? Answer: We live in a democracy. Where every citizen has the right to express their views and register their protest. I was always taught with complete honesty in college. When our taught students take the police recruitment exam and the very next moment their hard work is wasted due to a re-exam or a paper leak. The pain of that destruction shakes not only the student, but also their teacher. When I saw the future of students becoming dark in cases like NEET or other competitive exams, my conscience as a teacher could not accept it. On Sonam Wangchuk's call, I took to the streets with students at Jantar Mantar on 20th July. Question: Were you dismissed only because you are associated with SP? Answer: Absolutely, that is the real reason. I have sent WhatsApp chat evidence to many people, including Deepak, the founder of Cockroach Janta Party. The way this action has been taken with a spirit of revenge under pressure from the government is completely dictatorial. Although I may have been the president of Yuvjan Sabha on paper, I have given all my energy and time to my students and college. Question: Do you think there was political pressure on the college management? Answer: Obviously, there was tremendous political pressure on the management committee. All this happened overnight at their behest. Just a few days ago, when I was applying to Kumaon University, the manager of this very college had given me an NOC (No Objection Certificate). In that NOC and the character certificate given by the Principal, my efficiency, honesty, and active role in various committees were openly praised. How did a teacher who until yesterday was the most honest and hardworking in their eyes suddenly become incompetent just by participating in a protest at Jantar Mantar? This is clearly the result of political pressure from above. Question: Did you also face discrimination because of being a Brahmin? Answer: The situation of the entire state is before everyone. If you look at the records impartially today, in the majority community, if any section is being exploited and targeted the most, it is the Brahmin community. Whether it is the administrative department or public platforms, today everywhere, as per a specific strategy, only and only Brahmins are being targeted and harassed. My case could also be a link in that chain. Question: Was the college administration upset with you during your 2-year tenure? Answer: Look at my WhatsApp chats. Our students are writing that, sir, we are not able to sleep. We are worried. Tell us what we should do? This is the students' true love for me. If the college administration's attitude was right, then why did they remove me from the WhatsApp group overnight? They were afraid that the entire college and students might mobilize in my support. Even today, there is immense anger among the students. If I don't get justice soon, the students are ready to take to the streets themselves with a big movement against the college administration and demanding transfer. Question: Is SP standing firmly with you in this entire matter? Answer: The entire party and leadership are standing with me like a rock in this difficult time. Just this morning, former MP Praveen Singh Aron and our city president called. They clearly said that Mohit bhai, you are not alone. The party is standing with you with full strength. At whatever level we need to fight this battle legally or politically, we are all standing shoulder to shoulder with you. Question: What was going through your mind regarding the lathi-charge on students at Jantar Mantar? Answer: Even today my soul trembles remembering that horrific scene. Is the brutality with which the police wielded their batons, is justified by any definition of humanity? Daughters are the future and honor of this country. When policemen rained sticks on them and committed inhumane acts against them, as a teacher and as a human being, my heart cried out. Is this the real model of 'Beti Bachao' (Save the Daughter)? Question: Students involved in the movement were called anti-national on social media? Answer: When farmers sat for their rights, they were called Khalistanis. When students took to the streets for their future, they were falsely labeled as receiving foreign funding. The country's own Foreign Minister has stated that no such funding was confirmed in the investigation. However, it has become a habit of those in power that whoever questions the government is directly declared 'anti-national' or 'terrorist'. Is saying 'Inquilab Zindabad', 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' or raising a voice against paper leaks anti-national? Question: How do you view this movement and the major movements before it? Answer: This was not a movement of any one political party, but a movement of every affected family in the country whose children have been victims of paper leaks. I saw 80- 90-year-old elderly people in that protest. I saw a differently-abled young man reaching there by riding his tricycle for 3 days. In this, 30 to 35% were only women and daughters who left their jobs and studies to participate in this struggle. History is witness that, like the movements of Mahatma Gandhi and Anna Hazare, this was such a public wave that the government had to bow down before it. Question: How do you view the continuous paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment exams? Answer: A student from my college, Rahul Sharma, was preparing for the police recruitment exam. He scored excellent marks in the first paper, but after a re-exam or system manipulation, his marks became zero. That child is in depression today. When our taught children break down like this, a teacher's heart is shattered. The college management considers itself the owner of that educational institution. Whereas, this college is a temple built by the poor sugarcane farmers of Bahedi by saving penny by penny. These so-called managers are merely tenants sitting in the chair for 5 years.

stories.title: Heavy rain floods Noida, waist-deep water on streets:Colonies waterlogged in Meerut and Saharanpur as downpour hits 15 UP cities
stories.summary: The monsoon has become active once again in Uttar Pradesh. Since Tuesday morning, intermittent heavy rain has been reported in 15 cities, including Noida, Meerut and Gonda. Saharanpur received heavy rainfall from around 4 am. Two hours of torrential rain left roads submerged under 2–3 feet of water. The District Magistrate's office campus was flooded up to knee level. Water also entered the Officers' Colony, where the official residences of the District Judge, Commissioner and Municipal Commissioner are located. Most residential colonies across the city were inundated. In Noida, roads were submerged up to waist level. Women were seen carrying schoolchildren on their shoulders while wading through floodwater, and several motorcycles were partially submerged. Flooding disrupts offices In Meerut, rainwater entered the premises of the Development Authority office. Waterlogging outside the camp office left the Mayor stranded inside. In Raebareli, heavy rain created a two-foot-deep crater in a field. When villagers inspected the site, they discovered a tunnel. An Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) reached the spot and began an investigation. IMD issues rain alert for all 75 districts The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday. Very heavy rainfall is forecast in seven districts, while 53 districts are likely to receive heavy rain. Meanwhile, continuous rainfall in the hills has caused the Ganga, Yamuna, Ghaghara and Saryu rivers to swell. In Lakhimpur Kheri, riverbank erosion has washed away 120 bighas of sugarcane crop into the Sharda River. In Ballia, floodwaters from the Saryu River have entered several villages. See photos of rain- Lucknow weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said that the monsoon trough is once again moving towards Uttar Pradesh. At the same time, the low-pressure area formed over the Bay of Bengal is also strengthening. “Due to these conditions, good rainfall is expected in both eastern and western parts of UP. Several districts may receive light to moderate rain, while some areas could witness heavy showers till 30 July. There is also a possibility of lightning strikes in some regions,” he said.

stories.title: Why Jauhar University will not be demolished:5 key reasons, fear of Delhi-like protests and shifting 3,000 students pose major hurdles
stories.summary: Demolishing 38 buildings of Jauhar University is not easy. Equations have changed after the Gen-Z protests in Delhi. The government's stance on the university, which is related to education and students, has also softened. This is why on July 27, Anjaneya Kumar Singh, Commissioner of Moradabad Division, put a stay on the demolition proceedings until the next hearing. On the other hand, to avoid any legal setback, the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) has already filed a caveat in court, so that the court cannot issue any unilateral order without hearing the administration's side. Meanwhile, for the past 10 days, university students have been protesting outside the campus. Now the question arises: will the government demolish these buildings despite the protests? Let's understand in 5 points- Mayawati welcomes stay on demolition of Jauhar University buildings Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati on Tuesday welcomed the stay on the proposed demolition of 38 buildings on the campus of the Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur until the final hearing in the case. Reason 1. Fear of Delhi's Gen-Z movement Professor S.K. Yadav, who teaches media students at Allahabad University, says - Youth across the country staged a big protest regarding the NEET exam leak. Eventually, the central government was forced to retreat. Dharmendra Pradhan had to resign. After this one movement, the morale of the youth is high. If any action is taken against the university, there is a high probability that the youth will unite and try to save it. In such a situation, there could be a confrontation between students and the administration. The government wants to avoid this situation, especially when elections are due in just 6-7 months. Reason 2. Decisions made from Rampur, not Lucknow SP and Congress are protesting to save the university. Besides all this, local people also do not want the university to be demolished. Among them are a large number of people who do not belong to Azam Khan's politics and his party. Local BJP leaders also do not support its demolition. Whenever they are asked a question, they ignore it. Even at the state level, no leader seems to support the demolition of the university. An official close to the government in Lucknow says - CM Yogi or the government never intended to demolish the university. The local level officials are taking such decisions. However, the final decision will be from the court and Lucknow. Reason 3. No college big enough to shift students Currently, about 3,000 students are studying at the university. The university has 16 departments. There are 14 faculties and institutes. Courses in medical, engineering, law, and management are taught. Teachers associated with the university claim that there are no colleges nearby where all students can be shifted. Even if they manage to do so, they will not be able to provide facilities for different faculties. Reason 4. When the university was built, there was no authority The university administration says that the construction of Jauhar University started in 2006. At that time, there was no development authority. Despite this, an order was issued for the demolition of 38 buildings of the university. The university had filed a petition with this argument in the Allahabad High Court on July 20. Its hearing is scheduled for July 28. On July 26, the DM Rampur sent a team to the university campus and asked for building maps. The university administration provided maps of the medical college and academic block. They could not provide maps for the remaining buildings. Reason 5. UGC's support towards the university Experts say, UGC will support the university in this matter. This is because UGC had granted recognition based on the rules applicable at the time of the university's establishment. In 2014, UGC's expert committee investigated the university. At that time, it stated in its report that the fees for various courses at the university are significantly lower than those of other private colleges. This university is not operating for commercial gain. The authority that Azam built, has now become a problem In 2005, when the SP government was in power in UP, Azam Khan was the Urban Development Minister. During the same period, on April 15, 2005, the Rampur Development Authority was formed. Initially, 23 villages along with Rampur Nagar Palika were included in the ambit of the authority. On September 18, 2006, Azam Khan laid the foundation of Jauhar University in Singankhera village. At that time, Singankhera village was not under the jurisdiction of the authority. In July 2024, the authority expanded its boundaries and included 39 villages around the city within its ambit. Singankhera village was also among them. This is where the entire dispute began. After the SP government left power, the authority investigated the university's buildings. It was found that out of 40 buildings, only the medical college and administrative building had approved maps. The maps for the remaining 38 buildings were not approved. Based on this, a notice was issued to the university. The authority stated that these 38 buildings should be demolished by July 30, otherwise the administration would take demolition action. However, the matter is now in court. The university can be saved from demolition by imposing a fine According to legal experts, the High Court will not only see whether the buildings of Jauhar University should be demolished or not. It will also decide whether any other way can be adopted instead of demolition. First, the option of regularizing the matter by taking a fine and other fees can be discussed. Currently, Rampur Development Authority charges a development fee of Rs 1510 per square meter. In addition, a labor cess is also levied, which is 1% of the total cost of any project. The cost of Jauhar University is said to be around Rs 1000 crore. According to this, the labor cess alone amounts to about Rs 10 crore. In addition, supervision charges, map approval fees, compounding fees, and several other charges may also have to be paid. However, the exact amount the university will have to pay can only be calculated after the layout plan and complete records of the buildings are revealed.

stories.title: What's holding up UP's 69,000 teacher recruitment case:Government's 'special plan' for reserved candidates who moved to SC
stories.summary: Today, an important hearing is scheduled in the Supreme Court regarding the recruitment of 69,000 teachers in UP. 5 lawyers each from the UP government and the petitioners will present their respective sides. The future of more than 67,000 teachers and approximately 9,000 candidates who have been excluded from the reservation process depends on this decision. Earlier on Monday, both sides had filed affidavits in court and submitted their responses. Where exactly is the hitch in the appointments? What is the government's plan to resolve this before the 2027 elections? Read about it in this report... First, understand how the 69,000 teacher recruitment controversy began? On December 4, 2018, the UP government announced recruitment for 69,000 posts of Assistant Teachers in primary schools. These recruitments were to be conducted according to the UP Basic Education Service. The examination was conducted on January 6, 2019. The next day, on January 7, the cut-off was released. The passing cut-off for General Category candidates was set at 65 and 60% for Reserved Category. Out of 4.31 lakh applicants, 4.09 lakh people appeared in the examination. Cut-off itself was challenged in court As soon as the Recruitment Board released the cut-off, chaos ensued. The passing cut-off was challenged by reserved category candidates first in the High Court and later in the Supreme Court. The High Court's Double Bench on May 6, 2020, and the Supreme Court on November 18, 2020, dismissed these appeals. This meant they refused to make any changes to the passing cut-off. On May 12, 2020, the result of the Assistant Teachers recruitment examination was declared. Based on the cut-off, 1 lakh 46 thousand 60 people passed. 67,867 posts filled on merit basis Recruitment for 67,867 posts was completed under Appendix-1 of the Uttar Pradesh Basic Education (Teacher) Service Rules 1981. However, 1,133 posts reserved for the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category remained vacant due to non-availability of eligible candidates. Later, all these posts were filled with Scheduled Caste (SC) candidates. In the final selection list of recruitment, the cutoff for the General category was 67.11%, OBC was 66.73%, SC was approximately 61.01%, and ST was approximately 54.30%. Appendix-1 explains how merit will be prepared in teacher recruitment. It includes not only the marks of the recruitment examination, but also the marks of High School, Intermediate, Graduation, and BTC/B.Ed. Mistake made in preparing selection list According to Rajesh Chaudhary, Media In-charge of the Backward-Dalit Joint Front fighting the case in the Supreme Court, the merit list for recruitment was prepared according to Appendix-1 of the Basic Education Rules-1981. However, the rules of the Reservation Act-1994 were not properly followed. He says that according to the 1994 reservation rules, if a candidate from OBC, SC, or ST scores equal to or more than the general category cutoff, then they should get selection on a general seat. Such a candidate will not be counted in the reserved quota. This will leave their reserved seat vacant. Another candidate from the same category will get an opportunity on that seat. Reserved category candidates challenged in High Court Alleging that reservation rules were not properly followed in the recruitment, reserved category candidates filed a petition in the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court in July 2020. Along with this, the matter also reached the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC). The commission also acknowledged in its investigation that reservation rules were not fully followed in the recruitment. After this, candidates started a sit-in protest at Eco Garden in Lucknow. During the hearing of the case in 2022, the then Basic Education Minister Satish Chandra Dwivedi presented a second selection list of 6,800 candidates in court. The government stated that if reservation rules are implemented correctly, then appointments of this many more candidates would be justified. After this, on March 13, 2023, the High Court's single bench delivered its verdict. The court cancelled the second list of 6,800 candidates. The court said that doing so would increase the number of appointments in the recruitment to more than 69,000. However, the court upheld the first selection list as correct. The petitioners approached the double bench against this decision. Subsequently, on August 13, 2024, the double bench delivered a major verdict. The court ordered the government to prepare the entire selection list again. It said that a new merit list should be issued within 3 months, properly following all reservation rules. General category applicants filed a petition in the Supreme Court The order of the Double Bench of the Lucknow Division was challenged in the Supreme Court in August 2024 by Ravi Saxena, who was among the selected candidates from the general category. He said that his selection was done by the state government. He has been teaching since 2020. Many teachers have even taken loans. Now, if they are removed when a new list is prepared, where will they go? Lawyer representing reserved category candidates presented suggestion in court Currently, the case of 69,000 teacher recruitment is being heard in the Supreme Court by the bench of Justice Deepankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu. In the hearing on February 4, 2026, lawyer Manish Goswami, arguing on behalf of the reserved category, told the court that approximately 1.26 lakh posts are vacant in the Basic Education Department. If the government gives even about 10% of these posts to candidates involved in the dispute, the matter can be easily resolved. On this, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the government, first asked for 10 days' time to discuss with the government. Later, on February 16, she again filed an application asking for three more weeks. After this, the case was listed on March 19, but the hearing could not take place that day. Then, on May 19, the UP government informed the Supreme Court that if the court agrees, it is ready to prepare a new merit list. After this, in the hearing on July 21, the government presented a new list of 8,270 candidates in the court. The government also submitted a new cutoff merit list. According to the new cutoff- The government says that in this list of 8,270 candidates, the most affected candidates are from the General category. Who all are included in the 8,270, and where will the complications get stuck now The list of 8,270 candidates presented by the government in the Supreme Court includes various types of candidates. The largest number among these is 4,940 candidates who could not participate in the second and third counseling. Additionally, there are approximately 1,200 candidates who received 1 extra mark due to an incorrect question in the recruitment examination. Apart from these, some other candidates from different categories are also included in this list. However, there is another major controversy in this list. It includes approximately 4,000 B.Ed. degree holders. Actually, the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court had ruled in the Devesh Sharma case that B.Ed. degree holders cannot be appointed in new primary teacher recruitments going forward. Now, the question is: If new appointments are made in this case, will B.Ed. candidates get a chance, or will they be excluded based on the Constitution Bench's decision? That is, the issue of B.Ed. candidates in the list of 8,270 candidates still remains the biggest legal complication. The final decision on this will have to be made by the Supreme Court itself.

stories.title: ई-रिक्शा पलटने से बुजुर्ग की मौत, चार घायल
stories.summary: बांदा के कठवरिया घाटी में तेज रफ्तार ई-रिक्शा पलटने से चालक की मौत हो गई। इस हादसे में चार अन्य लोग घायल हुए हैं। चालक संतोष, अपनी पत्नी और बच्चों के साथ निमंत्रण से वापस लौट रहा था जब उसकी ई-रिक्शा का ब्रेक फेल हुआ। सभी घायलों को अस्पताल में भर्ती कराया गया है।

stories.title: पीड़िता बोली- न्याय न मिला तो मुख्यमंत्री से लगाउंगी गुहार
stories.summary: बांदा की एक महिला ने अपने गनर पर शादी का झांसा देकर रेप का आरोप लगाया है। महिला गनर के साथ रहने को राजी है, लेकिन गनर मना कर रहा है। महिला ने कहा कि यदि न्याय नहीं मिला, तो वह मुख्यमंत्री से गुहार लगाएगी। मामला परिवार परामर्श केंद्र में चल रहा है।

stories.title: Banda News: मारपीट मामले में तीन दोषियों को कोर्ट उठने तक की सजा व जुर्माना
stories.summary: Banda News: बांदा में विशेष न्यायिक मजिस्ट्रेट ने पांच साल पुराने मारपीट के मामले में तीन दोषियों को न्यायालय उठने तक की सजा और 800 रुपये का अर्थदंड सुनाया। आरोप आरोपितों पर पीड़ित राहुल से मारपीट करने और गाली-गलौज करने का था। अदालत ने उन्हें 'लघु अपराध' मानते हुए दंडित किया।

stories.title: कांवड़ मार्ग पर बिजली व्यवस्था को मुख्य अभियंता ने किया निरीक्षण
stories.summary: कांवड़ यात्रा को सकुशल एवं निर्बाध रूप से संपन्न कराने के लिए मुख्य अभियंता गुरजीत सिंह ने मवाना क्षेत्र के कांवड़ मार्ग का निरीक्षण किया। उन्होंने अधिकारियों को दिशा-निर्देश दिए तथा सुरक्षा से संबंधित कार्य समय पर पूर्ण करने के आदेश दिए। यात्रा के दौरान श्रद्धालुओं की सुरक्षा विभाग की सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता है।

stories.title: सड़क हादसे की रिपोर्ट दर्ज कराई
stories.summary: दिल्ली दून हाईवे पर सात जुलाई को एक भीषण सड़क हादसे में कार चालक आशुतोष मिश्रा के खिलाफ मुकदमा दर्ज किया गया है। इस हादसे में चालक सहित तीन दोस्तों की मौत हो गई और एक साथी गंभीर रूप से घायल हुआ। कार तेज गति से चलाकर अनियंत्रित हो गई थी, जबकि अन्य दोस्त चालाकी को ठीक करने का प्रयास कर रहे थे।

stories.title: एनसीसी: 99 विद्यार्थियों ने चयन प्रक्रिया में भाग लिया
stories.summary: गोरखपुर में 44वीं यूपी बटालियन एनसीसी के तहत महाराणा प्रताप इंटर कॉलेज में पहले वर्ष के कैडेटों की नामांकन प्रक्रिया संपन्न हुई। 52 सीटों के लिए 99 विद्यार्थियों ने भाग लिया। चयन प्रक्रिया शारीरिक परीक्षण और लिखित परीक्षा पर आधारित थी। प्रधानाचार्य ने चयनित छात्रों को शुभकामनाएं दीं।

stories.title: Hamirpur News: ट्रैक्टर की हेड लाइट से नहीं दिखी सड़क, बाइक चला रहे पेंटर की मौत
stories.summary: Hamirpur News: मौदहा में एक सड़क दुर्घटना में एक पेंटर और उसके साथी गंभीर रूप से घायल हो गए। राजवीर, 27 वर्ष, ने गंभीर चोटों के बाद इलाज के दौरान कानपुर में दम तोड़ दिया। यह हादसा उस समय हुआ जब राजवीर और उसके साथी लौट रहे थे और ट्रैक्टर की तेज रोशनी से बाइक अनियंत्रित हो गई।

stories.title: Revanth questions BRS’ silence on demand for Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation
stories.summary: Revanth refers to Intermediate examination paper evaluation controversy during the previous BRS regime, defends his governments initiatives and argues another dam would have to be constructed near Medigadda if water has to be stored

stories.title: Shamli News: सफाई कर्मचारी को निलंबित किया
stories.summary: Shamli News: कैराना के जिला पंचायत राज अधिकारी ने कांवड़ ड्यूटी में लापरवाही और अनुपस्थिति के कारण सफाई कर्मचारी सुधीर कुमार को निलंबित कर दिया है। वहीं, राजस्थान पुलिस ने गोकशी के आरोपी की तलाश में दबिश दी, लेकिन आरोपी नहीं मिला। दोनों मामले क्षेत्र में चर्चित रहे हैं।

stories.title: Shamli News: कैराना रोड की बदहाल साइड पटरी बनी हादसों का कारण
stories.summary: Shamli News: शामली में कैराना-पानीपत मार्ग की साइड पटरी की खराब स्थिति से राहगीरों को परेशानी हो रही है। बारिश के कारण गड्ढे बन गए हैं, जिससे दुर्घटनाएँ होने का खतरा बढ़ गया है। स्थानीय लोग पीडब्ल्यूडी से स्थायी सुधार की मांग कर रहे हैं। नगर पालिका क्षेत्र में भी कई सड़कों की स्थिति खराब है।

stories.title: Shamli News: हसनपुर लुहारी में पाइपलाइन लीकेज के कारण 15 हजार आबादी पानी को तरसी
stories.summary: Shamli News: हसनपुर लुहारी में पेयजल आपूर्ति पूरी तरह से ध्वस्त हो गई है। गांव की मुख्य पाइपलाइन में लीकेज के कारण 15 हजार लोग दिनभर पानी से वंचित रहे। गर्मी में पानी की सप्लाई ठप होने से दैनिक कार्य प्रभावित हुए। ग्रामीणों ने स्थायी समाधान की मांग की है, लेकिन अस्थायी मरम्मत से समस्या खत्म नहीं हो रही।

stories.title: औरैया में जंतर-मंतर लाठीचार्ज के विरोध में छात्रों ने निकाला शांतिमार्च
stories.summary: दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर पर छात्रों पर हुए कथित लाठीचार्ज के खिलाफ, औरैया में छात्रों ने शांतिमार्च निकाला। छात्रों ने काली पट्टी बांधकर घटना की निष्पक्ष जांच की मांग की और शिक्षा मंत्री से इस्तीफे की अपील की। प्रदर्शन के दौरान पुलिस बल तैनात रहा, लेकिन मार्च शांतिपूर्वक संपन्न हुआ।

stories.title: सपा के विरोध मार्च से पहले कमला नगर में पुलिस का पहरा
stories.summary: भाजपा विधायक पुरुषोत्तम खंडेलवाल के खिलाफ समाजवादी पार्टी द्वारा प्रस्तावित विरोध प्रदर्शन से पूर्व पुलिस ने कमला नगर क्षेत्र को छावनी बना दिया। सपा के कार्यकर्ताओं को बैरिकेडिंग कर रोकने के बाद शांत करने का प्रयास किया गया। सपा नेताओं ने विधायक पर भ्रामक पोस्ट करने का आरोप लगाया और कार्रवाई की मांग की।

stories.title: आईआईटी पहुंचना अंत नहीं, एक नई यात्रा की शुरुआत
stories.summary: आईआईटी कानपुर में ओरिएंटेशन कार्यक्रम में नवप्रवेशित छात्र-छात्राओं और उनके अभिभावकों के चेहरों पर गर्व और खुशी थी। प्रो. मणींद्र अग्रवाल ने छात्रों को प्रेरित करते हुए कहा कि यह एक नई यात्रा की शुरुआत है। कार्यक्रम में अकादमिक संरचना और कैम्पस जीवन की जानकारी दी गई।

stories.title: Hamirpur News: हेल्थ केयर का प्रशिक्षण प्राप्त कर रोजगार से जुड़ेंगे युवा
stories.summary: Hamirpur News: सुमेरपुर ब्लाक के पौथिया गांव में कौशल विकास सेंटर का उद्घाटन सदर विधायक डॉ. मनोज प्रजापति ने किया। केंद्र में युवाओं को हेल्थ केयर ट्रेड का नि:शुल्क प्रशिक्षण दिया जाएगा, जिससे 18 से 35 वर्ष के छात्र-छात्राओं को रोजगार के नए अवसर मिलेंगे। विधायक ने सरकार की योजनाओं के बारे में भी जानकारी दी।

stories.title: Hamirpur News: दुग्ध डेयरी मार्ग में गड्ढे ही गड्ढे, बारिश में चलना दूभर
stories.summary: Hamirpur News: भरुआ सुमेरपुर में दुग्ध डेयरी मार्ग की हालत खस्ताहाल है, जिससे स्कूली बच्चे, किसान और अन्य लोग प्रभावित हो रहे हैं। कीचड़ और गंदे पानी ने इस रास्ते को दलदल बना दिया है। स्थानीय निवासियों ने प्रशासन से मरम्मतीकरण की मांग की है। इसके अलावा, कानपुर-सागर हाईवे पर भी गड्ढों की समस्या है, जो दुर्घटनाओं का खतरा बढ़ा रही है।

stories.title: नैनो उर्वरकों के प्रयोग पर जिला सहकारी प्रशिक्षण आयोजित
stories.summary: शामली में इफको के तत्वावधान में नैनो उर्वरकों पर आधारित जिला सहकारी प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रम आयोजित किया गया। अधिकारियों ने किसानों को जागरूक करते हुए नैनो उर्वरकों के उपयोग को बढ़ावा देने पर जोर दिया। मुख्य अतिथि ने नैनो उर्वरकों के लाभ और उनकी बिक्री में वृद्धि के लिए समिति सचिवों की सक्रिय भूमिका की आवश्यकता पर बल दिया।

stories.title: EU locks in oil price cap in new Russia sanctions
stories.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked the EU for the latest measures, saying it was "crucial to preserve our unity and keep up this pressure" on the Kremlin.

stories.title: युवक ने फांसी लगाई, भर्ती
stories.summary: बांदा के कटरा मोहल्ला में 22 वर्षीय पीयूष ने कमरे के अंदर साड़ी से फांसी लगा ली। जब वह काफी देर तक बाहर नहीं निकला, तो परिजनों ने उसे फंदे से लटकते हुआ पाया। तुरंत फंदा काटकर उसे जिला अस्पताल भर्ती कराया गया।

stories.title: ई रिक्शा पलटा, युवक घायल
stories.summary: बांदा के पचनेही गांव में 21 वर्षीय सतीश ई रिक्शा से जाते समय दुर्घटनाग्रस्त हो गए। ई रिक्शा अनियंत्रित होकर पलट गया, जिसके कारण सतीश घायल हो गए। उन्हें तत्काल जिला अस्पताल में भर्ती कराया गया है।

stories.title: Nithin Raj case: prime accused surrenders before Crime Branch, remanded
stories.summary: The Crime Branch had sought permission to re-arrest Dr. Ram after the Thalassery Principal Sessions Court ordered his release, ruling that investigators had failed to comply with the Supreme Court’s guidelines governing arrests when he was taken into custody in Karnataka

stories.title: Hamirpur News: जल निकासी को नाली खोदी, मलबा न हटने से मुश्किलें
stories.summary: Hamirpur News: हमीरपुर के वार्ड नंबर नौ में जल निकासी की समस्या बढ़ गई है। नगरपालिका ने नाली खोदने के बाद मलबा नहीं हटाया है, जिससे निवासियों को आवागमन में कठिनाइयों का सामना करना पड़ रहा है। स्थानीय निवासी घायल हो रहे हैं और गंदगी फैल रही है। सभासद प्रतिनिधि ने जल्द निर्माण कार्य का आश्वासन दिया है।

stories.title: लोकतंत्र बचाने को कांग्रेसियों ने राज्यपाल से लगाई गुहार
stories.summary: कानपुर में, कांग्रेस कमेटी के अध्यक्ष संदीप शुक्ला ने अधिवक्ताओं और वरिष्ठ नेताओं के साथ जिलाधिकारी आवास पर राज्यपाल को ज्ञापन सौंपा। ज्ञापन में विपक्ष के नेताओं को हाउस अरेस्ट करके उनकी स्वतंत्रता का हनन करने का आरोप लगाया गया है। इस दौरान कई प्रमुख कांग्रेस नेता उपस्थित रहे।

stories.title: Agra News: घर में घुसकर महिला से दुष्कर्म का किया प्रयास मुकदमा
stories.summary: Agra News: सदर क्षेत्र की एक महिला ने दुराचार और फर्जी वीडियो के आधार पर बदनाम करने के लिए मामला दर्ज कराया है। आरोपी असरफ पर नशे का आदी होने और महिला के 6 वर्षीय बेटे को जान से मारने की कोशिश करने का आरोप है। पुलिस जांच कर रही है ताकि पीड़िता और उसके परिवार को सुरक्षा मिल सके।

stories.title: एक ही मामले में दो विपरीत आदेश देने पर हाई कोर्ट सख्त, यूपी सरकार की कार्रवाई पर जताया असंतोष
stories.summary: इलाहाबाद हाईकोर्ट ने देवरिया के तत्कालीन उपजिलाधिकारी (एसडीएम) द्वारा एक ही राजस्व वाद में एक ही तारीख को दो परस्पर विरोधी आदेश पारित किए जाने के मामले में उत्तर प्रदेश सरकार की कार्रवाई पर गंभीर असंतोष जताया है।

stories.title: Banda News: सांप ने दो लोगों को डसा, बिगड़ी हालत
stories.summary: Banda News: बांदा के अलीगंज में, 20 वर्षीय तालिब सफीक और 19 वर्षीय काजल को साँप ने डँसा। दोनों की हालत गंभीर होने पर परिजनों ने उन्हें जिला अस्पताल में भर्ती कराया। घटना से इलाके में भय का माहौल है।

stories.title: Chandrashekhar ends protest, ex-girlfriend says ‘bluff exposed’:Accuses him of leaving students during police action, fasting after eating parathas
stories.summary: Nagina MP from Uttar Pradesh and Bhim Army chief Chandrashekhar Azad ended his protest on Thursday. He had been sitting alone in a protest at Parliament for three days against the lathi-charge on students. Activist Dr Rohini Ghavari released a video taking a dig at Chandrashekhar, saying, “The air has gone out. Fasting is not your cup of tea, you were eating parathas there.” Rohini alleged that Chandrashekhar had gone to Jantar Mantar on July 20 to take credit for the 25-day-long struggle of students. She claimed that he made controversial remarks, following which students got agitated and police later used force. She said, “If you were such a big well-wisher of the students, why did you run away? You should have stood in front of the police and faced the action. The moment I asked you to demand Home Minister Amit Shah’s resignation, you left the protest.” Rohini Ghavari is a resident of Indore, Madhya Pradesh. She claims that she was in a relationship with Chandrashekhar. She met the Bhim Army founder while studying in Switzerland. 2 pictures of Chandrashekhar's dharna... Rohini said- If you had taken lathi blows, you would have become a national leader Rohini Ghavari said that students and others had been protesting peacefully at Jantar Mantar for 20-25 days, but Chandrashekhar arrived there later for political gains. She alleged that during the protest, he made statements that provoked students, leading to a tense situation. She claimed that when police took action, the MP left instead of standing with the students. According to her, if Chandrashekhar was genuinely concerned about students, he should have stood with them during the police action and stepped forward for their protection. She further alleged that his intention behind joining the protest was only to gain political benefit and take credit for the movement. Rohini said, “I am not making this video to troll you. I am only making you aware of your reality that whatever you are doing is not right. You were removed from the Jantar Mantar protest. Now you are saying that ‘I was never part of that protest, I was away from it.’ Because those people will not allow you to stand there after seeing that violence broke out because of you.” She added, “Imagine what the scene would have been if an MP was taking lathis while trying to protect students. You would have become a national leader that very day and people would have praised you. But you do not have that courage. You came only to take unnecessary credit.” “Hard work like this is not possible for you. Who knows you better than yourself? I can identify what a person is capable of by looking into their eyes,” she said. ... Rohini Had Given a Challenge Had Said - Demand Home Minister Amit Shah's Resignation Rohini Ghavari had challenged MP Chandrashekhar on Thursday morning, saying, “If you are such a well-wisher of students, I have one demand. The police personnel who lathi-charged them come under Delhi Police, which works under Home Minister Amit Shah. So why don’t you demand his resignation?” She said, “If you do this, I will genuinely appreciate that you have courage. Demand the Education Minister’s resignation, and now demand the Home Minister’s resignation too. Stop this drama. I want to see how you leave the protest and who comes to remove you.” Know who is Rohini Ghavri, what is the dispute with Chandrashekhar? Dr Rohini Ghavari belongs to Indore, Madhya Pradesh. She got an opportunity to study in Switzerland under a fellowship scheme of the Madhya Pradesh government. She completed her PhD there and founded an NGO named ‘Janpower’. She currently lives in Switzerland. According to Rohini, Chandrashekhar hid the fact that he was married and allegedly exploited her by promising marriage. She claims that after he became an MP from Nagina, he started distancing himself from her. Rohini had also filed a complaint against Chandrashekhar with the Women’s Commission, but no action was taken. On the other hand, Chandrashekhar and his supporters have filed an FIR against Rohini. She has been running a campaign against him on social media for the past one year. Know about the Jantar Mantar incident... Cockroach Janata Party supporters' Parliament march, lathi-charge The supporters of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) organised a march from Jantar Mantar to Parliament on Monday, July 20. During the protest, which continued from 8 am to 5 pm, several clashes took place between protesters and police. The protest began at 8 am, and around 10 am, protesters broke barricades and marched towards Parliament. The protesters moved from Jantar Mantar through Parliament Street, Janpath crossing, War Memorial, Kartavya Path and Vijay Chowk before reaching near Parliament. When protesters attempted to enter Parliament, security was increased and the main gate was closed. Police used tear gas shells. Later in the evening, visuals of stone-pelting also surfaced. More than 50 police personnel and an equal number of protesters were injured. CJP alleged that police used lathi-charge and tear gas against unarmed protesters. Pictures of several injured people emerged during the action. Police cleared Jantar Mantar by 5 pm. However, around 11 pm, CJP supporters returned to Jantar Mantar and resumed their protest.

stories.title: 25,000 UP instructors to receive 9 years' pending arrears:Supreme Court dismisses state government's review plea
stories.summary: Around 25,000 instructors in Uttar Pradesh have received major relief from the Supreme Court. The court has ordered that instructors be paid a monthly honorarium of ₹17,000 along with arrears pending since 2017. On Thursday, the court upheld its February 4, 2026 judgment and dismissed the Uttar Pradesh government's review petition. Following the Supreme Court's order, the state government will now have to proceed with the payment of the revised honorarium and pending arrears. A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Prasanna B. Varale said there was no apparent legal error in the February 4, 2026 judgment that warranted a review. Demand for hearing in open court also rejected The Supreme Court also rejected the state government's application seeking an open court hearing of the matter. With this, all pending applications related to the case were also disposed of. Instructors will receive arrears from 2017 In its February 4, 2026 judgment, the Supreme Court had directed the state government to pay instructors a monthly honorarium of ₹17,000. It also ordered that arrears pending since 2017 be paid within the stipulated time frame. Around 25,000 instructors are currently working under Uttar Pradesh's Basic Education Department. Counsel for the instructors, Durga Tiwari, said that following the Supreme Court's latest order, the government must now begin the process of paying arrears in line with the original judgment.

stories.title: BJP MLA turns bus driver:Shouts 'Ayodhya, Ayodhya' to attract passengers in Mahoba
stories.summary: BJP MLA Brijbhushan Rajput, who held Minister Swatantra hostage, was seen in a new avatar on Thursday. He inaugurated a direct roadways bus service from Charkhari in Mahoba to Ayodhya Dham. Then he himself drove the bus for about 800 meters. During this, Charkhari MLA Brijbhushan Rajput stuck his hand out of the bus window and called out for passengers by shouting "Ayodhya... Ayodhya...". He said - Look, is there any passenger for Ayodhya? At this, the passengers sitting in the bus welcomed the MLA by clapping. A video of this entire incident has also surfaced. Before this, a 12-year-old student showed the green flag to the bus. Now the complete matter in detail The distance from Charkhari town to Ayodhya Dham is 372 kilometers. It takes approximately 7.5 hours to reach Ayodhya from here by car or bus. Since the construction of the Ram Temple, a large number of people from here go to Ayodhya for darshan. That's why Charkhari MLA Brijbhushan Rajput had been demanding the start of a direct bus service to Ayodhya for quite some time. His demand was fulfilled on Thursday. Brijbhushan Rajput says I can drive a bus, handcart, everything In the video, while driving the bus, the MLA is saying- I am not just any ordinary MLA, I can drive a bus, handcart, everything. To this, a passenger present in the bus said that you are driving the bus very well. ARM was also present in the bus. The MLA told him- Get its horns fixed properly. There should be no deficiency in any vehicle running on the road. The MLA said- The safety and facilities of the bus in which people from our area will travel must be better; that is most important. I drove a bus for the first time in my life, but I felt it necessary to check the arrangements myself for the safety of passengers. Says direct facility to Ramlala is a gift for the area While addressing the program held at the bus inauguration, MLA Brijbhushan Rajput said, “Ayodhya is the centre of faith for crores of people. It is a great achievement for devotees of Charkhari to get direct facility to reach Ramlala's court. Calling passengers for the bus going to Lord Ram's abode was a fortunate moment of my life.” The MLA expressed gratitude to UP's Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh for this bus service. He said, “This is not just a transport service, but an initiative to fulfil the religious sentiments and needs of the area residents that are several years old. This bus service will increase the number of devotees going to Ayodhya. The Bundelkhand region will also get a new identity from religious tourism.” Says we love Ram Lalla from our hearts MLA Brajbhushan Rajput said, “Lord Ram is the centre of faith for all of us. We have a lot of devotion towards the Lord. We love Lord Ram very much from our hearts. In such a situation, calling passengers for the bus going to Lord Ram's abode becomes a fortunate matter in itself. If we can be of any service to God, we consider ourselves very fortunate.” Who is Brijbhushan Rajput? BJP MLA from Charkhari (Mahoba) Brijbhushan Rajput was born on 28 May 1982 in Orai (Jalaun). His father Ganga Charan Rajput has been a Lok Sabha MP 3 times (1989, 1996, 1998) and a Rajya Sabha MP (2009). Brijbhushan Rajput married Kanak Lodhi on May 9, 2005. He has two sons. Brijbhushan Rajput inherited political confrontation. His father Ganga Charan Rajput was known for controversies and defections in UP politics. Ganga Charan Rajput has been in Janata Dal, BJP, Congress and BSP. He led several movements on electricity-water and OBC issues in Bundelkhand. On May 18, 2004, after UPA's victory, when there was talk of Sonia Gandhi becoming Prime Minister and she declined the post, a high-voltage drama took place outside the Congress office in Delhi. Ganga Charan Rajput climbed on the roof of a car, brandished a pistol and threatened while pointing it at his own temple that if Sonia Gandhi did not become PM, he would shoot himself.

stories.title: UP reel-making groom’s ‘three brides’ wedding sparks legal trouble:One bride found minor; 'All 4 of us will end our lives'
stories.summary: Three reel-making sisters who married a cameraman in Amroha are in the headlines. Hindu organisations are opposing this marriage. The police have also become active. On Thursday morning at 10 am, all four were called to the police station. Three hours later at 1 pm, the three brides arrived at the police station with their husband, where everyone appeared quite happy. The three brides told the police, “We did not marry under any pressure. All three of us are adults. We used to think that if we marry, we would marry into the same house, but we couldn't find such a house where there would be three boys of our age. That's why we married one boy. We will die but will not separate.” On the question of registering the marriage, they said, “Some marriages don't work even after registration. We are happy as we are, if someone asks us for proof then we will see.” The three sisters had married their cameraman on July 17 at Chamunda Mata Temple. The wedding video surfaced on Wednesday. 'Dainik Bhaskar' spoke with the three brides. Read the report… Havan-worship in temple, took seven rounds Alka (20 years), Devika (19 years) and Santosh (18 years) are sisters living in Dhauria village in Hasanpur Kotwali area. All three create video content on Instagram and Facebook. Alka and Santosh are real sisters, while Devika is their maternal aunt's daughter. Devika has been raised with Alka and Santosh since childhood. Vikas alias Vikku, a resident of Shyampuri village, is the cameraman for all three sisters. He had been working for the three girls for the past 6 months. He also played the role of husband in reels. All three sisters say that they always wanted to live together, but the family members were not agreeable. On July 17, all three married Vikas in a temple. Family members did not attend the wedding At the temple, the cameraman filled the vermilion in the parting of all three brides one by one, and the brides touched their husband's feet to seek his blessings. However, no one from either family attended the wedding. This wedding came to light when the video surfaced on Wednesday evening at 5 PM. The three sisters have defended themselves by releasing a video. They said, “In ancient times, there was King Dashrath who had three queens. So what wrong have we done?” Now read the conversation Dainik Bhaskar first spoke with the eldest sister Alka- Question: Are all three of you real sisters? Alka: Yes, one is a cousin sister, but we have grown up together since childhood, so we consider her as our own. Question: How did all three of you meet Vikas? Alka: We used to make videos on YouTube, so we needed characters. That's how we met him. Question: Is this marriage fake, done to increase followers? Alka: No, we have gotten married. All three of us don't want to live separately. Question: Have you registered the marriage? Alka: Some marriages don't work even after registration. We are married, we are happy. Otherwise, if someone asks us for proof of this thing, we will give it. Question: Can all three live with one husband? Have you made any plan? Alka: Our plan was already made beforehand. We had been thinking from before that if we get married, we would either do it in one house, but we didn't find such a house. That's why we did it with one boy. We will die, but we won't separate; we have been saying this from before. Everything happened with our consent and all four of us are very happy. Devika said- People talk, we cannot stop them The second sister Devika said - We three sisters are together. We are feeling very good. After marriage, there has been no problem between the four of us. Some people are opposing, many people are also supporting. Many people are speaking well, but some people are speaking badly. It's people's job to speak. We cannot stop them. Santosh said - We three were saved from death The third sister Santosh says that if we had separated, we might have died. We survived death and are together, and now we will always remain together. The family members wanted to get us married separately. We had told Vikas about this. He agreed to marry all three of us. Got married against parents' wishes All three sisters said - We got married against our parents' wishes, but now they have also agreed. Some Hindu organizations are raising questions. So how is our marriage against Sanatan? King Dashrath was also a Hindu. He also had three marriages. How can we be wrong? If we are criminals, then he was also wrong. Vikas has been living at his in-laws' place since the wedding It should be noted that Alka is a B.Tech second year student, while Devika and Santosh have passed 12th grade. Father Ramesh is a farmer. Vikas passed 12th grade this year. He now wants to pursue LLB. He is the youngest among three brothers. After the wedding, these four people are living at a relative's house. See 2 pictures after the wedding Household expenses will be managed through social media income After the wedding, on the question of expenses, all three brides said - We earn income from social media. We will work even harder in the future. There is also some land in our husband's name, which will cover the expenses. Police said - Action will be taken after checking documents Hasanpur police station in-charge Rajesh Tiwari said that three young women have married one young man. All three young women and the young man have been called to the police station. They are being interrogated. After examining the statements and age-related documents, further action will be taken in the matter.

stories.title: Varanasi woman dies by suicide after mother stops mobile use:Police bring down body from noose; forensic team arrives
stories.summary: In Varanasi, when her mother forbade her from using her mobile phone, the daughter locked herself in her room. Family members kept knocking on the door from outside, but the young woman did not open it. On Thursday at 12 noon, angry with her mother, the young woman hanged herself. Family members informed the police, after which the door was broken down. Inside, the young woman's body was found hanging from a hook. She was then taken down from the noose. The police called the forensic team. They took possession of the body, completed the inquest, and sent it for post-mortem. Now read the full story Hanuman Chaurasia lives with his family on rent in a house in Lallapura, under the Sigra police station area. His wife, son, and daughter Pooja Chaurasia (19) also live with them. One son and daughter are already married and live separately with their families. The whole family was troubled by the habit of using the phone Hanuman Chaurasia was busy preparing for his daughter Pooja's wedding, but the whole family was troubled by Pooja's habit of using her phone. In recent days, there were several arguments at home over talking on the phone all night, but Pooja was not ready to listen. Kept using the phone all night On Wednesday night, Pooja took her phone and went out of the room and kept using the phone all night. When her mother reprimanded her, she got angry, saying she was watching reels on social media. After this, when her mother expressed displeasure in the morning, an argument broke out between them. After this, Pooja went inside the house and locked herself in the room. Then, she placed a cylinder on the cot, made a noose with a dupatta in the fan hook, and hanged herself. Her mother kept screaming and shouting from the window, but Pooja did not listen at all. Police broke down the door and removed the body In a hurry, neighbours were called to try and break down the door, but the latch did not break. After this, Sigra police were called, and the door was broken. After this, ACP Chetganj Shubham Singh also reached the spot and gathered information. Family members said that the deceased Pooja was forbidden by her mother Savitri Chaurasia, from using her mobile phone late at night. She was one of two brothers and two sisters; one brother and one sister were already married. She was the third child and had studied up to class 5, after which she left school.

stories.title: Executive engineer slapped in Gorakhpur:Black helmet-clad attackers storm office and assault him
stories.summary: A case of assault and life-threatening attack on an Executive Engineer has come to light in the flood division office of Gorakhpur. The commotion continued in the office for about 20 minutes. The entire incident has been captured on the CCTV camera installed there. In it, the Executive Engineer is seen being slapped by a youth wearing a black helmet along with other people. The incident occurred on Thursday afternoon around 1 PM. Cantt police, who arrived upon receiving information, are investigating the matter. The Executive Engineer has accused a clerk from his own office of the assault. Executive Engineer Vipin Singh had gone to inspect the Flood Division office located in Padleganj, in the Cantt police station area, along with Chief Engineer Vikas Singh. It is alleged that during this time, the accused clerk came with his companions and started abusing. Upon protesting, the Executive Engineer was attacked. During this, there was an atmosphere of chaos in the office. Employees working in the office came screaming to intervene. Right in front of them, a youth wearing a black helmet slapped the Executive Engineer several times. After the incident, the accused left, threatening to kill him. The Executive Engineer alleges that the clerk is suspended in a case. Police from Cantt police station reached the spot and started an investigation. The accused who attacked are also being identified from the office's CCTV cameras, who had come with the clerk.

stories.title: 1.86 lakh UP teachers must take TET:Centre rejects state's demand; Jayant Chaudhary says no relaxation possible
stories.summary: Around 1.86 lakh teachers in Uttar Pradesh have received a major setback from the central government. Union Minister of State for Education Jayant Chaudhary has refused to grant exemption from the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). In response to a question asked in the Lok Sabha, he said, “The matter of passing TET is linked to a Supreme Court order, therefore no relaxation is possible at present. Old teachers will also not get any kind of relief.” The decision was announced after Congress MP from Karnataka E. Tukaram had asked a question on whether an amendment to Section 23 of the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 is being considered to provide relief to teachers appointed before TET was implemented. The Union Minister said, “The government is not bringing any such proposal at present, nor is any interim relief being considered.” Meanwhile, the UP government is going to conduct a special TET for teachers of the Basic Education Department soon. The government has asked the Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission, Prayagraj, to immediately provide a detailed action plan for the examination. Special Secretary Awadhesh Kumar Tiwari issued a letter in this regard on 21 July. The Selection Commission has been asked to soon provide the complete action plan for conducting special TET for both categories. Central minister says teacher recruitment is a matter of the state government Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary said, “Recruitment and service conditions of teachers are state subjects; therefore, data of such teachers is with state governments. The Supreme Court, in its judgment dated September 1, 2025, clarified that TET is the minimum qualification prescribed under Section 23 of the RTE Act 2009. TET is mandatory to become a teacher in schools covered under RTE.” While hearing review petitions filed thereafter, the Supreme Court on May 29, 2026 gave relief by extending the final date for passing TET from August 31, 2027 to August 31, 2028. This means teachers have got an additional one year. States ordered to conduct TET twice a year The Supreme Court also stated in its order that state governments and concerned authorities should attempt to conduct TET at least twice every year. There should be a gap of approximately 6 months between both examinations. This will provide teachers with adequate opportunity to fulfil the qualification. This means that now there is increased pressure on all states, including UP to conduct TET regularly. In UP, the TET examination was held in July. In this regard, the TET examination should now be conducted again in January 2027. 1.86 lakh teachers in UP fall under this order According to the UP Basic Education Department, there are approximately 1.86 lakh teachers who have not yet passed TET. A large number of these are teachers who were appointed before the TET system was implemented. This includes assistant teachers, teachers adjusted from Shiksha Mitras, teachers with old training, and teachers working in remote areas for a long time. These teachers argue that the RTE Act was passed in 2009 and implemented in UP in 2011. In such a case, how can this be applied to the recruitment of teachers who were already working before this. Why was there hope for relief? Teacher organisations had demanded that the RTE Act be amended to provide exemption to old teachers. Their argument was that experience should be considered as eligibility. They were talking about providing relief at least to teachers who had reached close to retirement. However, the central government has made it clear in Parliament, citing the Supreme Court's order, that it is not ready for any kind of amendments to the RTE. What Next? The UP government will have to conduct regular TET examinations as per the Supreme Court's directives. Teachers will have to be allowed to apply. Arrangements will have to be made to complete the qualification by August 31, 2028. Failing to do so, the services of such people will be considered terminated after the stipulated time period. Those who do not pass TET will also not get the benefit of promotion.

stories.title: Fake international call centre busted in Lucknow:Four, including uncle-nephew duo, arrested for targeting US citizens
stories.summary: Police in Lucknow's Vibhuti Khand area busted a fake call centre which targeted American citizens by posing as Apple customer support officials. Police have arrested four operators of the call centre. The role of 35 calling agents found at the scene is being investigated. During the operation, a large number of laptops, mobiles and other electronic devices were seized. DCP East Dr Diksha Sharma held a press conference on Thursday and informed that on the night of 22 July, Vibhuti Khand police station in-charge Upendra Singh was conducting vehicle checking in front of Jalwa Bar. During this time, an informer provided information about a fake call centre operating in flat number 420A on the fourth floor of Cyber Height building. After this, a raid was conducted at around 2.55 AM along with the crime team and the call centre was busted. Mastermind was running gang with relatives Police arrested Suraj Tripathi, a resident of Pratapgarh, his relatives Vivek Pandey and Rahul Tripathi, and Mumbai resident technical expert Akash Arun Datta alias Ricky from the spot. Investigation revealed that Suraj is the mastermind of the entire gang, while Akash operated the fake website and VOIP system. This is how they used to defraud people in America Investigation revealed that the gang promoted a fake Apple customer support website through s on Google. When calls came from America to the number given on the website, the calls reached the call centre located in Lucknow through voice over internet protocol (VOIP). Here, agents would identify themselves as customer support officers. After this, the call closers would extort money in the form of gift cards, gold, or cash by intimidating or luring victims by posing as officials from government departments like the FTC or the US Supreme Court. Money reached through hawala According to the police, gang members present in America would collect the extorted money. After this, the money was sent to Lucknow through hawala. Employees were also paid in cash, so that there would be no digital record of the transactions. During the raid, 35 workstations were found running in the call centre. Thirty-five calling agents were working here. Among them, the highest number of 10 agents were from Uttarakhand, 9 from Maharashtra, 3 each from Gujarat and Nagaland, two each from Assam and Manipur. Apart from this, agents from West Bengal, Telangana, Tripura, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Nepal were also working. Police are interrogating all of them and investigating their roles. Investigation of Calling Agents' Roles 35 calling agents were also found at the location. The police are interrogating them. The police are trying to find out from the arrested agents whether they were aware of the fraud or were employed and made to work as employees. Information including their bank accounts is being collected. Maternal uncle and nephew were running the fraud call centre Among the arrested accused, three are relatives. Rahul Tripathi is Suraj Tripathi's maternal uncle, while Vivek Pandey is the son of main accused Suraj Tripathi's paternal aunt. Suraj is a graduate, while Vivek Pandey has done a diploma. Rahul Tripathi has passed 12th grade and the fourth accused, Akash Arun Datta looked after field operations. All the fraudsters were committing fraud worth $4.000-$5,000 daily.
