stories.title: Are you eating flour or powdered stone?:Wheat ground with white stone in UP mills; undercover probe exposes racket
stories.summary: 'This is powdered white stone. It is mixed into flour to increase profits. In the coming years, it will make people so sick that even doctors will say- Brother, there's no treatment for you.' These are the words of Sonu Kumar, an operator at a flour mill near Agra. He alleges that factory owners mix powdered white stone into flour to boost profits. According to him, the adulterated flour is sold across the country under the names of well-known brands. A Dainik Bhaskar undercover reporter spent 25 days working as a labourer inside the flour mill. The reporter gained access to the section where the stone powder was allegedly mixed into the flour. Inside, there was a setup where, at the press of a button, the powdered stone was automatically blended into the flour. Posing as a worker, the Bhaskar reporter secretly recorded the entire setup and the alleged adulteration process using a hidden camera. Read the full investigation… In Firozabad, Bulandshahr and Aligarh, officials recently caught adulteration of stone in branded flour. When we investigated, we found that this black game of adulteration is going on in many factories. Even now, stone powder is being mixed in flour in factories in Hathras and Firozabad. We reached two factories in Hathras and Firozabad disguised as labourers. We built rapport with other workers. We asked contractors for work. After wandering for three days, we got work. On the first day, we lifted sacks of wheat. On the second day, we were put on duty to supervise wheat. Then we got the job of filling sacks with chaff. For the first two weeks, we continued working as labourers. By the third week, we won the supervisor's trust. Finally, we got duty at that secret place for which we had been labouring for 2 weeks. This was a room with various machines installed. In one machine, stone powder was filled, which was being mixed into the flour. The operator and labourers did the work of setting and monitoring the percentage of stone powder to be mixed. We have exposed that stones are being mixed in flour. But, who is involved in this game? On what scale is this work happening? To find this out, we now became flour traders. We met factory operator Sonu Kumar in Tundla. Sonu understands the intricacies of mixing stone powder in flour. We told Sonu that we have got a tender to supply flour in Rajasthan. We need to set up a factory, which we will get done through you. Sonu explained the entire game of adulteration- Reporter: How much stone powder should be mixed in flour... 20% or up to 30%? Sonu: Keep it below 10%, otherwise complaints start coming about the flour. Reporter: What is the maximum percentage that can be mixed? Sonu: Currently, 10% is running in the market. If there's to be no return, you can adulterate up to 15% to 20%. Reporter: Which powder is it? Sonu: Sunsilk, soapstone (a type of stone powder). When you go to buy that powder, taste it to check that it's not gritty. Second, it should be white because some come with a yellowish tint too. Reporter: After mixing stone powder, what difference does it make in the flour roti? Sonu: No, there's no difference. Reporter: In taste? Sonu: No difference in taste either; I've checked the roti made from it. Reporter: You've eaten it? Sonu: Yes, one has to eat it, brother. When we add the material, we check what result will come in the market, right? Actually, let me tell you one thing: this is poison. If we mix rice flour, at least that's grain. With this, in the coming time people will develop so many diseases that doctors will start refusing, saying Brother, there's no cure for you. What is the math of profiteering? To find out, we expressed our desire to meet the flour factory owner. Operator Sonu introduced us to Raman Kumar, who runs a brand called Maharaja Bhog Atta in Tundla, Firozabad. Raman: If you mix 9-10% powder, you will get 70-80 paise per kilogram of flour in your pocket. Reporter: 70-80 paise or even more than that. Raman: Yes, you will get a profit of one rupee. Reporter: Meaning, ₹100 profit per quintal. Raman: Yes, what else? If 70-80 quintals of goods (flour mixed with stone powder) are sold daily, then there will be a profit of ₹7-8K. (Flour factory owner Raman showed adulterated flour) Raman: These are my goods; this number one is running. It's going for ₹28 per kilo. Operator Sonu: My father is running the machine; no problem. Raman: Everyone does mixing (adulteration of stone powder in flour). Otherwise there's no profit. You tell me - wheat is coming at ₹25 per kilo and flour is selling at ₹26.50 per kilo. Only ₹1.50 difference, whereas the cost in this is ₹1.70 per kilo. Like this, 20 paise more is going from us. That's why we're mixing 10% powder. Reporter: Can you keep the powder in the factory? Raman: Privacy has to be maintained. Don't know when, which officer might come? Although whoever comes, comes to take money. They take ₹5,000 every month and go. Now know the mathematics of profiteering by mixing stone powder Wheat rate: ₹2,500 per quintal White stone powder rate: ₹1,400 per quintal Grinding and labour cost: ₹170 per quintal With 10% adulteration Cost: ₹2,560 per quintal Flour will be sold in market: ₹2,700 per quintal Profit: ₹140 per quintal Available in market: Most companies are doing this much adulteration. With 20% adulteration - Cost: ₹2,450 per quintal Flour will be sold in market: ₹2700 per quintal Profit: ₹250 per quintal Available in market: This type of flour is being consumed in large events, community feasts, and mid-day meals. Now know, how much is the profit? A flour mill has four grinders. They grind 100 quintals of wheat in 10 hours. Then the profit for one day- At 10% adulteration: ₹14,000 At 20% adulteration: ₹25,000 They are earning a profit of up to ₹90 lakh per year from one flour mill. How is the stone powder setup installed? To answer this question, we met mechanic Sunil Kumar through a source. Sunil installs setups for mixing stone powder in flour factories. Sunil called us near Shahdara Police Chowki in Agra. Reporter: Need to set up a plant, will you install the adulteration setup? Sunil: I will arrange it in such a way that even if any flying team comes, or food product officials come, they won't find anything. Reporter: What rate will stone powder be available at? Sunil: This will be available for ₹12 to 14 per kilo. How does stone powder come here from Rajasthan? To answer this, we spoke with Vimal Agarwal, a dealer in Hathras. He told us that he would supply us with as much powder as we need to mix in flour. Reporter: We need it for mixing in flour. Is this powder being used in flour? Vimal: Yes, our powder is being used in flour. Everywhere (gesturing about money), this works. Many flour mill operators are mixing it. This is soil from the mountains; you also know this. Businessman Vimal showed us samples of stone powder. He claimed that there is no shortage of it. Vimal took us to the warehouse, where the stock of the powder was stored. Now know, what is white stone powder? This powder is called talc or soapstone. It comes from mines in some districts of Rajasthan. It is used in cosmetic items, face cream, plastic granules, paint, paper, and statue making. It cannot be eaten, but is being mixed in flour for profit. Doctors say- eating stone powder can damage liver and kidneys Lucknow's senior physician Dr. Gyan Tiwari said- stone powder has high calcium carbonate content. If you eat roti made from this flour, it will get stuck in the intestines. This damages the digestive system. Most people are facing such problems these days. Questions sent to Minister Ashish Patel; he did not respond In this matter, we tried to speak with Consumer Protection Minister Ashish Patel. On the first day, his phone was answered, and when the representative asked questions, we provided them. After that, we called 12 times in 7 days, but each time we were not allowed to speak, making excuses that Minister Patel was busy. We also sent questions to PRO Amaresh asking for answers, but he too did not provide any responses. Does your flour contain stone powder? Identify it like this Serving poor quality flour in mid-day meals We tested the flour used in mid-day meals at 3 schools in Western UP. We filled a glass with water and mixed a little flour in it. When doing this, pure flour dissolves in water, and flour with stones settles at the bottom. Here, at all three places, the flour settled at the bottom of the water. This made it clear that the flour being used in children's mid-day meals contains stone powder. Rotis made from this flour mixed with stone powder are being fed to children. Flour for mid-day meals is being purchased at ₹28 per kilogram.

Man dies after Jagannath chariot collides with high tension line:Accident amidst rain in Meerut; 11 devotees burnt, 2 thousand people were present
stories.summary: In Meerut on Friday, during the Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath, the chariot touched an 11,000 volt high-tension line. One devotee died due to electrocution. 11 people were burnt. The accident occurred in Parikshitgarh town. This Rath Yatra was being taken out amidst rain. About 2,000 devotees were participating in it. The injured have been admitted to the hospital. According to eyewitnesses, as soon as the current struck, several people sitting on the chariot fell down. There was screaming and crying at the spot. Stampede-like conditions arose. Devotees started running here and there to save their lives. See two pictures- The Katha concluded on Thursday evening A procession and Katha program of Lord Jagannath was organized at Om Public School in Parikshitgarh town. Five days ago, a grand procession of Lord Jagannath was taken out in the city. After this, a religious discourse was being organized by Maharaj Rohit Risaliya Vrindavan. The discourse concluded on Thursday evening. On Friday afternoon, Lord Jagannath's chariot procession was taken out in the city with bands playing. This accident occurred as soon as the procession started. Chariot procession started without worship rituals Lord Jagannath was already seated on the chariot. Preparations for worship rituals were underway so that the chariot procession could begin properly. During this time, as soon as it started raining, some people began pulling the chariot rope and taking it away. Some devotees protested against this, but they didn't listen to anyone. They started taking the chariot towards the Rajwahe track. Here, the top of the chariot touched the 11000 volt high tension line passing overhead and electric current flowed down. One youth died, 11 devotees burnt In the accident, Sachin (30), a resident of Parikshitgarh, was severely burnt. He was taken to the Community Health Center, where doctors declared him dead. Meanwhile, 11 burnt devotees have been admitted to the Community Health Center and private hospitals. Sachin used to support his family by doing labor work. His father Nandkishore also does labor work. The family includes his mother, younger brother Vishal, and two sisters Prachi and Vishakha. There was chaos at home after Sachin's death. The condition of some of the injured is said to be critical. Among the burnt people are 11 including Priyanshu, Vivek, Manish residents of Aurangabad, Shivam, Yash, Pihu residents of Parikshitgarh, Nimesh resident of Ahmadpuri, Maharaj Bharatdas from Lakhimpur Kheri, Rajesh Mishra. Now what did the eyewitnesses say, let's know- Police had raised objection regarding the 14 feet height As soon as information about the accident was received, Rural SP Abhijit Kumar reached the spot. Police from several stations also reached the incident site along with him. Officials inspected the incident site and gathered information about the causes of the accident. According to police, this time the main patron of the katha was social worker Atul Sharma. This katha has been taking place in the village for the past seven years. Police are investigating how the chariot came in contact with the high-tension line and also looking into safety standards. Some villagers who reached the mortuary said that every year the organizers and venue of the katha change. This time the responsibility of organizing was with Atul Sharma. When this chariot was prepared, its height was approximately 14 feet. Police had raised objections to this, but the organizers did not listen. DM said - Will investigate and take action DM VK Singh said - About 11 people came in contact with the electric current in the accident. All the injured were immediately taken to CHC and district hospital. Most of them are in stable condition and are out of danger. One woman has been referred for better treatment. Teams from police, health department and administration are present at the spot. The entire matter is being investigated and necessary action is being taken.

stories.title: Explosion rocks firecracker factory, 2 dead, 2 missing:Body parts are thrown 100 metres away, houses walls shaken
stories.summary: A powerful explosion ripped through a firecracker factory in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur on Friday evening, killing two workers and leaving two others missing. Sutli bombs have reportedly been manufactured at the factory for the past five years. At the time of the blast, 24 workers were on duty, of whom 20 escaped safely. The explosion was so intense that the victims' bodies were torn apart. One body was recovered from beneath the factory debris, while the other was found nearly 100 metres away near a field. The body was badly mutilated, with the face beyond recognition and body parts scattered across the area. According to the village head, the blast occurred at around 5 pm. The impact was so strong that walls of houses in the village, located about 500 metres away, shook. Police, district officials and fire brigade teams are carrying out rescue operations at the site. The firecracker factory, spread across nearly 10 bighas of land, is located on the outskirts of Naya Gaon in Gangoh police station area, around 54 km from the district headquarters. Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Abhinandan confirmed the two deaths. He said part of the factory collapsed and caught fire after the explosion. Rescue teams are continuing to search the debris for those still trapped. The exact cause of the blast is yet to be determined. 2 pictures related to the incident

stories.title: Class 12 student dies by suicide:Shoots himself in head; father brings rifle home the previous night
stories.summary: An 18-year-old boy shot himself dead on Friday morning in Agra. He was an intermediate student and the only son of his parents. His father had brought a licensed rifle home on Thursday night. Around 10 AM, the student locked himself in a room and shot himself in the head, blowing off half of his face. Hearing the sound of firing, family members and people from the vicinity rushed to the spot, but by then he had already died. The family is in deep shock due to the child's suicidal act. The reason why he did it has not come to light. Police have questioned people. See 3 pictures... The father had arrived home at 2:30 AM, the son himself had opened the door. The incident is from Teachers Colony in Bah police station area. Aditya Sharma (18 years old), who lived here, was a 12th-grade student. His mother, Dolly, is a homemaker. His father, Sudeep Sharma, is a security guard in a private company in Rajasthan. He often stays out for work. According to family members, Sudeep Sharma reached home around 2:30 AM on Thursday late night. At that time, Aditya was awake. When his father arrived, he was the one who opened the door. Sudeep had placed the rifle on top of a trunk in the room and then went to sleep. He had no idea at that time that such a big accident would happen just a few hours later. Didn't go to school in the morning, locked himself in the room On Friday morning, Aditya did not go to school. He was sleeping in the room on the roof. Family members thought he might be resting due to staying up late. After some time, when his mother went to wake Aditya, he locked the door from inside. The mother came down from the roof and got busy with her work. Parents rushed upon hearing the gunshot Around 10 AM, Aditya shot himself with a rifle. The firing caused chaos in the house. His parents and neighbors rushed towards the roof. The police were informed. When the police broke down the door and entered, Aditya was found covered in blood. Half of his face was missing. Family said - he was treated for depression Father Sudeep said, Aditya was in depression two-three years ago. He used to get angry over small things. He was treated for it. Then he got better. In recent days, he was behaving normally. There was no problem. We don't understand why he did this. Police seized the rifle Police have taken possession of the rifle. The forensic team has also collected evidence from the spot. Currently, no suicide note has been recovered from the crime scene. Station in-charge Devi Prasad Tiwari said that according to the initial investigation, it is a case of suicide. However, further action will be taken only on the basis of the post-mortem report, forensic investigation, and other evidence.

stories.title: 34 questions for Shri Ram Trust CEO:Form asks candidates if they are ‘staunch Hindu’ or a believer
stories.summary: Information has been sought from applicants for the CEO post of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on 34 questions. A three-member selection committee has provided an online Google Form to all applicants to fill out. It asks for information ranging from personal details to their administrative capabilities and crowd management. The selection committee has to prepare a list of three best applicants out of 5200 and submit it to the Trust before September 2. Personal and General Information In nine points, the applicant is asked for their personal information. This includes the applicant's full name, date of birth, age, and contact details (address, city, state, pin code, mobile number, email). Additionally, they will have to state their proficiency in Hindi and English. Options are provided for all answers. Educational and professional qualification The applicant will have to state their highest educational qualification. For instance, whether they are a graduate or hold any other qualification including a PhD. Are they currently employed somewhere or have they retired? The full details of that organisation must be provided. They will also have to state their total experience in the corporate, administrative, or managerial sector. For this, they will have to choose an option of 20 to 30 years or more. They will also have to state their field of work. Such as whether they are associated with corporate, defence, administration, bureaucracy, public sector undertakings, banking, IT, or any other sector. How many employees have they led so far? For this, they need to choose an option from 1000 to 5000 or more. How much experience in managing large events? Many large events take place throughout the year in Ayodhya. Millions of people gather for these. In such a situation, crowd management skills will be crucial. For this, the selection committee has asked applicants which large event they have previously operated or managed. Applicants will have to choose the option indicating how many people participated in those events: 5,000 to 20,000 or more. They will also have to state how many days the event lasted, whether it was 1 to 5 days or more than that. The applicant will also have to state in which year they led the said large event, the name of that event, and their own role played in it. Questions related to social, religious, and spiritual beliefs The applicant will have to state whether they have previously been associated with any social or religious organization or any monastery-temple. If yes, what was the duration of their experience? For this, an option of 1 to 10 years or more will have to be selected. What was the size of the said religious or social institution? The applicant will also have to state whether they are a staunch Hindu or a devout Hindu. Applicant must state their vision, plan, and references For Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra, the applicant will also have to state their vision, action plan, and suggestions. If the applicant has any specific or extraordinary achievement, they will have to state it. To verify their professional, social, and religious experiences, they will have to provide the names and contact details of at least 2 reputable individuals as references. Final selection will be under the supervision of the Center and RSS A senior member of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust said - The final selection of the CEO for this sensitive post will be under the direct supervision of the Central Government and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). The person who will sit on the CEO's chair will be someone on whom both the government and the Sangh agree. Not only that, in the future, the consent of the Center and the Sangh will play an important role in the selection of the CEO office staff.

stories.title: Officer slapped during inspection:Suspended clerk attacks official, says, ‘Take out the pistol, let’s kill him’
stories.summary: An executive engineer was allegedly assaulted inside the Irrigation Department's Flood Division office in Gorakhpur while carrying out an official inspection. According to the complaint, a suspended clerk, an assistant engineer, and another man entered the office, surrounded him and repeatedly slapped him. The engineer alleged that during the assault, the suspended clerk shouted, “Take out the pistol, let's kill him today. I won't spare him.” The altercation continued for around 20 minutes before officials and staff intervened and brought the situation under control. The incident took place at around 1 pm on Thursday, while a video of the assault surfaced on Friday. Engineer alleges attack linked to suspension of clerk The Executive Engineer alleged that he had suspended the clerk following a departmental inquiry and had also ordered his salary to be withheld. He claimed the assault was carried out in retaliation for those disciplinary actions. Based on his complaint, police have registered a case against two named and four unidentified accused. 'Office staff saved my life,' says Executive Engineer According to Executive Engineer Vipin Singh, he and Chief Engineer Vikas Singh were inspecting the Flood Division office in the Cantt police station area on Thursday afternoon when the incident occurred. Vipin Singh said- While I was inspecting the office, Irrigation Department clerk Deepak Pandey arrived with his associates. They pushed past the Chief Engineer to reach me and began abusing me. He added- When I objected, they started assaulting me. A man wearing a black helmet slapped me first, after which all three repeatedly hit me. The office staff somehow managed to save my life. The accused fled after threatening to kill me. I immediately went to Cantt police station and lodged a written complaint. Clerk had allegedly issued earlier threats The Executive Engineer further alleged that clerk Deepak Pandey had threatened him on previous occasions in January and April, including warning that he would have him abducted from his home through another employee. He said he had reported those threats to the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), District Magistrate (DM) and Commissioner. Following a departmental inquiry, Deepak Pandey was suspended on 30 April, and his salary was withheld. Police begin investigation CO Cantt Abha Singh said a case has been registered based on the Executive Engineer's complaint. She said both parties will be questioned and statements will also be recorded from employees who were present in the office at the time of the incident. Further action will be taken after the investigation is completed.

stories.title: Heavy rain puts Uttar Pradesh on edge:Flood alert in 54 districts, 10 rivers overflow; crocodile enters village in Lakhimpur Kheri
stories.summary: Continuous rainfall over the past 15 days has begun to worsen flood conditions across Uttar Pradesh, with more than 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Yamuna, flowing above normal levels. The Hindon in Baghpat and Noida, the Ganga in Budaun, the Ghaghara in Ayodhya, Gonda and Ballia, and the Gandak in Kushinagar are all flowing above the danger mark. Meanwhile, authorities have issued a rain alert for 54 districts on Friday. Dam gates opened, floodwater enters villages In Sonbhadra, three gates of the Kanhar Dam were opened after the reservoir's water level rose significantly. In Sitapur, around 320,000 cusecs of water were released from the Banbasa, Girija and Ghaghara barrages, causing the Sharda and Ghaghara rivers to swell. Floodwater has entered several villages, and in one village, water is flowing over an unpaved road, forcing residents to travel by boat. Crocodile spotted on road, riverbank erosion intensifies In Lakhimpur Kheri, a crocodile was seen running along a village road after floodwaters spread into nearby areas. In Basti, severe erosion has been reported along the banks of the Saryu River, with several trees collapsing into the river. Rain in Lucknow, cloud cover across more than 30 districts Light rain was recorded in Lucknow and Gonda on Friday morning. Cloudy conditions prevailed in Barabanki, Agra, and more than 30 other districts across the state. On Thursday, an average of 2.2 mm of rainfall was recorded across 42 districts, with Sonbhadra receiving the highest rainfall at 13 mm. See 3 photos- CM Yogi orders officials to remain on the ground Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to stay in the field and closely monitor the situation. He instructed them to provide all possible assistance to people affected by heavy rain, flooding and lightning. Rainfall to ease for three days before monsoon strengthens again According to Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, rainfall activity is expected to decline over the next three days. With the monsoon trough shifting southwards and the low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal weakening, rainfall activity will temporarily reduce. Monsoon activity has currently shifted towards west-central India. Weather conditions are expected to change again after three to four days, and the monsoon is likely to become active once more from 26–27 July, bringing widespread rainfall.

stories.title: Varanasi Senior DMM taken into CBI custody:Raids conducted at home and office; action taken over alleged bribe of ₹1.70 lakh
stories.summary: CBI's Lucknow Anti-Corruption Unit has taken Nitesh Agarwal, Senior Divisional Materials Manager (DMM) of the Banaras Division of North Eastern Railway, into custody over allegations of accepting a ₹1.70 lakh bribe. The action followed a complaint lodged by a businessman. On Thursday evening, the CBI team reached the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) office and carried out searches at Nitesh Agarwal's office and residence. Family members and office staff were also questioned as part of the investigation.

stories.title: CM Yogi hears grievances of 150 people at Janta Darshan:Assures swift action on all complaints
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who is on a three-day visit to Gorakhpur, once again interacted with members of the public during 'Janta Darshan' on Friday morning. This was the second consecutive day that he held the public grievance session. The Chief Minister met around 150 people, listened to their concerns and assured them that effective action would be taken on every complaint. He instructed officials present at the event to ensure that all grievances received during the Janta Darshan are resolved promptly. CM personally collects applications, directs officials on the spot On Friday morning, the Chief Minister personally met people seated outside the Mahant Digvijaynath Smriti Bhawan in the Gorakhnath Temple complex. He listened to each person individually, collected their written applications and issued directions to the officials standing nearby regarding the resolution of their grievances. Applications relating to various issues were forwarded to the concerned administrative and police officials, with instructions to ensure fair and time-bound action. Orders strict action on crime and land encroachment complaints Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed police officials to take strict action on complaints related to crime and illegal land encroachment. He also reviewed applications seeking financial assistance for medical treatment and instructed officials to expedite the preparation of hospital cost estimates. The Chief Minister assured applicants that once the estimates are received, the government will release the required financial assistance without delay. Several women attended the Janta Darshan with their children. During the interaction, the Chief Minister greeted the children warmly, blessed them and distributed chocolates. The Chief Minister assured applicants that once the estimates are received, the government will release the required financial assistance without delay. Cattle respond to CM's familiar voice at Gorakhnath Temple cowshed During his stay at Gorakhnath Temple on Friday morning, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath visited the temple's gaushala (cowshed) and spent time feeding the cattle. While walking through the cowshed, he called several cows by their names. Familiar with his voice, the animals came running towards him. The Chief Minister affectionately stroked their foreheads and fed them jaggery by hand. He also offered jaggery to other cows and Nandi housed in the temple cowshed. Before leaving, he instructed the cowshed staff to continue ensuring proper care and welfare of the cattle.

stories.title: Village chief's lawyer son shot dead at restaurant:Was having dinner with friends when the attacker quietly approached, shot in the head
stories.summary: A village pradhan's son was shot dead at point-blank range inside a restaurant in Jhansi on Thursday night, triggering panic in the busy commercial area. Sanjay Singh had arrived at The Mad Kitchen restaurant near Elite Chowraha in the Nawabad police station area around 9.30 pm with four friends for dinner. While they were eating, an armed assailant walked in, placed a pistol against Sanjay's head and fired a single shot. Gunman escapes on waiting motorcycle, victim dies in hospital After carrying out the attack, the shooter ran to the restaurant's parking area, where an accomplice was waiting on a motorcycle. The two fled the scene before police arrived. Sanjay's friends rushed him to the medical college for treatment, but he succumbed to his injuries at around 1 am. Police have launched an investigation and are examining CCTV footage from the area to identify the attackers. LLB student and court clerk was living in Jhansi Sanjay Singh aka Sanju (33), the son of village head Ramdevi, was a resident of Haiwatpura village under the Garautha police station limits in Jhansi district. According to family members, Ramdevi has three children. Her elder son Sarvesh and daughter Rachna are married, while Sanjay was unmarried. Worked with advocate while completing law degree Sanjay had been living at a relative's house near Nandanpura in Jhansi for the past six years while pursuing his LLB. Alongside his studies, he worked as a clerk for Advocate Dashrath Singh at the district court. It was there that he became friends with Shivam, who was also employed in the same office. Returned from Datia temple before fatal shooting Sanjay Singh had returned from a visit to the Pitambara Peeth temple in Datia just hours before he was shot dead, according to his friend Shivam. Shivam said, “The group left the court around 4.30 pm on Thursday. Advocate Narayan Ojha, who had come to Jhansi from Chandauli, wanted to visit the temple. Sanjay, Shivam, Narayan Ojha and Advocate Dashrath Singh travelled to Datia by car and returned after offering prayers.” Gunman opened fire as friends finished dinner On their way back, the group stopped for dinner at The Mad Kitchen restaurant near Elite Chowk. Sanjay also called his friend Dharmendra, and the five of them were dining together. Shivam said, “We had almost finished eating when a young man dressed in black walked in and suddenly opened fire.” He added, “At first, we couldn't understand what had happened. When I looked at Sanjay, he stood up briefly and then collapsed. He had been shot in the head, and blood was flowing.” Guard tried to stop gunman, attacker escaped on number plate-less bike According to Sanjay's friend Shivam, the shooter fled the restaurant while brandishing his pistol after opening fire. A security guard stationed in the parking area attempted to intercept the attacker, but he escaped on a motorcycle driven by an accomplice. The bike reportedly had no number plate. Shivam said neither he nor his friends had seen the assailant before. Panic at restaurant as diners fled after gunshot Restaurant owner Vansh said, “The gunshot triggered panic among customers, many of whom abandoned their meals and rushed out of the premises.” He added, “A crowd soon gathered outside the restaurant, and the police were alerted. Officers from Nawabad police station reached the scene and launched an investigation.” Police are now examining CCTV footage from the restaurant and nearby locations to identify the attackers and trace their escape route. Family says Sanjay had no known rivalry Sanjay Singh's family rushed to Jhansi after learning about the murder. During questioning by the police his elder brother Sarvesh said that the family had no known enmity with anyone and was unaware of any motive behind the attack. He said, “There was no ongoing dispute related to the village pradhan's post and that the family had not received any threats.” Victim had been living in Jhansi for six years According to Sarvesh, “Sanjay had been residing in Jhansi for the past six years and only visited his native village occasionally.” He added, “Besides pursuing his law studies and working at the district court, he was also involved in land-related work. We had no idea who carried out the shooting or what prompted the attack.” Three police teams deployed, CCTV footage under scrutiny Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) B.B.G.T.S. Murthy said, “Multiple police teams, including the Special Operations Group (SOG), have been assigned to investigate the murder.” He said, “Officers are analysing CCTV footage from the restaurant and nearby areas to identify the gunman and trace his movements before and after the attack.” Police claim key leads, hunt for accused continues The SSP said, “Investigators have already obtained some crucial leads and are actively pursuing them.” He added, “We are confident the case will be cracked soon.” However, despite the ongoing search operation, the accused had not been traced till now.

stories.title: 'Our husband is our God,' say reel-making sisters:Married to stay together in Amroha, turned down a government employee's proposal
stories.summary: “Vikas has saved us sisters, he is like God for us. Papa had found a boy with a government job for didi, but we want to stay with Vikas only. We married him for his love. Some people think we did this for social media content and views. Let us tell you that our videos already get a lot of views.” This is what the 3 sisters who married a cameraman in Amroha say. The sisters made and posted a video. They say, “Since the wedding, people are asking all kinds of questions. We want to tell everyone that we are happy and together. Everyone should accept this.” The three sisters made a video to respond to people Hasanpur Kotwali area residents Alka (20), Devika (19) and Santosh (18) are from Dhauriya village and are real sisters. All three married their cameraman Vikas in a temple on July 17. After the wedding video surfaced, people have been commenting and asking various questions. To answer these questions, they have created and shared a six-minute video. The three sisters were already famous on social media The reel-making sisters have an account on Instagram under the name Rajput Girl. They have posted 981 posts so far. They have 4.72 lakh followers. Until 16 July, funny videos were posted on this account, which received views in millions. Posted 12 videos after the wedding, got 40 million views In the Instagram videos, sometimes all three sisters appeared together, sometimes they posted separately. Cameraman Vikas also often appeared in their videos. Since the wedding, they have posted 12 videos so far, which have received 40 million views. The three sisters say, “We also thought a lot initially. We looked for homes where we could find 3 boys. But that didn't happen. Somewhere there were two boys, somewhere one boy was quite young. After all paths were closed, we chose this option. We married our cameraman.” They say being short doesn't make someone a minor Alka says, “Some people are saying that our youngest sister is a minor. Let us tell you that she became an adult last year itself. Some people have short height. Neha Kakkar is 4 feet tall, so will you people call her a minor too? Get our blood test done through the government. If someone's face looks childlike, then will you people keep calling them a minor for 100 years?” Groom said they don't need my love Cameraman Vikas, who married all three sisters, says, "I could have married just one of them if I wanted. But their situation was not like that. They wanted to stay together. I am just a means to keep them together. They don't need my love, there is already a lot of love among them. They said, “Our videos already have a lot of views” In response to those commenting on the marriage, the three sisters say, “When our family has accepted us, you people should also accept. We had only two options, either die or live together. Vikas saved us. He is God for us. We have gotten married and are happy. If you think we did this for content, then look at our account. Our videos were already getting a lot of views.” It should be noted that after the wedding video surfaced, Hindu organisations have objected to it. The police have also become active. On the morning of Thursday, July 23, at 10 AM, the three sisters and their husband were called to the police station. There, all four were interrogated for 3 hours. Married of our own free will, police told All three brides told the police, “We did not marry under any pressure. All three of us are adults. We will die, but will not separate. On the question of registering the marriage, they said that some marriages don't work even after registration. We are happy as we are. If anyone asks us for proof, then we will see. After questioning, the police let all four go home.”

stories.title: Why no consensus on Ram Mandir Trust general secretary:RSS-VHP back different names; announcement delayed as 3 names emerge for 2 posts
stories.summary: Differences have emerged within the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust over the appointment of its next General Secretary, with the RSS and the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) backing different candidates for the post. Krishna Mohan, who is currently serving as the Acting General Secretary, is reportedly the RSS's preferred choice, with several office-bearers supporting his candidature. However, a section of the Trust members has proposed the name of VHP International General Secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra for the position. Decision on three vacant posts deferred until September The Trust also failed to reach a consensus on two other vacant positions, with the names of litterateur Yatindra Mohan Mishra, Ayodhya saint Raghavacharya and Mithilesh Nandini Sharan under consideration. While some members have backed Yatindra Mohan Mishra, others have expressed support for Mithilesh Nandini Sharan. With no agreement emerging, the Trust has decided to defer all three appointments to allow time for wider consultations. According to sources, efforts are underway to build a consensus, and the final decision is expected to be announced during the Trust's meeting scheduled for September 2. Trust meeting convened to fill General Secretary and member vacancies The July 22 meeting of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust was convened primarily to appoint a new General Secretary and fill vacant positions within the Trust. Acting General Secretary Krishna Mohan had issued the meeting notice to all Trust members on July 7. According to the notice, the meeting was scheduled to be held in two phases. No consensus despite discussion on five names The first session, which began at 3 pm, focused on filling the vacant posts. Trust members discussed the proposed candidates, with the understanding that appointments would be announced only if a consensus was reached. During the hour-long deliberations on Wednesday, five names were considered for the vacant positions. However, the members failed to arrive at a unanimous decision, prompting the Trust to defer the appointments until a broader consensus is achieved. RSS, VHP lobby for their candidates in closed-door discussions The RSS reportedly made behind-the-scenes efforts to build consensus over all three vacant positions in the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. According to sources, the exercise was coordinated by RSS Eastern Region Pracharak Anil Kumar, who held a confidential meeting with key Trust members to discuss a strategy for securing support for the Sangh's preferred candidates. The Trust meeting began at 3 pm at Maniram Cantonment under the chairmanship of Mahant Nritya Gopal Das. Deliberations centred on appointing a new General Secretary and filling vacant Trust member positions. VHP stakes claim to General Secretary's post During the meeting, some members proposed confirming Acting General Secretary Krishna Mohan, an Indian Forest Service (IFS) officer and former regional coordinator for Eastern Uttar Pradesh, as the permanent General Secretary. However, differences soon emerged. While one section argued that the post should now go to an RSS nominee, others maintained that the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP), which played a key role in the Ram Temple movement, deserved to retain the position. VHP International General Secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra's name was formally proposed for the post. Bagra, who had attended the Trust's July 7 meeting, had also arrived in Ayodhya ahead of the July 22 meeting. Despite sustained efforts to secure approval for his candidature, the members failed to reach a consensus, leaving the appointment unresolved. Trust defers appointments after disagreement over two member posts The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust also failed to finalise appointments to two vacant member positions, with multiple names emerging during the discussions. One vacancy arose after Dr. Anil Mishra resigned on June 26 following the donation theft controversy, while the other was created after the death of Ayodhya's titular king, Bimalendra Mohan Pratap Mishra. Differences among the Trust members prevented a final decision on either post. Three names proposed, consensus remains elusive As both vacancies had previously been held by residents of Ayodhya, members agreed that the new appointees should also be from the temple town. Mahant Dinendra Das of the Nirmohi Akhara proposed the name of litterateur Yatindra Mohan Mishra, son of the late Bimalendra Mohan Pratap Mishra, describing him as an honest and widely respected figure with a literary background. The names of Ayodhya saints Raghavacharya and Mithilesh Nandini Sharan were also put forward. Raghavacharya serves as the President of the Ramlala Sadan Devasthan Trust and the Peethadhishwar of Shridham Math, Ramvarnashram, while Mithilesh Nandini Sharan is regarded as a respected scholar and is considered close to both the RSS and the VHP. With three candidates in contention for two positions, the Trust could not reach a consensus and decided to postpone the appointments until a broader agreement is achieved. Trust aims to finalise appointments at September 2 meeting The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust is expected to take a final decision on filling its vacant posts at the next meeting, likely to be held on September 2. Speaking to the media after the July 22 meeting, Trust Treasurer Govind Dev Giri said the appointments had been deferred and would be finalised in the next round of deliberations. By then, the Trust is also expected to shortlist three candidates for the post of its new Chief Executive Officer (CEO). Focus shifts to building consensus on remaining vacancies According to sources, there is relatively little disagreement over the candidature of Bajrang Lal Bagra for the General Secretary's post. The main challenge lies in reaching a consensus on the two vacant Trust member positions. The Trust plans to continue consultations over the next two weeks and will take a final decision only after a broad agreement is achieved. If consensus remains elusive, the appointments may be decided through a formal vote among the Trust members.

Answer: There are 4 major political reasons for this Question-3: How much will BJP be harmed by this action on the university? stories.title: Jantar Mantar lathi-charge lookalike found in Ghaziabad:Says he is receiving death threats; TMC MP had called him a 'hired goon'
stories.summary: A video showing a baton charge during a student protest at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, on 20 July 2026 has gone viral on social media. In the footage, a young man in plain clothes can be seen carrying what appears to be a police baton. Social media users claimed the man was Honey Dagar, a resident of Ghaziabad. They alleged that although he is not a Delhi Police officer, he was seen wielding a baton alongside police personnel during the crackdown. The claim also drew political attention, with Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Mahua Moitra questioning the identity of the man and asking whether he was a hired goon. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Honey Dagar, who categorically denied the allegation. That is not me. The person may resemble me to some extent, but it isn't me. I run a gym in Ghaziabad. Since that day, my name, address, mobile number and details of my gym have been circulated on social media. He said the fallout has been severe. My family and I began receiving death threats. Around 30 men came to my gym and threatened me. I had to shut the gym for several days. Read the full conversation- 'My business has stopped, and I'm receiving death threats' Honey Dagar said the harassment began on the morning of 21 July. When I woke up, I saw abusive messages on Instagram. People called me an agent of an organisation and threatened to kill and assault me. He said the abuse continued across multiple platforms. When I opened WhatsApp, I found I was being trolled there as well. Initially, I had no idea why people were abusing me. Later, I realised that my name and address were being shared on social media, claiming I was the person involved in the baton charge at Jantar Mantar. Honey insisted he has no connection with the Delhi Police. I have never served in the Delhi Police. No one in my family is in the Delhi Police. I have never even visited Jantar Mantar, nor have I ever had any dispute with anyone. He said social media users have been posting his personal details—including his name, address, mobile number, village and gym address, as if they belonged to the man seen in the viral video. People are abusing me because of mistaken identity. Gym shut after men arrived to threaten him Fearing for his safety, Honey said he removed the signboards from his gym. About 30 men came to my gym to threaten me. Because of the fear, I have stopped opening the gym. He added that he has deactivated his social media accounts and changed his phone number. I closed my Instagram and Facebook accounts. I also stopped using my WhatsApp number. Because of the threats, I bought a new SIM card. Police provide security to the family Honey said he is originally from Chhajjupur village in the Partapur police station area of Meerut. His father, Indrapal Singh, is a farmer. Honey completed a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) at IMR College, Ghaziabad, before opening his own gym. His family includes his wife, Akanksha Chaudhary, and their three-year-old son. According to Honey, the abuse has extended to his family as well. Since 20 July, my family has also been receiving abusive messages. He said the police have now provided protection. Two police officers have been deployed for our security. The police have told me that if a crowd gathers at the gym or anyone comes to threaten us, I should inform them immediately so action can be taken. Honey has submitted a complaint at Nandgram police station in Ghaziabad, seeking the registration of an FIR. In the complaint, he stated that he has been receiving death threats because of mistaken identity. He also alleged that his wife and young son have received threats of murder and kidnapping. He claimed to have received more than 10,000 messages and phone calls. Neighbours say the man in the video is not Honey Dagar Dainik Bhaskar also spoke to Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) leader Sanjeev Chaudhary and several shopkeepers in Honey's neighbourhood. They said the Honey Dagar identified on social media is not the same person who appears in the viral video. According to them, Honey owns and operates a gym in the area and commutes daily from Chhajjupur village in Meerut, returning home each night. A nearby shopkeeper, speaking on condition of anonymity, said groups of young men have been repeatedly visiting the area looking for Honey. He said the gym remains closed because of fears that someone could vandalise the premises or physically attack him.

stories.title: Meet the 13-year-old who designed affordable ‘allergy spoons'
stories.summary: Abigail Stein developed an ingenious spoon designed to identify food allergens, providing a safety net for students with severe allergies during school meals. This innovative Allergy Spoon changes color upon detecting specific allergens, enhancing awareness and safety. Abigail was celebrated as a leading finalist in a prestigious young scientist challenge, with aspirations that her practical solution will address a significant concern for many families.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi's 'advice' to PM Modi, and 3 guarantees to students over police action on protesters
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of denying him Lok Sabha speech rights. He refused to apologize for blaming Amit Shah for police brutality. Gandhi demanded the Home Minister's dismissal and an independent probe. He alleged police used pellet guns and nail-fitted lathis on students. Gandhi promised justice and accountability for the injured students.

stories.title: Australia built a $187,000 electric fence across Wild Horse Plain, but the real reason lies beneath one of its rarest alpine wetlands
stories.summary: A new electrified fence protects rare alpine wetlands in Kosciuszko National Park. This enclosure safeguards endangered sphagnum bogs and associated fens from wild horse impacts. Horse activity damages these vital peatland ecosystems and their stored carbon. The $187,000 project was funded by biodiversity offsets from Snowy 2.0. This targeted measure protects a small but environmentally important area within the park.

stories.title: A trekking pole pierced a nurse through the torso; he then hiked 10 miles for...
stories.summary: In an incredible display of resilience, a nurse endured a life-threatening injury on Granite Peak in Montana. With a pole piercing his side, he bravely trekked over ten miles down the treacherous terrain. Relying on his medical expertise, he evaluated his injuries and chose to make the strenuous descent, aided by his friends. Now on the mend, he dreams of conquering the mountain again next year.

stories.title: Half of England declared in drought as July records near-zero rainfall
Evening News Wrap: Air India crash probe finds no fuel switch fault; RS clears Vande Mataram Bill & more
Florida sixth grader Naboshree Santra developed biodegradable soilshade balls designed to...
stories.summary: An 11-year-old Florida student has reached the finals of a national science competition. Her innovative soilshade balls help farmers conserve water during dry weather conditions. This eco-friendly invention slows evaporation and keeps soil moist for extended periods. She will compete for a $25,000 prize and mentorship from 3M scientists. The competition celebrates young innovators using STEM to solve real-world problems.

Bihar transgender welfare board approves proposal to build temple dedicated to PM Modi
stories.summary: The Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board approved constructing a temple for Prime Minister Narendra Modi. A board member stated the prime minister provided the community with respect and rights. This proposal was moved during the board's inaugural meeting after the new act's implementation. The board functions under the Bihar government's Social Welfare Department for community empowerment. This decision reflects the transgender community's institutional representation in the state secretariat.

In 2018, an undocumented migrant scaled a Paris apartment building to save a four-year-old boy hanging from a fourth-floor balcony, earning the nickname 'Spider-Man of Paris'
stories.summary: Mamadou Gassama, an African migrant, rescued a child hanging from a Paris balcony. His brave actions led to him being honoured by the French president. Gassama received French citizenship and an internship with firefighters. This incident brought Gassama international recognition and a new life.

stories.title: Barracuda bites Texas girl, 13, but cannot shake her ocean dream
stories.summary: A Texas teenager is recovering after a rare barracuda attack during a family vacation. Claire Macdonel experienced the frightening incident in shallow waters while wearing a shiny bracelet. She is now home and preparing for surgery to repair her hand injury. Despite the painful ordeal, Claire still dreams of becoming a marine biologist. Her family shares the story to raise awareness and encourage water safety precautions.

stories.title: For more than 300 years, the Bermuda petrel was believed extinct. A remarkable discovery in 1951 gave the 'lost bird' a second chance
stories.summary: The Bermuda petrel, once thought extinct, was rediscovered in 1951. A young naturalist, David Wingate, led a long recovery effort for the cahow. Conservationists protected nests and restored Nonsuch Island for the seabirds. The cahow population has grown, though challenges remain from storms. This story highlights species recovery and the importance of habitat restoration.

stories.title: 'Donate your $1 trillion fortune by 2036': Nobel economist challenges Elon Musk after his 'money won't matter' prediction
stories.summary: Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu challenged Elon Musk to donate his fortune by 2036. Musk responded positively, suggesting he may consider a major philanthropic move. His past giving has focused on science, education, and technology initiatives. Donating such a vast sum presents practical challenges regarding asset transfer and oversight. This potential commitment marks a notable shift in his philanthropic approach.

stories.title: E20 petrol and vehicle mileage: What Nitin Gadkari said amid growing concerns
'Citizens have every right to demand answers': CJP responds to Delhi Police notice to X over 'derogatory content'
MEA goes the meme way to reinforce India’s position on J&K, Ladakh

'Only tear gas used, no shots fired': Centre counters Rahul's charge, demands apology
Researchers studied 1,561 forest plots across 10 tropical countries; non-native trees formed 28% of stems in young moist forests, but declined as the canopy returned
stories.summary: Young tropical forests show many non-native trees while canopies remain open. As forests mature and canopies close, these non-native species tend to decrease. This pattern was observed across ten tropical countries in a recent study. Early forest regeneration is vulnerable to invasive species, which can establish easily. Understanding these dynamics aids effective forest restoration planning and native ecosystem recovery.

stories.title: Inside Coober Pedy: The Australian desert town where thousands escaped 50°C heat by building an entire underground world beneath the Earth
stories.summary: Coober Pedy, Australia, features a unique town built underground by opal miners. Residents live below the surface to escape the harsh desert climate and high cooling costs. This subterranean living provides stable temperatures year-round, offering practical comfort and savings. Underground homes and businesses are common, transforming excavated mining areas into functional spaces. The town's success depends on specific geological conditions and dry weather for construction.

stories.title: Indian national Amritpal Singh added to FBI’s 'Most Wanted' list in drug trafficking case
E20 petrol row: Arvind Kejriwal alleges 'strong-arm tactics’; BJP hits back
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal raised concerns over the Centre's alleged pressure on automakers regarding the compatibility of vehicles with E20 petrol. He suggested that vehicles manufactured before 2023 might suffer from damage and performance issues. However, the BJP dismissed these allegations, referencing statements from leading industry figures who confirmed E20 petrol’s safety following comprehensive testing and validation, thus reinforcing the automotive sector's support for the E20 initiative.

In 2006, a rescued dog saved Houssein Hamze from a bomb; in 2026, he refused to flee Lebanon and stayed to care for hundreds of animals
stories.summary: Houssein Hamze turned his life around after his dog saved him from a devastating bomb attack, and he founded a shelter for abandoned animals in his village. Ignoring the threat of drone strikes, he continually provided food and water for displaced animals. His remarkable dedication attracted international recognition and donations, allowing him to persevere in his mission of promoting kindness towards animals.

stories.title: Bermuda snails were thought to be extinct from the island, a decade later breeders have released over 100,000 of them back
stories.summary: Once thought to be lost forever, the incredible Bermuda snail has been successfully revived. A decade ago, a small group was rediscovered and subsequently bred at Chester Zoo. Thousands were released back into safeguarded woodland areas in Bermuda, where six colonies have thrived. This success not only supports ecosystem recovery but also allows conservationists to shift their attention to breeding another rare native snail species.

stories.title: Russia's Telegram crackdown: Pavel Durov charged with aiding terrorism, puts him on international wanted list

Rahul also shared a student's definition of a true student. He alleged rampant privatization and RSS capture of the education system. The opposition leader targeted home minister Amit Shah over alleged police actions.

stories.title: Oregon engineer spent $100,000 on a retired Boeing 727 and turned it into a home
Ancient footprints found in Kenya reveal how early human relatives may have travelled and lived together 1.43 million years ago
stories.summary: Ancient footprints found in Kenya offer rare glimpses into early human relatives. These impressions date back approximately 1.43 million years to a lakeshore environment. The tracks suggest several large-bodied individuals moved together across muddy ground. This discovery provides new evidence about hominin body size and social organization. The findings reshape current ideas about Homo erectus and Paranthropus boisei.

stories.title: Coal block scam case in Supreme Court: Ex-PM Manmohan Singh gets clean chit two years after his death
El Salvador archaeologists lifted a burial sealed beneath 2,800-year-old volcanic ash; the person lay face down with a sea turtle-shaped vessel near one hand
stories.summary: Archaeologists discovered a 2,800-year-old burial in El Salvador clutching a sea turtle vessel. This Mesoamerican burial may belong to a pre-Maya civilization which practiced human sacrifice. The skeleton was found under volcanic ash from an eruption dating to 850-830 BC. Cassava remnants found in the pit symbolize continuation and spiritual resonance. Further chemical analysis will reveal more about the individual's life and diet.

stories.title: One of America's most active volcanoes: How Pagan Island became home to just two residents
Spain's 'cannibal cave': New fossils reveal adults were also eaten by Homo antecessor
China lost more than 50% of its mangrove forests by the 2000s, now it has restored 22,500 hectares of the trees
stories.summary: China has made remarkable strides in restoring its mangrove ecosystems, committing to large-scale projects that have expanded coverage significantly. By planting and revitalizing thousands of hectares, not only has biodiversity surged, but the quality of these crucial habitats has also seen improvement. Robust legal measures now safeguard more than ninety percent of mangrove areas, complemented by the establishment of an international center focused on mangrove conservation in Shenzhen.

stories.title: A 66-million-year-old dinosaur highway in Bolivia reveals more than 16,000 fossil footprints from the final days of the dinosaurs
Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina plans Bangladesh return: 'I may be killed, I may be sent to prison'
stories.summary: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh by December. She is prepared to face arrest, imprisonment, or even execution upon her arrival. Hasina fled the country in August 2024 after widespread protests ended her rule. Her party faces repression and legal proceedings following the change in government.

stories.title: Delhi Police serves notice to X over 'derogatory' posts targeting constitutional heads
stories.summary: Delhi Police has requested X to remove content deemed defamatory towards constitutional authorities. The platform must also provide user details and preserve all related data. This action follows similar directives for posts targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The police social media monitoring team continuously scans for objectionable online material. These developments occur amid heightened political tensions following recent student protests.

stories.title: In 2001, scientists released beetles to fight an invasive tree. Years later, an endangered bird had lost 94% of its habitat along one western river
Antarctica averages minus 55°C at Vostok Station, yet a lake remains liquid beneath four kilometres of ice
stories.summary: Lake Vostok, a massive body of water, lies four kilometers beneath Antarctic ice. This subglacial lake remains liquid due to insulating ice and geothermal heat. Its existence challenges our understanding of life's extreme limits and nature's magic. The lake has been isolated from the atmosphere for millions of years. Scientists continue to study this unique environment and its potential inhabitants.

stories.title: A 13-year-old boy was airlifted after a rabid beaver attacked him at a Maryland state park, forcing officials to close the swimming beach
NEET-UG leak probe: CBI gets 3 more days to file annexures in chargesheet, hearing on August 3
stories.summary: A special court will consider the CBI's chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case. The agency filed charges against thirteen accused, including NTA experts and coaching associates. Investigations uncovered the entire conspiracy from paper leak sources to beneficiary candidates. The CBI also traced the money trail and froze several linked bank accounts.

Trump bans new Chinese robots and power inverters over security fears
stories.summary: Explaining the decision, the FCC said the targeted products could expose the country to supply chain risks and cyber threats. "These devices could create supply chain vulnerabilities that could disrupt US economic and national security and could create a cybersecurity risk that threatened American critical infrastructure," the agency said. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr added, "The FCC will continue to do our part to secure America’s critical supply chains."

stories.title: In 1934, this Pennsylvania mountain went from a hawk killing ground to the world's first raptor sanctuary and changed bird conservation forever
Middle East war escalates: Multiple dead in US-Saudi strikes in Iraq; Iran targets Hormuz ships - top developments
stories.summary: United States and Saudi Arabia launched joint strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq. Iran claimed to have intercepted oil tankers and fired missiles at US installations. Eight Iraqi PMF members were killed in the joint US-Saudi attacks. Oil prices climbed amid concerns over energy supply disruptions. Diplomatic efforts continue as tensions between nations rise.

stories.title: Our FTAs fair & equitable, protect farmers, MSMEs, labour sector: Govt to NDA MPs
stories.summary: Government ministers defended trade pacts, contrasting them with past agreements. These new deals involve larger economies and aim for balanced growth. Fisheries sector exports have doubled, showing significant economic expansion. New markets are emerging, offsetting reduced exports to the United States. The government secured substantial committed investments from European and New Zealand trade partners.

stories.title: Shark attack rescuer Charlie Verco breaks world paddleboarding record
stories.summary: Australian paddleboarder Charlie Verco won his fourth Molokai to Oahu world championship in Hawaii in record time, just weeks after rescuing a woman during a great white shark attack off Sydney's Coogee Beach. The trained surf lifesaver said a relaxed approach helped him break the previous course record by three minutes.

stories.title: 'Deeply concerning': In UNSC, India strongly condemns attacks on commercial ships near Hormuz
stories.summary: Speaking at an open debate of the United Nations security council on the situation in the Middle East, India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, said the recent escalation after a brief lull in fighting was deeply worrying. He urged all sides to return to dialogue and diplomacy to prevent the conflict from worsening.

stories.title: Oman proposes Gulf-backed voluntary fees to use Hormuz
stories.summary: Oman has presented Iran with a plan backed by Gulf states for managing the Strait of Hormuz. This proposal includes collecting voluntary fees for ships utilizing the vital waterway. Iran has yet to respond to the Omani proposals for trade disruption resolution. The plan aims to avoid sole Iranian control and make fees voluntary. Gulf Cooperation Council ministers met to discuss waterway safety and cooperation.

stories.title: Italy's fertility rate falls to 80-year low: Report
stories.summary: Italy's birth rate fell nearly four percent last year, reaching a historic low. The fertility rate dropped to 1.14 children per woman, a significant decline. Economic pressures and a lack of support for working mothers contributed to this trend. This rate is far below the 2.1 needed for a stable population. Motherhood desires clash with job insecurity and high living costs.

stories.title: New chapter in reading: AI companion tools let readers chat with books
stories.summary: New artificial intelligence tools now let readers ask questions directly to books. These innovative platforms offer e-books and audiobooks alongside AI chatbots for immediate answers. Companies like Sinai.ai and Amazon's Audible are developing these interactive reading experiences. However, copyright and author compensation remain significant unresolved issues for these tools. Some platforms are exploring ways to pay authors and publishers for their content.

stories.title: US envoy Gor to visit Bangladesh as Dhaka deepens ties with Beijing
stories.summary: US special envoy Sergio Gor will visit Bangladesh on July 30. He will meet Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and the foreign minister. This visit follows Prime Minister Rahman's recent tour of China. The US seeks understanding of Bangladesh's foreign policy priorities. Washington remains concerned over China's economic corridor proposal.

stories.title: NEET has flaw in design, it is not necessary: DMK's Dayanidhi Maran
stories.summary: DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran demanded NEET be scrapped in Lok Sabha. He argued the proposed paper leak law amendment misses the core issue. Maran highlighted DMK and Tamil Nadu's long-standing opposition to the medical entrance exam. He also raised concerns about Meta smart glasses recording protesting students. Maran mentioned issues with WhatsApp broadcast limits for MPs and a removed Facebook post.

stories.title: Union minister, BJP MP got NHB subsidies, mantri refunded it: Government
stories.summary: Union minister Bhagirath Choudhary and MP Lumba Ram received central scheme aid. Choudhary has since refunded the subsidy to the National Horticulture Board. The government informed Parliament about these financial assistance instances. Existing scheme guidelines lack specific conflict of interest provisions. All eligible applicants are treated equally under the transparent NHB mechanism.

stories.title: India slams POK elections, Pakistan's claims over Indus Valley legacy
stories.summary: India has condemned Pakistan's legislative assembly elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. The Ministry of External Affairs called the polls a cosmetic exercise to hide illegal occupation. India reiterated its firm stance that the entire Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India. The spokesperson highlighted Pakistan's promotion of terrorism and religious fundamentalism. This stance questions Pakistan's claims to any pluralistic cultural legacy.

stories.title: Dealers can't keep over 400 tonne stock of sugar: Government
stories.summary: The government has capped sugar stock at 400 tonnes per dealer. Dealers must liquidate excess stock by August 1 and sell within thirty days. This measure aims to prevent hoarding and stabilize sugar prices. The essential commodities act was invoked to impose these restrictions. Sugar exports have also been banned amid monsoon deficit forecasts.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha adjourned as opposition seeks Shah statement on police action
stories.summary: Rajya Sabha adjourned for the day amid opposition protests demanding a statement. MPs demanded Union Home Minister Amit Shah explain police action against demonstrators. The House was first adjourned within minutes of assembling at 11 am. Later, legislative business was attempted while opposition MPs continued their sloganeering. The Deputy Chairperson adjourned the House till Wednesday as protests persisted.

stories.title: PM Modi's message to key ministries: Be youthful, dynamic and adaptable
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged government ministries to remain youthful and forward-looking. He stressed the need for young entrepreneurs' active participation in key sectors. Officials were asked to devise industry-aligned courses for emerging sector skills. Proactive communication is vital to counter misinformation on major national initiatives. Citizens must remain at the center of all policy decisions and governance reforms.

stories.title: Centre notifies 7th draft for ecological zones in Western Ghats
stories.summary: The Centre has released its seventh draft notification for ecologically sensitive areas. This proposal aims to protect 56,825 sq km across six Indian states. States have raised objections, primarily Kerala, citing livelihood concerns. The draft allows for phased implementation, potentially speeding up the process. This initiative follows previous attempts since 2011 to conserve the fragile region.

stories.title: 1 officer, 1 car: Government tightens rules for use of official vehicle for staff
stories.summary: Government has tightened rules for official vehicle usage by employees. Officers will now receive only one official car, even with additional charges. They are also barred from using PSU vehicles except during official tours. This aims to optimize vehicle utilization and prevent misuse of government assets. Strict compliance is sought from all ministries and departments.

stories.title: Centre may table bill to make deepfakes, digital arrest separate offences
stories.summary: The government plans to introduce a bill addressing digital arrests and AI deepfakes. Existing laws do not define these emerging digital crimes effectively. The Supreme Court urged the government to create specific offenses for these issues. This new legislation will categorize digital arrest and deepfakes as distinct offenses. Consequential punishments and asset freezing measures will be included in the proposed law.

stories.title: MBBS admissions: NMC puts focus on ability, not disability
stories.summary: New National Medical Commission guidelines assess functional abilities for disabled students seeking MBBS admission. Medical boards will now evaluate candidates' capabilities rather than just disability percentages. Enabling units will provide support and a barrier-free learning environment for these students. Reasonable accommodations and assistive devices will be considered before making admission decisions. Patient safety remains a key consideration while promoting inclusive medical education for all.

stories.title: UK company in spotlight as Nishikant Dubey vows 'disclosure' in Parliament
stories.summary: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey plans to disclose information about a UK-registered company. He will reveal which Indian politician is a director in Backops Limited. Dubey stated that Brian Lovegrove and Ulrik McKnight are linked to this company. These individuals are associated with numerous companies and TV channels registered at one address. The MP will present these findings inside Parliament soon.

stories.title: NEET row: CBI chargesheets 13 in paper leak
stories.summary: The CBI has filed a chargesheet against thirteen individuals in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case. These accused include three NTA subject experts and several middlemen involved in question distribution. The agency's investigation confirmed the circulation of leaked questions prior to the examination date. Digital forensics and expert opinions corroborated the accused's involvement in the paper leak. Further investigation is ongoing, with a supplementary chargesheet anticipated soon.

stories.title: Delulu opposition thinks youth are with it, Rahul suffering from FOMO: NDA
stories.summary: BJP and allies defended the government's handling of student protests and paper leaks. They asserted that the youth trust Prime Minister Modi's commitment to reforms. Opposition leaders were criticized for using students for political gains and spreading cynicism. The government highlighted its efforts to reform the education system and address concerns. Measures were taken to clean the examination system after incidents occurred.

stories.title: 1st direct freight train opens new India-Nepal chapter
stories.summary: India and Nepal have initiated a new era of rail connectivity. The first direct commercial container freight train arrived in Nepal last week. This new service is expected to significantly reduce transit times and logistics costs. The achievement builds upon the broad-gauge rail link inaugurated in June 2023. Direct freight movement to Biratnagar has now become operational, boosting bilateral trade.

stories.title: What happened to Yonna? Twitch streamer reacts after e-bike accident on livestream
stories.summary: Twitch streamer and TikTok creator Yonna crashed an e-bike during a recent IRL livestream after losing control and hitting a gate. She first answered “No” when friends asked if she was okay but later laughed and joked about the incident. No serious injury has been confirmed. Yonna recently returned to Kai Cenat’s Streamer University 2026 as Drama Club director.

stories.title: Don't touch water bodies under garb of beautification, Supreme Court tells Bihar government
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered the Bihar government to stop filling historic ponds in Darbhanga. This action follows allegations that the state is filling water bodies for public amenities. The court warned the state not to touch the ponds without its explicit approval. The project aimed to beautify and rejuvenate Gangasagar, Digghi, and Harahi Lake. The Supreme Court directed the government to ensure the ponds' areas remain intact.

stories.title: Congress, BJP spar over Pralhad Joshi's pick as education minister
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticized Pralhad Joshi's appointment as education minister. Gandhi accused Joshi of defending rapists in a past TV interview. BJP spokesperson Anil Baluni refuted these claims, stating Joshi commented on remission processes. Baluni accused Gandhi of distorting facts for personal attacks. The exchange highlights a political dispute over the minister's past statements.

stories.title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised, reveals CRPF review
stories.summary: CRPF analysis indicates police action against protesters followed standard operating procedures. Non-lethal means like pellet guns were authorized for crowd dispersal. Force gradient was followed, with lower measures failing before pump action guns. Protesters and personnel sustained injuries during the July 20 incident. The matter is now sub judice before the Supreme Court.

stories.title: India is second-largest sailor supplier in world
stories.summary: India now ranks as the world's second-largest supplier of seafaring personnel. This significant achievement is highlighted in the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026. The report indicates India's share of global sailors has doubled over the past five years. Indian officers comprise thirteen point four percent of the world's officer workforce. This growth positions India strongly within the global maritime industry.

stories.title: Ahmedabad tragedy: Supreme Court accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public
stories.summary: The Supreme Court accepted a father's request concerning the air crash inquiry report. The government will submit the final report in a sealed cover to the court. An NGO questioned the inquiry's impartiality and adherence to standard procedures. The Air Accident Investigation Bureau anticipates completing its investigation within six weeks. The final report is expected to be ready for distribution around October 2026.

stories.title: After stalemate, government, opposition spar over paper leak law in Lok Sabha
stories.summary: Parliament debated a bill to strengthen penalties for exam paper leaks. Opposition members supported student protests and criticized police actions during demonstrations. Government speakers highlighted past paper leaks and PM Modi's reform efforts. They emphasized the bill's aim to protect student welfare and ensure fair examinations. The proposed law seeks to deter organized gangs and individuals involved in leaks.

stories.title: Kai Cenat defends Tyla from alleged catcaller during Disney World livestream, fans applaud response
