Experts weigh in on what's the path forward for Mamata Banerjee and TMC.

stories.summary: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey asked protesting students to return to their studies for future success. He emphasized education over agitation for achieving career aspirations in medicine and civil services. Dubey advocated for a stringent law against examination paper leaks in Parliament. He suggested that this new law could even include the death penalty for offenders. The government is committed to ensuring the harshest punishment for those arrested.

stories.summary: The government is engaging opposition leaders to resolve the Parliament deadlock over the NEET paper leak. Discussions aim to end disruptions which have stalled proceedings since the Monsoon session began. The Centre is ready for debate without preconditions, including minister's resignation. Australian agronomist Tony Rinaudo's FMNR revives Niger's dry landscapes with 200 million trees
stories.summary: An Australian agronomist's simple idea transformed Niger's dry landscapes into a success story. Tony Rinaudo helped farmers regenerate over 200 million trees by reviving existing root systems. This low-cost approach restored millions of hectares of degraded farmland and improved food security. Indigenous trees regenerated, providing shade, preventing soil erosion, and enriching the soil. The technique is now a global model for restoring degraded land worldwide.

stories.title: Scientists are dropping thousands of fish from airplanes into remote mountain lakes; here's why the unusual conservation strategy has worked for decades
stories.summary: Utah's Division of Wildlife Resources stocks remote mountain lakes by dropping fish from airplanes. This method efficiently reaches inaccessible waters, maintaining fish populations for anglers. Tiny trout and other species are released, with survival rates exceeding ninety-five percent. Biologists carefully select species, often using sterile fish to control numbers and protect native ecosystems. This practice balances recreation with conservation in challenging mountainous terrain.

She questioned the government's handling of demonstrations and alleged police brutality against students. The Prime Minister announced fast-track courts for paper leak cases amid ongoing parliamentary protests. Opposition MPs demanded the Education Minister's resignation while BJP leaders called for debate. Tensions briefly escalated between rival party members outside Parliament.

stories.title: India's dying rivers: How our cities are choking their lifelines
stories.summary: India's expanding cities are encroaching upon rivers, reducing their width and flow. Many rivers now carry more sewage than freshwater, impacting ecosystems and communities. Efforts to clean these waterways face challenges from ongoing pollution and development pressures. The Brahmaputra river faces erosion, while the Ganga struggles with industrial and ritual waste. Protecting river floodplains and managing sewage are crucial for their survival.

stories.title: 'Considerable time:' Private airport operators flag BCAS clearance delays with Govt
stories.summary: Private airport operators are flagging significant delays in project implementation. Security vetting approvals from BCAS are taking an unacceptably long time. These delays impact operational efficiencies and passenger convenience at major airports. The Association of Private Airport Operators has requested faster processing timelines. They seek to ensure timely capacity enhancements and improved passenger facilitation.

stories.title: Thousands of idle ships trapped near the Strait of Hormuz could become floating nurseries for invasive marine species
stories.summary: Ships lingering in the Persian Gulf could unintentionally facilitate the spread of harmful marine invaders worldwide. Extended anchorage allows marine organisms to thrive on the hulls, creating significant biofouling concerns that threaten global maritime commerce. These invasive species can inflict extensive ecological and economic harm on coastal areas. It is imperative for nations to join forces to address biofouling issues and prevent future outbreaks of invasion.

stories.summary: Soviet engineer Petr Borisov proposed damming the Bering Strait to warm Siberia. This bold plan aimed to transform frozen lands into productive agricultural areas. Modern researchers now study closing the strait to stabilize ocean circulation. Their simulations explore impacts on the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation system. Scientists remain cautious about such large-scale environmental interventions.

stories.title: Tony Parker's mansion slashes price: Texas estate drops to $11 million; despite luxury features, still seeking buyer
stories.summary: Tony Parker's Texas mansion has seen another significant price reduction. The sprawling estate is now listed for eleven million dollars after several adjustments. This luxurious property features an enormous private water park and extensive sports facilities. Despite extensive publicity and a past peak price of twenty million dollars, it remains unsold. The highly customized luxury estate continues its search for a new owner.

stories.title: Orcas filmed tearing apart giant Sunfish with new hunting technique
stories.summary: Researchers have documented a previously unknown hunting behaviour in orcas in the Gulf of California. The animals were filmed working together to hold and ram giant sharp-tail sunfish until the carcass broke into thousands of pieces. Scientists believe the behaviour may help younger orcas feed more easily or could simply be play.

stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has started a suo motu public interest litigation to monitor stray dog management. Notices were issued to the Delhi government and Municipal Corporation of Delhi. Authorities must submit a status report detailing steps taken by July thirty-first. The court expressed concern over the increasing stray dog population in the city. This action follows Supreme Court directions for all High Courts to oversee compliance.

stories.title: Climate change is driving beavers into Canada's Arctic, where they are reshaping the landscape
stories.summary: A new study has traced the northward expansion of North American beavers into Canada's Arctic by analysing shrub growth scars and satellite images. Researchers found evidence of colonisation beginning in 2008 and say the method can help track wildlife spread, landscape changes and the effects of climate change in remote Arctic regions.

The world's largest waterfall isn't on land. It is hidden beneath the ocean, where billions of litres of water plunge every second
stories.summary: An immense underwater waterfall exists between Greenland and Iceland. Cold, dense seawater sinks beneath warmer Atlantic waters creating this cascade. This hidden giant plays a crucial role in ocean currents and global climate. Researchers use specialized instruments to monitor this vast, dynamic underwater system. Its flow influences heat and salt distribution across the Atlantic Ocean basin.

stories.title: Scientists claim Moon is drifting away from Earth at 3.8 centimetres a year. What will happen to the planet as it goes further?
stories.summary: The Moon is gradually distancing itself from Earth, which has significant implications for our planet. Over millions of years, this migration will result in extended daylight hours and the end of total solar eclipses. Furthermore, the weakened tides will disrupt coastal ecosystems and marine life. As the Moon ascends to a higher orbit, Earth's rotation continues to decelerate, marking a slow but profound transformation in our natural environment.

stories.summary: An old proverb suggests that a true traveler aims not for a destination, but for the adventure along the way. This philosophy highlights the value of immersing oneself in experiences, rather than merely seeking end goals. By concentrating on our journey, we become more adept at navigating surprises and changing landscapes. Modern psychology backs this notion, revealing that states of flow arise from genuine involvement in our pursuits.

This profound statement confronts economic structures that disregard the sanctity of human life. In today’s world, challenges such as access to healthcare and adequate housing reveal entrenched tensions. Too often, profit motives overshadow the critical importance of safety and well-being, urging institutions to prioritize human survival above financial considerations.

stories.title: Scientists found a 2,865-pound predator from before dinosaurs ruled Earth
stories.summary: In an exciting collaboration, over 2,000 public volunteers are meticulously cleaning a colossal 1,300-kilogram fossilized skeleton of a Mastodonsaurus, an ancient amphibian that roamed the Earth 240 million years ago. Armed with specialized tools and ultraviolet light, these dedicated individuals are uncovering the mysteries of our planet's history. The spectacular skeleton is expected to be on display by October or November, showcasing humanity's connection to a distant past.

stories.title: Terrorist kill J&K cop in Anantnag market, first strike since Pahalgam attack

A tapeworm infects ants and makes them live several times longer by turning their bodies into...

This fascinating research sheds light on the complexities of genetic control related to aging processes.

The nonnative leaves serve as an excellent nourishment source for mosquito larvae, promoting faster growth and larger size, which ultimately enhances their ability to transmit diseases. This finding underscores the significance of plant quality over quantity in managing mosquito outbreaks.

stories.title: Hidden in Egypt's Dakhla Oasis, 7,000-year-old rock carvings are slowly disappearing
stories.summary: Ancient rock art in Egypt's Dakhla Oasis is facing significant decline. Natural erosion and shifting weather patterns are gradually wearing away these ancient markings. Modern graffiti and human activity also add new scars to the desert art. Archaeologists are documenting the fragile rock art to preserve its details. Efforts aim to record this history before it is permanently erased.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Elon Musk: "Being an entrepreneur is like eating glass and staring into…" - brutally honest lesson on entrepreneurship, resilience and the hidden reality behind building a business
